# THREATS: threat model

Each row: who attacks, how, what stops it, and the test that proves it (or a tracked TODO with
the milestone that adds the test). Reviewer findings from each loop are added here.
IDs are stable; never reuse one.

## Attackers
- **Cheating miner**: wants rewards without doing the work, or wants a false number finalized.
- **Lazy validator**: wants validator pay without rerunning anything.
- **Griefing challenger**: wants to delay finality or drain honest miners' time.
- **Data thief**: wants paid data without paying, or wants to resell licensed data.
- **Malicious recipe author**: wants a recipe that gives different answers on different hosts.
- **Label spammer / doxxer**: wants false or personal labels published.

confidence rules.

## Review findings, M0 loop 2 (second fresh reviewer, 2026-10-06)

## Loop 22 design notes (M4 validation)

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Attack | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| R-M4-2 | Lazy validator | High | Approve everything without recomputing | Committed canaries with known wrong roots; wrong verdict slashed | FIXED loop 23 (L22-F6): canaries can make a wrong root the plurality; the plurality copier and the griefer are slashed (`validate::settle_reruns_disputes_and_lazy_actors_lose`); a blind Agree on a wrong canary root is slashed (`validate::lying_source_leaves_shard_pending_and_known_miners_are_never_canaries`); on chain silent assigned validators are slashed once (`OnyxSettlement.t.sol::test_SilentAssignedValidatorIsSlashedOnce`) and wrong verdicts are slashed by the rerun case (`OnyxDisputes.t.sol::test_RerunCaseClosesTheFreeVeto`). L9 2026-10-14: confirmed; the catch rate rests on canary density (L26-F4) and an unbiasable beacon (R-M4-6, H2). |
| R-M4-3 | Copying validator | Med | Copy another validator's verdict | Signed verdict commit-reveal | FIXED loop 22: verdicts are commit-revealed and the commit hash binds seed, validator, shard, miner, verdict and salt, so a copied commit cannot be revealed by the copier and nothing is visible before reveal (`OnyxSettlementVectors.t.sol::test_VerdictCommitHashesMatchRust`, `OnyxSettlement.t.sol::test_VerdictRevealMustMatchCommit`). L9 2026-10-14: confirmed on chain. |

| R-M4-5 | Coordinator | Med | Frame a validator with a canary list chosen after the fact | Canary list committed before the round, opened at settlement, must match | FIXED loop 23 (L22-F2/F3): canaries carry roots, strictly sorted, must match reveals and be fresh; truth from recompute. `validate::lying_source_leaves_shard_pending_and_known_miners_are_never_canaries` |

| R-M4-7 | Beacon manipulator | Med | Bias the seed through the beacon block | Future block hash; Base sequencer can bias it (validation.md open question) | DEFERRED: M6 seed is keccak(tag, blockhash(beaconHeight)) (`OnyxSettlement.t.sol::test_DrawnSeedIsTagAndBlockhash`); the Base sequencer can bias blockhash, accepted for testnet (ADR-0022 item 5). L9 2026-10-14: still true. TODO H2: mainnet randomness item (drand, VRF or L1 RANDAO); blocks mainnet, not the testnet launch |

## Review findings, loop 23 (nineteenth fresh reviewer, on commit 790f978)

Reviewer verdict: root selection is sound (only a unanimous undisputed root or a deterministic rerun
decides). The coordinator can still decide who gets paid via the paths below. Fixes go to loop 27.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Proposed fix | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L26-F1 | Coordinator | Med-High | Committers become "known" only when their own round's validation starts; validating round B before round A lets an honest new miner in A be listed as a canary in B | Record committers in the ledger when reveals close (`Round::close(&mut Ledger)`) | FIXED loop 27: committers recorded at `Round::commit`; `Validation::new` and `Ledger::apply` treat anyone active in another round as known (loop 28: `apply` uses the snapshot taken at validation start, L27-F2). Test `committers_are_known_whatever_the_validation_order` (both orders). Residual: the coordinator orders calls until the chain orders them (M6) |
| L26-F2 | Coordinator, copier | Med | A planted canary plus withheld inputs voids any shard at `pending_close`; the work is re-offered and its public honest root copied next round | Never release voided work whose reveals are public (or pay the earliest matching voided reveal later); require `pending_close` well after `canary_open_close` | FIXED loop 27: voided work with reveals is burned (stays taken); `MIN_PENDING_GAP` at open. Tests `withheld_inputs_void_the_shard_at_the_deadline` (copier round refused), `validation_rules_are_fixed_at_open` |
| L26-F3 | Coordinator | Med | `RuleSet` is a type parameter chosen at the call site; a caller can name its own rule set, and settlements carry no record of it | Bind the rule set to the ledger (`Ledger<R>`); document that the guarantee is the published settlement binary, enforced by independent settlers in M6 | FIXED loop 27: `Ledger<R>`, settlements carry `TypeId` of `R`, `apply` checks it; ADR-0019 item 20 documents the binary as the remaining trust (M6). Test `settlement_under_other_rules_is_refused` |
| L26-F4 | Lazy validator | Low | Validator deterrence uses the sampling rate as the catch rate; a blind Agree is caught only on wrong reveals (canaries), which the coordinator can set to zero | Minimum canary density in the round config, or mark L25-F8 PARTIAL | ACCEPTED (testnet): deterrence is computed at `min_canary_ppm` (`round::validation_rules_are_fixed_at_open`, `OnyxSettlementRegression.t.sol::test_F3_NoCanaryDensityRefused`) but the chain does not count the opened list, so a coordinator can open an empty one; the coordinator is the operator and already holds the canary keys (ADR-0022), and wrong unanimous roots are still caught by challenges. Reopen before mainnet or when another party coordinates rounds. L9 2026-10-14: still true; density not enforced on chain |

funded-looking bond can turn a split first panel into a rerun for free. Cost to honest parties:

decides correctly. TODO (M6): charge the would-be appellant the burned fees.

| REV-L4-F1 | Fee spike, dropped transaction, restart | Medium | After its last fee bump a dropped `credit` was never re-sent and never given up (the reporter said `waiting` forever, no error); the in-flight `credit` lived only in memory, so a restart bumped a new, later nonce instead of the stuck one; self-settles queued behind the gap (payers charged late, no data) | Every post hands each unmined `credit` to the node again as signed (`Sender::rebroadcast`); `Reporter::with_state_file` keeps the `credit`s in flight (nonce, fees, signed transactions) on disk and a restart resumes them, bumping the lowest unmined one at its own nonce; past its last bump and 30 min (`with_give_up`) a `credit` is reported (`last_error`, `stuck_since`, `/v1/health` `reporter`) and new batches wait; the `Sender` refuses any new send while `latest` has been behind `pending` longer than its gap limit (60 s; `SendError::Stuck`, a settle answers 503 and sends nothing) | FIXED: `reporter::tests::a_credit_stuck_past_its_last_bump_is_resent_and_reported`, `reporter::tests::a_credit_in_flight_survives_a_restart_and_is_bumped_not_resent`, `reporter::tests::no_new_credit_is_sent_behind_a_stuck_transaction`, `self_settle::tests::a_settle_behind_a_stuck_transaction_sends_nothing`, `tests::health_shows_a_stuck_reporter`; tests/reporter_rpc.rs |
| REV-L4-F2 | Bad clock | Low | A retry wait is an absolute unix time: one written while the clock ran ahead stranded its receipt (never due, never dropped) | Waits are pulled back to at most `now + max_wait` on open and on every peek | FIXED: `receipts::tests::a_wait_written_while_the_clock_ran_ahead_is_pulled_back` |
| REV-L4-F3 | Busy server | Low | One `credit` in flight until final: at most 64 receipts per finality interval; a busier server filled the log and dropped receipts | Up to 4 `credit`s in flight (`with_max_in_flight`); a batch mined but not final no longer holds up the next; no receipt is in two batches at once | FIXED: `reporter::tests::a_batch_waiting_to_be_final_does_not_hold_up_the_next` |
| REV-L4-F4 | Someone who can write the state directory | Low | The journal checksum has no key: an edited line with a recomputed sum loads (REV-L3-F6 overstated it) | Docs now say the sum detects damage, not deliberate edits; the state directory is the operator's alone (whoever can write it can also replace the binary or the key) | Documented (out of scope): `journal::tests::an_edited_line_fails_its_checksum` shows both cases |
| REV-L4-F5 | - | Low | Docs said unaccounted receipts were "never deleted" and the payment retries took "about 2 hours"; they were dropped after 8 posts, about 63.5 minutes | Unaccounted receipts get their own `Retry::Unaccounted` with the long wait (15 min doubling to 6 h, about 20 h in all) before they are dropped and counted; the 63.5-minute figure for why 2 is in the docs | FIXED: `reporter::tests::unaccounted_receipts_go_back_and_an_address_without_code_is_refused`; receipts.rs and reporter.rs docs |
| REV-L4-F6 | Misconfiguration | Low | A self-settle's state write errors counted only its pending settles, so a write error of its own receipt log (when the server kept another log) never stopped new paid requests | `SelfSettle::state_write_errors` adds its receipt log's errors | FIXED: `self_settle::tests::a_receipt_log_write_error_counts_for_the_facilitator` |

## Proof ladder level 2: re-observed feeds (loop 57, ADR-0027)
| ID | Actor | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L2-F1 | Lazy observer | Medium | Copies another observer's answer instead of fetching (freeloading) | Commit-reveal with the observer address and the round id inside the commit; reveals only after commits close; a mismatched or late reveal counts as unrevealed (`outlier_slash`) | TESTED: `observe::tests::copier_cannot_reveal_a_copied_commit_or_change_its_answer_late` |
| L2-F2 | Colluding observers / coordinator | High | A bribed or colluding strict majority settles a false value; until now the coordinator listed the observers itself, so it could pick a colluding set | Observers drawn from a bonded pool (ADR-0027 amendment 6, R-OBS-2a), the draw announced ON CHAIN (ADR-0030 amendment L2RND-R1): `OnyxRegistry.announceDraw` stores the draw commitment `drawCommit(pool hash, spec id, config hash)` and a future beacon height once per fact and attempt (sequential, immutable, at most 64), so every draw input (pool, window, `min_bond`) is fixed before the beacon (L2RND-R3); `fixBeacon` stores `blockhash(beaconHeight)`; `recordObservation` needs a fixed draw and the committed pool, spec and config; `drawMatches` is true only for the fact's latest attempt, announced before its height, with this commitment and the fixed beacon. Off chain the store reads the height and the beacon from a chain reader, never from the caller; the runners (`observe::draw_and_open`) announce on chain, save the book before the beacon height, fix the beacon and open. The draw and the round id v2 bind it into the on-chain result hash; clients recompute the draw (`onchain_observation_check`, web `level2_draw_check`) and ask `drawMatches` with their own node (Rust client, demo-local); the web verifier checks the recorded announcement of the local rehearsals for consistency. One bond backs one round at a time; quorum over all drawn observers; money markets default to levels 1 and 3. Residuals: (a) a colluding strict majority of the POOL (or of a draw) still settles a false value (pool 9, draw 5: 3 colluders win one draw 11.9%, the best of 3 public draws 31.6%; 4 colluders 35.7% / 73.4%; L2RND-R3-F4); (b) the beacon is an L2 block hash the Base sequencer can bias (ADR-0022 item 5); (c) pool membership is the coordinator's attested snapshot (not read from an on-chain bond book); (d) a coordinator can abandon a seen draw and announce the next one: since review L2RND-R2 at most 3 draws per (metric, subject), across all windows, may be without a recorded value until the registry owner records `reopenDraws` (on chain, `DrawsExhausted`), so the coordinator still chooses among up to 3 public draws per subject and owner reopen; since SEC-R2-F1's publication a client sees every earlier draw of a fact (`outcome=all` + `verify_attempts_onchain`): each is a published round without a value or a draw whose beacon was never fixed, so a MISSING round for a fixed draw is detected, though the choice among public draws remains; a substituted round is refused (observer signatures, ATT-R1-F3), and a draw without a fixed beacon had no committee only while observers obey `check_commit_allowed` (ATT-R1-F4); (e) the site's rehearsals ran on a local anvil that no longer exists, so the page checks the recorded announcement's consistency, not the chain | PARTIAL (post-beacon grinding CLOSED by L2RND-R4; residuals a-e open: colluding pool majority, sequencer-biased beacon, attested pool snapshot, choice among at most 3 public draws, site checks a local-anvil rehearsal): `OnyxRegistryDrawBound.t.sol::test_PipelinedAttemptsOnlyTheLatestCounts`, `observe::tests::observers_are_the_draw_and_a_hand_picked_set_is_refused`, `draw_commit::collusion_odds_of_the_rehearsal_pool`. B2 (2026-10-17, ADR-0027 amendment 9): observers are processes of their own with their own keys; each checks that the registry's draw commits to ITS copy of the pool, spec and config before it commits (`b2_observers::b2_an_observer_commits_only_to_a_draw_of_its_own_pool`), the coordinator holds no observer key, and a colluding minority of a draw is outvoted while a colluding majority still wins (`b2_observers::b2_colluding_observers_win_only_as_a_majority_of_the_draw`); independent OPERATORS (residual a in practice) need the project owner. TODO C13 (pool from on-chain bonds, level-2 disputes; designed in ADR-0027 amendment 10 item 10), B6. L9 2026-10-14: partly true; not a launch blocker while money markets take levels 1 and 3 only (`proof::tests::money_markets_take_levels_one_and_three_only`). |
| L2-F3 | Lying minority | Medium | A minority reports an extreme number to drag the median | Lower median of all numbers, then only numbers within `tolerance` count; a strict majority within tolerance is always inside the band | TESTED: `a_tolerant_majority_is_always_inside_the_band` (2,000 random cases), `honest_majority_settles_the_median_and_slashes_the_minority_liar` |
| L2-F4 | Silent observers | Medium | Observers stay silent so a small agreeing group decides | Quorum counts assigned observers, not reveals; absent `-miss_slash`, unrevealed `-outlier_slash` | TESTED: `silent_observers_never_let_a_minority_decide`, `a_tie_or_a_plurality_is_no_result_and_judges_no_revealer` |
| L2-F5 | Feed author | Low | The example fetcher is pinned by a version tag, not by content-addressed code; two builds could extract differently | Rules written in the crate docs and the spec; tests on fixed pages | DEFERRED: fetcher still pinned by a version tag; extraction tested on recorded pages (`fiscaldata::tests::the_recorded_record_reads_to_the_cent`, `level2_real::field_host_and_fetcher_substitutions_never_open`). L9 2026-10-14: still true; TODO C14: fetchers compiled to WASM and run under the recipe host |
| L2-F6 | Source / network | Medium | Source spoofing (DNS, MITM) or a source that serves different bytes to different clients | https only; each reveal carries the raw page hash as evidence; a majority must agree | ACCEPTED: each observer fetches independently over HTTPS and one spoofed observer is outvoted and slashed (`level2_real::a_lying_observer_is_outvoted_and_slashed`); a majority spoof is the L2-F2 collusion limit; the wired level-2 sources (Treasury Fiscal Data, SEC EDGAR) serve the same public JSON to every client; money markets refuse level 2. Reopen if a personalisable source is added, observers share a network path, or money accepts level 2. L9 2026-10-14: partly true in theory, accepted; zkTLS is not on the roadmap. |
| L2-F7 | Observer clock | Low | Observer reports a fetch time it did not use, or fetches outside the window | Value is "as of `window_end`"; `observed_at` must be in the window; commits close at most 600 s after the window; tolerance covers drift | TESTED: `phases_members_and_reveal_shape_are_enforced` (reveal outside window refused) |
| L2-F8 | Flaky source | Low | Honest observers slashed for an outage | Explicit `Unavailable`: a majority of it settles `SourceUnavailable` with no slash; a value during an outage is no call; `Unavailable` during a settled value costs only `miss_slash` | TESTED: `source_unavailable_consensus_slashes_nobody_who_said_so`, `unavailable_while_a_value_settles_costs_the_small_slash` |
| L2-F9 | Feed author | High | A feed points at a source whose terms forbid redistribution | `ObservationSpec::validate` runs `DataRights::check_ingest`; every real source is wired in only after a rights review (first: `us.treasury.fiscaldata`, docs/spec/rights.md) | TESTED: `proof::tests::spec_rules`, `observe::tests::open_checks_order_bonds_and_timing` both assert a Forbidden source is refused. L9 2026-10-14: tests exist and assert the claim; CLOSED |
| L2-F10 | Fetcher | Low | A JSON float is rounded through f64 and observers disagree on the last digit | The example fetcher refuses JSON floats (`Unavailable`); decimals only from strings or integers | TESTED: `exact_and_unavailable_answers_follow_the_fetcher_contract` |
| L2R-F1 | Lying minority | Medium | Honest numbers drift apart in the window (spread between one and two tolerances); a 2-of-5 minority chose which honest edge was slashed `outlier_slash`, and was rewarded | Numbers between one and two tolerances from the center are no call; outliers start beyond twice the tolerance; numeric windows at most 300 s | FIXED loop 58: `observe::tests::a_minority_cannot_choose_which_honest_observer_is_slashed`, `proof::tests::spec_rules` |
| L2R-F2 | Lazy majority | Medium | Answering `Unavailable` cost nothing, left no evidence, and a majority of it was paid `reward`: a free Schelling point and a costless way to block a result | A `SourceUnavailable` round pays nobody (all no call) | FIXED loop 58: `an_unavailable_majority_is_paid_nothing`, `source_unavailable_consensus_slashes_nobody_who_said_so` |
| L2R-F3 | Claim submitter | Blocking | `ReObserved { spec }` named only the feed: anyone could mint a level-2 claim with any value for a feed that settled no value or never ran | `ReObserved { spec, result }` with the round's `result_hash` (binds feed, round, outcome); `ObservationSettlement::backs` checks feed, result, a settled value and the exact claimed value | CLOSED loop 61 (review 4: closed): the claim-backing family L2R-F3, L2R2-F1, L2R3-F1 is closed; tests `level2_intake::*`, `level2_review4::every_field_variant_of_a_backed_claim_is_refused`, `level2_review4::a_result_from_another_store_is_refused` |
| L2R-F4 | Minority inside the band | Low | Moves the settled value within the band and is rewarded | Bounded: the value is the median of in-band numbers and stays within the honest majority's range; documented (R-OBS-7) | TESTED: `a_minority_in_the_band_stays_inside_the_honest_range` |
| L2R-F5 | Assigned observer | Low | Refusing a hash already posted let an observer front-run another's commit from the mempool and block it | Duplicate-hash refusal dropped (the address in the commit already stops copying) | FIXED loop 58: `front_running_a_seen_commit_hash_fails`, `copier_cannot_reveal_a_copied_commit_or_change_its_answer_late` |
| L2R-F6 | Observer in a later round | Low | Commits bound the feed, not the round: round B could copy round A's public reveals | Commits and results bind a round id (feed, config, observer set) | FIXED loop 58: `a_reveal_from_another_round_of_the_same_feed_never_counts` |
| L2R-F7 | Feed author / round opener | Low | No bound on tolerance (`u128::MAX` made every answer agree); a huge reward clamped silently to `i128::MAX` | Tolerance at most 10^30; reward and slashes must fit `i128`, refused at open | FIXED loop 58: `proof::tests::spec_rules`, `open_checks_order_bonds_and_timing` |
| L2R-F8 | Market | Medium | Money policy was documented only, and level 2 also covered `OfficialSourceMatch` (no observers, no bonds) | `OfficialSourceMatch`/`CrossSourceQuorum` are level 4; money default = levels 1 and 3 (a set); the API settlement endpoint refuses other levels (409) | FIXED loop 58: `money_markets_take_levels_one_and_three_only`, `every_method_has_a_level`, API `markets_settle_only_on_accepted_proof_levels` |
| L2R-F9 | - | Medium | ADR number collision with main's ADR-0026 (self-settled x402) | Renumbered to ADR-0027 with every reference | FIXED loop 58; docs-only: docs/adr/0027-proof-ladder-level-2.md and every reference (scripts/check-docs.sh now requires each ADR in DECISIONS.md). L9 2026-10-14: no ADR number collision on main |
| L2R-F10 | - | Low | No golden encodings: "encodings unchanged" was unpinned | fixtures/claims/vectors.json pins every method (tags 0-5) and a claim | FIXED loop 58: `claim::tests::verification_method_and_claim_encodings_are_pinned` |
| L2R2-F1 | Claim submitter | Blocking | `backs` and the zero-hash check were never called on any intake path, and `ObservationSettlement` had public fields and a decoder, so a submitter could supply a settlement that backs any value | `ObservationResults`: the coordinator's own store, filled only by `settle` (each round once); `accept_claim` is the one intake (validate, then look the result up in the store, require the feed's rights, `backs`); settlement fields private, no decoder | CLOSED loop 61 (review 4): only `ObservationResults::settle` fills the store, the store is not `Clone` (compile_fail doctest), `accept_claim`/`decode_claim` are the one intake; tests `level2_intake::*`, `level2_review4::a_result_from_another_store_is_refused` |

## Series recipe `btc-entity-flow-series` (recipe-etf branch): self-noted before review
| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Fix | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SER-1 | Liveness | Medium | With label set v2 (9,850 labels) the 24-block live shard costs ~2.39 B fuel for both the range recipe and the series, about 60% of the 4 B budget: above the 50% headroom rule (R-DET-4), so a busier range could run out of fuel and settle with no data. Pre-existing for the range recipe (v1 used 1.25 B) | Round preflight (`Round::open_preflighted`) refuses any shard over half its fuel; shards sized by inputs plus outputs (~0.56 B + ~3.8 k per in/out, docs/spec/recipes.md); a round over the live range uses 12-block shards (1.39 B). The 24-block website range is a display rerun, not a round shard | FIXED for rounds (SER-R1-F2): `series_props::preflight_refuses_a_shard_over_half_its_fuel`, `golden_series::series_on_the_live_blocks` (24-block v2 refused, 12-block passes at <= 50%). OPEN: decode labels once per range set to cut the fixed cost |
| SER-2 | Cheating miner | Low | A series shard could omit an (entity, block) row: a missing row reads as zero flow (R-SERIES-1) | Rows are committed under the series root like any shard and rerun by validators; consumers can check R-SERIES-2 against the range shard of the same blocks (the website does, in the browser). The sums cannot catch flow moved between two blocks of one entity: only a rerun or the pinned series root can (SER-R1-F3) | MITIGATED: `golden_series::series_golden_v2_labels`, verifier `series_sums` tests (incl. the sum-preserving shift caught only by the root) |
| SER-R1-F1 | Liveness | Medium | A range with no labelled activity made the series recipe return zero rows, which the host turns into `BadOutput`, and honest miners could not commit a failure leaf at all (`Miner::work` refused failed runs) | The recipe returns `NO_ACTIVITY` (code 8); miners commit deterministic failure leaves, which validators and settlement already classify as the root; readers show `NO_ACTIVITY` as an all-zero series | FIXED: `a_quiet_range_is_no_activity_on_the_canonical_engine`, `series_props::a_quiet_range_is_no_activity_on_the_canonical_engine`, `validate::unanimous_no_activity_settles_cleanly`, verifier `no_activity_is_an_all_zero_series` |
| SER-R1-F2 | Liveness | Medium | Fuel headroom: label decoding plus ~3.8 k fuel per in/out lets a dense range exceed the budget (24 fixture-density blocks with doubled in/out: 3.38 B, 85%) | Round preflight refuses shards over half the budget; shard sizing documented | FIXED (see SER-1): round preflight refuses shards over half the budget: `series_props::preflight_refuses_a_shard_over_half_its_fuel`, `golden_series::series_on_the_live_blocks`. L9 2026-10-14: tests confirmed |
| SER-R1-F3 | Docs | Low | SER-2 claimed consumers can check R-SERIES-2, but sums cannot catch an intra-entity shift between blocks | SER-2 and R-SERIES-3 now say only the root or a rerun catches it | FIXED (wording): SER-2 and R-SERIES-3 say only the root or a rerun catches an intra-entity shift; `onyx-web-verify::tests::series_adds_up_and_tampering_is_caught` shows the moved row is caught by the root only. Corrected by SER-R2-F3: the recount now refuses exactly what the recipe refuses (an entity id with a zero byte, conflicting labels) and accepts an empty id as the recipe does | PARTIAL: FIXED: `scripts/recount-entity-flow-series.py` (checked by hand on crafted label files) L9 2026-10-14: no test exercises it. ## Proof ladder level 3: source-signed data (loop 62, ADR-0028), self-noted before review
| ID | Actor | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L3-F1 | Data thief / submitter | High | A claim names a signed report it does not match (other value, metric, subject, source, time, report or key), or skips the intake | One intake (`SignedSources::accept_claim`) binds every claim field to the payload (spec R-SIG-7); `Claim::decode` refuses `SignedSource` | TESTED: `signed::tests::every_claim_field_is_bound_to_the_payload`, `claim::tests::decode_refuses_signed_source_claims`, `signed::tests::claim_decode_refuses_signed_source_claims`. L9 2026-10-14: tests exist and assert every listed field; CLOSED |
| L3-F2 | Forger | High | A report signed by someone other than the source, an edited payload, or a malleated signature | EIP-191 canonical form only (`v` 27/28, low `s`), signer must equal the registered key's | TESTED: `signed::tests::a_forged_signature_is_refused`, `signed::tests::a_wrong_key_is_refused`, `level3::a_tampered_fixture_or_another_documents_key_is_refused`. L9 2026-10-14: tests assert edit, garbage, high-s and wrong key; only the v 27/28 rule lacks its own case (Low); CLOSED |
| L3-F3 | Key thief | High | A stolen source key signs false values (level 3 is in the money default, so they can settle markets) | `mark_compromised`: nothing signed by the key counts any more, whatever its stated time; accepted reports observed or accepted after `since` are listed for re-review; 7-day intake window; equivocation suspends the key | DEFERRED: compromise handling tested (`signed::tests::a_retired_key_signs_only_the_past_and_a_compromised_key_nothing`, `level3_intake::a_new_key_restates_the_truth_after_a_theft`, `level3_lifecycle::a_fact_is_settleable_only_after_the_dispute_window`); a theft is caught only when the source reports it or equivocates. TODO H6: level-3 settlement unwind (with C2). L9 2026-10-14: still partly true; no level-3 fact is served or settled today (library only, no real source), so not a launch blocker until one is wired |
| L3-F4 | Replayer | Medium | An old signed report fed in again, out of order, or with a second signature over the same payload | One payload per `(key, sequence)`; exact replay and re-signature are `Replay`; 7-day age and 300 s future bounds; any order (L3R-F5); entries older than the window pruned (L3R2-F5) | TESTED: `signed::tests::a_used_sequence_is_refused_but_order_is_free`; sequence book rules changed by L3R-F5 |
| L3-F5 | Equivocating source | Medium | The source signs two different values for one fact or one sequence, and a buyer gets whichever suits a submitter | Fact book per source (across keys) and sequence book per key; both reports kept as evidence; the fact disputed (no value) and every key involved suspended until re-review (ADR-0028 amendment 1) | TESTED: `signed::tests::two_values_for_one_fact_or_one_sequence_suspend_the_key`, `level3_intake::a_disputed_fact_accepts_nothing_until_review` |
| L3-F6 | Cross-source replayer / reviewer error | Medium | A report from source A presented as source B, A's key used for B's payload, or a key for B registered under A's origin | Key id binds source and signer; payload source must be the key's source; claim source must be the payload's; all keys of a source share one origin; an origin serves one source (L3R-F7) | TESTED: `signed::tests::a_report_never_crosses_sources`, `level3_intake::another_source_cannot_use_a_taken_origin` |
| L3-F7 | Coordinator | Low | Sequence and fact books live in one coordinator's store; another coordinator could accept a replay or the other side of an equivocation | One book on chain for every coordinator and client: `OnyxSignedBook` holds the key registry, the never-pruned `(key, sequence)` and payload books and the fact book (ADR-0028 amendment 6, spec R-SIG-ON-1..6); consumers settle on its `settleable` at a finalized block; each coordinator's `SignedSources` is a pre-check (still not `Clone`) | FIXED 2026-10-17 (C2, not deployed): `test_L3_F7_AnotherCoordinatorMeetsTheOtherSideOfAnEquivocation`, `test_L3_F7_AReplayThroughAnotherCoordinatorIsRefused`, `test_L3_F7_SequenceEquivocationAcrossCoordinators`, `test_L3_F7_TheChainBookMatchesTheStoreOnTraces0To39` (differential traces, all four ranges), `level3_chain_anvil::two_coordinators_meet_in_the_chain_book` (opt-in, anvil). Wired 2026-10-17 (C10): coordinators post every report they take (`every_report_taken_is_posted_whatever_the_store_says`), the API serves only `settleable` at a finalized block (C10-2..C10-5). The live Base Sepolia deploy: TODO C10 (lead) |
| L3-F8 | Reviewer | Medium | Key provenance is a review record: a lookalike origin, or a source whose origin is not the publisher named in its rights, would register a key nobody legitimate controls | Origin must be a host name (never an IP); one origin per source; the review must tie the origin to the reviewed rights. No real source is wired in | ACCEPTED: origin rules enforced (`signed::tests::origin_hosts`, `level3_intake::another_source_cannot_use_a_taken_origin`); the residual is reviewer judgement and only matters once a real source is registered, which the hard limit forbids without a rights review. Reopen before the first real signed source: written checklist plus keys-document re-fetch. L9 2026-10-14: still partly true, no real source wired, accepted until one is proposed |
| L3-F9 | zkTLS | Info | zkTLS (lane b) would prove the HTTPS response without the source's cooperation | Design only; adoption criteria in ADR-0028 item 8 (non-alpha, TLS 1.3, audited, license-clean, bondable Notary trust) | ACCEPTED: not an attack but a design option for level 3 lane (b); adoption criteria in ADR-0028 item 8; the site lists it as planned. Reopen when a zkTLS stack meets those criteria (then a Phase C item). L9 2026-10-14: nothing built, nothing claimed |
| L3R-F1 | Key thief | High | A stolen retired key signed never-stated facts dated just before its rotation and they were accepted for the whole 7-day window (the signer sets `observed_unix`) | A retired key's reports count only while `now < retired_at + RETIRED_GRACE_SECS` (1 h) | FIXED loop 63: `level3_intake::a_retired_key_is_dead_after_its_grace_period` |
| L3R-F2 | Griefer / relayer | Medium | Any second report for a fact suspended the key, even with the same value, so relaying an honest re-publish or a dual-sign during rotation suspended an honest key | Same value = `AlreadyStated` (restatement, nobody suspended); only a different value equivocates | FIXED loop 63: `level3_intake::a_same_value_restatement_suspends_nobody` |
| L3R-F3 | Key thief | High | When two keys of a source disagreed, only the second was suspended: a thief stating a lie first got the honest key suspended and the lie stayed accepted | The fact becomes `Disputed` (no value), the accepted report is withdrawn to re-review, every key involved is suspended; `resolve_fact` / `reinstate_key` for the reviewer | FIXED loop 63: `level3_intake::a_thief_first_lie_is_withdrawn_and_the_fact_disputed` |
| L3R-F4 | Key thief | Medium | After `mark_compromised`, the thief's fact entries stayed, so the source's new key restating the truth was suspended: no recovery | `mark_compromised` withdraws everything the key stated from `since` (observed or recorded): accepted reports to re-review, their facts cleared, its reports out of disputes | FIXED loop 63: `level3_intake::a_new_key_restates_the_truth_after_a_theft` |
| L3R-F5 | Censor | Medium | The per-key high-water mark let anyone holding a later public report refuse every earlier unsubmitted one by delivering it first | High-water mark removed; the never-pruned `(key, sequence)` book plus the 7-day window is the replay guard | FIXED loop 63: `level3_intake::a_later_sequence_first_censors_nothing` |
| L3R-F6 | Equivocating source | Low | A contradicting value under an older sequence was refused as plain `Replay`: no evidence kept, key still active | The fact book runs before acceptance; an unused old sequence reaches it and equivocates | FIXED loop 63: `level3_intake::a_contradiction_under_an_older_sequence_is_evidence` |
| L3R-F7 | Reviewer error | Low | THREATS L3-F6 said a key for B under A's origin was refused; only a second origin for one source was | Origin -> source map: an origin serves one source (`OriginTaken`) | FIXED loop 63: `level3_intake::another_source_cannot_use_a_taken_origin` |
| L3R-F8 | Coordinator / on-chain port | Info | Freshness, grace and `accepted_at` use the caller's `now` (coordinator clock, not chain time, not checked monotonic); sequence `u64::MAX` could have bricked a key under a high-water mark | `u64::MAX` reserved (`SequenceReserved`). The chain book uses `block.timestamp` for freshness, grace, retire and compromise points, `recordedAt`, `acceptedAt` and the dispute window (R-SIG-ON-4); the store's clock is monotonic (`ClockWentBack`) and takes the latest block's timestamp | FIXED 2026-10-17 (C2): `level3_intake::the_top_sequence_is_reserved`, `test_L3R_F8_FreshnessUsesBlockTime`, `test_L3R_F8_RetiredGraceUsesBlockTime`, `test_L3R_F8_CompromisePointIsBoundedByBlockTime`, `level3_chain_book::the_clock_never_steps_back` |
| L3R2-F1 | Key thief | High | `reinstate_key` set a suspended key to `Active`, so a stolen retired key that contradicted within its grace, then was reinstated, signed fresh facts a day later (the L3R-F1 fix undone); one enum held both life cycle and suspension | Life cycle (forward only: Active -> Retired -> Compromised) separate from a suspension flag; reinstating clears the flag only (ADR-0028 amendment 2, transition table); exhaustive check of every sequence of up to 5 events against a reference model, all 56 state/event pairs | FIXED loop 64: `level3_lifecycle::reinstating_never_resurrects_a_retired_key`, `level3_lifecycle::every_state_and_event_pair` |
| L3R2-F2 | Reviewer error / insider | Medium | `mark_compromised` took any `since`: a forward-dated point kept forgeries accepted while the key read compromised; `since = 0` silently erased honest history; nothing recorded who did it | `since` after `now` refused (`TimeInFuture`); a later call may only move `since` earlier; every reviewer action in an append-only decision log (who, what, when, reason); `since = 0` allowed and logged. | ID | Actor | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |

| L3C-1 | Griefer / relayer | Medium | The chain records any validly signed payload, including one the off-chain intake refuses (wrong value kind, unregistered subject, non-UTF-8): a source that re-signs a corrected payload under the same sequence equivocates once anyone posts the first, and its key is suspended (review C2-R1 finding 1) | Rule stated: a signed payload burns its `(key, sequence)` for good; sources never re-sign under a used sequence (spec R-SIG-7, R-SIG-ON-1, ADR-0028 amendment 6 item 2) | TESTED: `test_L3C_1_ARefusedOffChainPayloadStillBurnsItsSequence` |
| L3C-2 | Base sequencer | Medium | The sequencer can delay or censor a post; forced inclusion through L1 can take up to the sequencing window (hours), longer than the 1 h dispute window, so a held-back contradiction lets the first value become settleable meanwhile (review C2-R1 finding 3) | Timestamps are not the sequencer's choice (OP Stack derivation, RESEARCH "Level 3 books on chain"); the contradiction still disputes the fact when it lands; nothing settles money on level 3 yet | DEFERRED: TODO H6 (dispute window above the forced-inclusion bound before any level-3 settlement). The serving policy is in (C10, spec R-SIG-ON-7): a fact is held while any of its posts known to the operator is pending or not final, and a post pending over 600 s stops level 3 (`c10_3_a_delayed_contradiction_holds_the_fact`, `c10_3_a_post_pending_too_long_stops_level_3`) |
| L3C-3 | Reorg | Low | A post in an unfinalized block can be reorged out or reordered, so a fact read as settleable at `latest` can change | Consumers read `settleable` at a finalized block (spec R-SIG-ON-6); `SignedBookCast::check_settleable` takes the block tag | ACCEPTED: the read rule is in the spec and the client takes a finalized tag; the 1 h window is longer than Base finality, and nothing settles on level 3 until H6 |
| L3C-4 | Store holder | Low | One far-future `now` (milliseconds for seconds, a bad RPC answer) moved the monotonic store clock for good, so every later action failed `ClockWentBack` (review C2-R1 finding 4) | The clock moves only when an action changes the store; a refused action moves nothing. A time ahead that the store acts on still moves it; the store is a pre-check, the chain decides | FIXED 2026-10-17 (C10): `level3_chain_book::a_refused_action_does_not_move_the_clock`, `level3_chain_book::the_clock_never_steps_back`; coordinators take `now` from the chain's latest block and refuse one far from the host clock (`c10_4_a_chain_clock_far_from_the_host_is_refused_and_nothing_changes`, `the_store_runs_on_the_latest_block_time_never_back`) |

| L3C-6 | - | Info | The spec said a dispute holds at most one report per key; a key that contradicts its own accepted report adds two | Wording: at most two per key, then the key is suspended and posts nothing | docs-only: docs/spec/proof-ladder.md |

| L3C-8 | Griefer | Medium | Junk writes to the book (a stranger's key, a registered key id signed by someone else, a payload naming another source, a malleated signature, a mutated payload) | Key registered by the reviewer, key's source bound to the payload, canonical EIP-191 signature by the registered signer before any write | TESTED: `test_L3_F7_OnlyARegisteredKeyWrites`, `test_L3C_8_NonCanonicalSignatureFormsAreRefused` (v 0/1/29/30, 64-byte, zero r or s, empty; review C2-R2), `testFuzz_AMutatedPayloadIsNeverAccepted` |

| L3C-10 | Reviewer key holder | Medium | One immutable reviewer key registers, retires, compromises, reinstates and resolves | Every decision is an event with its reason; the reviewer cannot write reports or change a recorded sequence | DEFERRED: TODO H1 (multisig or timelock) |
| L3C-11 | Relayer across deployments | Low | What a source signs names no chain id and no book address, so anyone can post a report to every `OnyxSignedBook` (any chain, any redeploy, a rehearsal anvil) that registered its key; a source keeping a separate sequence counter per deployment, or a test key registered in a production book, equivocates there and its key is suspended (review C2-R2) | By design: a report is the source's statement, also verified off chain, not an authorization, so replaying it states nothing new. Reopen on written permission or an openly licensed issuer attestation (owner decision). L9 2026-10-14: grep finds no Chainlink reader anywhere; the attack needs a build that does not exist |
| POR-2 | Reader | Medium | If ever built: a PoR answer proves only that the oracle network wrote a number at a round, not that the reserves exist or are unencumbered; a self-attested feed is the issuer's own claim | Any future metric must say "declared by the issuer via the oracle" and never "reserves held"; proof level for the attribution stays a claim | ACCEPTED: with POR-1, nothing built. Reopen when POR-1 unblocks: the metric must say 'declared by the issuer via the oracle', never 'reserves held', proof level a claim. L9 2026-10-14: not built, accepted with POR-1 |

## Post-merge review ATT-R1 (of the level-2 attempts feature, e59c250): 2 should have blocked

| Id | Sev | Threat | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| ATT-R1-F1 | High (blocking) | The runners (fiscaldata, EDGAR) returned `Err` for a round without a value, so `results_store`'s attempt branch was unreachable; and the store was rewritten per run, so a re-draw's store dropped draw 0 and `verify_attempts_onchain` refused the honest multi-draw fact | FIXED: runners return the run whatever the outcome (`RoundRun::claim: Option`, `RoundRun::value()`); `append_results` / `ObservationStore::append` add rounds and never replace them; the `level2-round` examples append to an existing `--store`. End to end (runner, store, API, client, chain draw records): `att_r1_non_value_store::a_round_without_a_value_is_published_and_checks_on_chain`, `a_redraw_store_keeps_the_earlier_round_and_verifies_on_chain` (also shows a replaced store fails) |
| ATT-R1-F2 | High (blocking) | Data thief: the free `/attempts` answer served a dated fact's honest reveals before its value settled; the value a later round sells was readable for free | FIXED: reveals only once the fact is closed (`ObservationFeed::fact_closed`: a value, or a fixed fact with a round; the store refuses a value for a fixed fact after a round without one); before that rounds are served sealed (`revealed` replaces `reveals`: no observation, page hash or salt); the client checks a sealed round's draw, committee, commits, round id and result hash (`check_sealed_attempt`, `CheckedAttempt::sealed`) and refuses sealed rounds in `outcome=all` and for fixed facts. Trade-off: a sealed round's outcome is the server's word. `att_r1_attempts::the_free_answer_does_not_leak_the_value_a_later_round_sells`, `a_fixed_fact_without_a_value_is_closed_and_served_open` |
| ATT-R1-F3 | Medium | Coordinator: commits and reveals carried no observer signature, so a fixed draw's real round (a dissenting one) could be replaced by a fabricated round for the same draw and every client check passed; the docs claimed a hidden dissenting round is detected | FIXED (ADR-0027 amendment 7): each observer signs its commit and its reveal (EIP-191 secp256k1, canonical `v`/low `s`, as level 3) over `observation_commit_message` (round id, attempt, observer, commit) and `observation_reveal_message` (round id, attempt, observer, keccak of the observation: value or `Unavailable`, time, page hash; salt). The signer is the observer's pool address, which the pool hash, the draw and `drawCommit` already bind. `ObservationRound::commit`/`reveal` refuse an unsigned one (`BadSignature`); every consumer path (`rebuild_round`, so store load, `check`/`check_attempt`/`check_sealed_attempt`, `verify_observation`, `verify_attempts`, and through them `verify_observation_onchain`/`verify_attempts_onchain`) requires them; the web verifier checks both signatures of every shown round. Transcripts carry `sig` on every commit and reveal. Tests: `att_r1_attempts::a_substituted_round_for_a_fixed_draw_is_refused` (was `known_limit_...`: own-key, copied-signature, real-commit and other-attempt forgeries refused at load and by the client), `observe::tests::commits_and_reveals_need_the_observers_own_signature`, `registry_vectors::a_consumer_rebuilds_the_observation_from_its_own_template`, web `level2_round::an_unsigned_commit_or_reveal_fails`, `the_edgar_rounds_check_signed_and_sealed`, e2e "moved observer signature". Residuals: a server can leave a reveal out (the observer shows as committed, not revealed), and a sealed round's outcome is its word until the fact is closed (ATT-R1-F2); rehearsal observers use public fake test keys (`observe::test_keys`), so the rehearsals show the mechanism, not independent observers |

Residual: in the rehearsal the observers read the record the chain wrapper returned; a real observer must read `drawOf` itself. `level2_draw_chain::observers_commit_only_to_a_draw_whose_beacon_is_fixed_on_chain` |
| ATT-R1-F5 | Low | The free `/attempts` endpoint had no rate budget and built its body under the catalog read lock (AUD-1-F4, AUD-2-F4 pattern) | FIXED: per-client scope `attempts:` (`free_attempts_per_minute`, 30), the template and the fact's rounds copied before the lock is released. `tests::level2::free_attempts_are_rate_limited_per_client` |

Limit, corrected by review R9: a book lost AFTER its round's log snapshot (receipts on chain) VOIDS the fact (its round cannot be finished: the receipted reveals left with it; REVLOG-R5-1d), and operator action reaches it (REVLOG-R9-F3). Review R8's "13 of 2,400" counted only the cases ending in the fatal state, under a client check with `transcriptComplete` stubbed true; the real counts are in REVLOG-R9-F2. Review R9 also found a lost book adopting a draw already published (REVLOG-R9-F1, fixed). `revlog_r8::r8_2_lost_book_adopts_the_latest_draw_after_a_fixed_one` (the PoC: draw 1 adopted and opened), `r8_2_the_pending_branch_adopts_the_latest_draw_too` |

Reviewer: `ONYX_R8_CASES=1 ONYX_R8_SEED=17822 cargo test -p onyx-source-fiscaldata --test revlog_r8 property_the_book_never_loses_a_draw` | FIXED: (a) a runner reads the results store before a run (`run_and_save(.., results, ..)` in both adapters, `note_results` → `ObservationResults::note_published_draws`, from `ObservationStore::published_draws`); a draw the results store publishes is never adopted (`ObservationResults::adoptable`); the latest one it publishes is followed by a next draw (it was released when published); without the results store read nothing is adopted; a fact whose VALUE it publishes stops the run (settled) unless the book still keeps that round (a crash after the write republishes it unchanged). ## Chain indexer review IDX-R1 (2026-10-12)

Branch `indexer-fixes`. Findings of the lead's review of ADR-0033; each PoC is now a regression test in `crates/onyx-api/src/indexer_tests.rs`.

| Id | Sev | Threat | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| IDX-R1-1 | Low-Med | One forged or buggy log at a real (block, log index) wedged the indexer for good: every later poll failed on the overlap re-read before `judge` ran, the cursor froze, and a restart reloaded the bad event (recovery meant deleting the state file) | FIXED (the wedge): events are hints; a different log at a known position is kept as another candidate (at most 4 per position; a state file with more is refused), counted (`conflicts`, `conflictingPositions`, `lastConflict` on `/v1/health`), and `getFinalizedRoot` plus the held data hash and binding decide; `judge` runs even when the scan fails. Runbook: docs/ops/deployment.md "Chain indexer" (cursor reset, never needed for this). `idx_r1_1_a_conflicting_log_is_a_candidate_and_the_contract_decides` (the PoC, restart included), `idx_r1_1_candidates_per_position_are_bounded`, `idx_r1_1_judging_runs_when_the_scan_fails`. CORRECTED by IDX-R2-1: "more dropped" plus "served only if a kept log names the contract's root" let 4 forged logs read first keep a final held shard out for good; a full position now evicts refuted or redundant logs and the contract's view alone decides the root |
| IDX-R1-2 | Low | One block with more `Finalized` logs than one answer may carry (the 1 MiB RPC body cap, or 10,000 logs) failed as a one-block range every poll: no later event was ever found | FIXED: the indexer's transport reads up to 16 MiB (`HyperPost::for_logs`; 10,000 logs fit); a block still refused is read for the held shards only (block header first, so a dead node moves nothing; then held shard ids as a topic-2 filter, 64 per call) and counted (`partialBlocks`). Not split by round: a block's rounds are unknown before it is read. Residual: other operators' shards in such a block are not listed until the overlap reads it whole. `idx_r1_2_one_oversized_block_is_read_for_the_held_shards` (the PoC), `idx_r1_2_a_body_cap_is_survived_and_a_dead_node_moves_nothing`, `x402::tests::rpc_transport_has_its_own_body_cap` |
| IDX-R1-3 | Low | A dispute ending `NoValidRoot` (`dEnd` emits no event) left the shard `pending` forever and cost an `eth_call` per poll | FIXED: a held shard that is not final is checked with `shardState`; `NoValidRoot`, `Unresolved`, `Voided`, `Empty` and never-opened (`not_on_chain`, a forged event; judged again if a new event names it) are marked ended (`ended` count) and not polled. `idx_r1_3_a_case_ending_without_a_root_is_ended_and_not_polled` (selector pinned there) |
| IDX-R1-4 | Low | A wrong `deployBlock` in the manifest: later than the deployment skips events silently | FIXED: `Indexer::check_deploy_block` (no code at `deployBlock - 1`, code at `deployBlock`; a node without old state is a clear "archive node" error); `onyx-node`, demo-local and `index-scan` refuse to start otherwise. Checked live: 0x7d25..7116 has no code at 48037566 and code at 48037567 (sepolia.base.org serves that state). `idx_r1_4_the_deploy_block_is_checked_against_the_code` |
| IDX-R1-5 | Info | `/v1/health` walked every event per request (`known()`); the state file was fsync'd per range on the async runtime; health lists held shard ids and node error text to anyone | FIXED: health is a snapshot rebuilt per poll (a request clones it); saves once per poll and every 50 ranges, on `spawn_blocking` (`stateWrites` counted); `ONYX_INDEX_HEALTH=summary` shows counts only (docs/ops/deployment.md "Chain indexer", config.md). `idx_r1_5_health_is_a_snapshot_saves_are_bounded_and_detail_can_be_hidden`, `config::tests::the_indexer_is_opt_in_and_bounded` |

## Chain indexer review IDX-R2 (2026-10-12)

Branch `indexer-fixes`, strike 1 on this branch. Fresh review of the IDX-R1 fixes; the PoC is now a regression test in `crates/onyx-api/src/indexer_tests.rs`. ADR-0033 Amendment 2.

| Id | Sev | Threat | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| IDX-R2-1 | Medium | A lying backend fills the 4-candidate cap at the honest log's (block, log index) with forged logs naming the held shard with wrong roots; every honest re-read was dropped by the cap, and a shard was served only if a kept log named the contract's root, so it stayed `chain_disagrees` forever, also after a restart | FIXED: the contract's view alone decides the root (a kept log only names the (round, shard) to judge; `chain_disagrees` removed). A full position refuses a newcomer whose (round, shard) is already named, not held or ended, and otherwise evicts a log whose shard is not held or whose (round, shard) ended or never opened, then one whose (round, shard) another kept log names; never the last log naming a held (round, shard) not ended. Unjudged logs (after a restart) are judged before the scan. Counted: `candidatesDropped`, `candidatesEvicted`. Guarantee: once a log naming a held (round, shard) is kept, it is judged until the contract ends it. Residual (documented, ADR-0033 Amendment 2): a backend answering every read of a block inside the overlap can withhold the honest log, or fill its position first with logs for four other genuine held (round, shard)s the contract has opened and no other log names; recovery: change provider, reset the cursor. `idx_r2_1_forged_logs_filling_a_position_cannot_keep_a_final_shard_out` (the PoC, restart included), `idx_r2_1_a_sustained_forgery_stream_cannot_evict_the_honest_shard` (16 alternating polls, fresh forged rounds, unheld shards and wrong roots each lying answer, restart midway, shard pending until after the position left the overlap), `idx_r2_1_a_full_position_evicts_only_what_the_contract_refuted`; CORRECTED by IDX-R3-1/2: "until the contract ends it" meant one `shardState` answer, one wrong view was cached, and a refused newcomer reopened refuted slots |
| IDX-R2-2 | Low | The deploy-block check (IDX-R1-4) called any `eth_getCode` failure, including a transient 429 or timeout, or a node whose head is below `deployBlock`, "needs an archive node", and refused to start | FIXED: each read retried after 0.5, 1.5 and 4 s; the error names the cause: the node failing (with the try count and last error), head below `deployBlock` (`eth_blockNumber`; wrong network or syncing), no old state (`missing trie node`, `pruned` and similar; not retried; the only case naming an archive node), or the real mismatch. `idx_r2_2_the_deploy_check_retries_and_names_the_cause`, `idx_r1_4_the_deploy_block_is_checked_against_the_code` |
| IDX-R2-3 | Low | A hostile 16 MiB `eth_getLogs` body like `[0,0,...]` parsed into about 8 million `serde_json::Value`s (0.3 to 0.5 GB) per answer | FIXED: `HttpJsonRpc` parses every answer with a budget of 262,144 values (`roots::MAX_RPC_VALUES`; a full 10,000-log answer is about 150,000), refused while read. `roots::tests::an_answer_with_too_many_values_is_refused_while_read` |
| IDX-R2-4 | Info | The run page said "Nobody hands the API a list of shards", but operators supply the held specs | FIXED: "a list of servable shards" (`apps/web/src/routes/run/+page.svelte`; no browser test checks the sentence) L9 2026-10-14: docs-only: apps/web/src/routes/run/+page.svelte |

## Chain indexer review IDX-R3 (2026-10-13)

Branch `indexer-fixes`, strike 2 on this branch (a third failing review: the lead decides a narrower design or parks the fixes). Both PoCs are regression tests in `crates/onyx-api/src/indexer_tests.rs`. ADR-0033 Amendment 3. Rule now: no single answer from one RPC call is final; an end or a final view counts only when reads on two polls agree, and one read, lying or failing, never makes a held (round, shard)'s last log evictable.

| Id | Sev | Threat | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| IDX-R3-1 | Medium | `add_log` reset a (round, shard) from `not_on_chain` to unchecked before the full-position refusal: a liar naming four forged keys again at another full position un-refuted them each poll, so every honest read of the honest log's position was dropped and a final held shard was never served. Also: a backend failing every `eth_call` about its forged keys kept them unchecked, and an unchecked slot was never evicted | FIXED: a refused newcomer changes nothing; a kept log naming a key judged never opened marks it for one more read and keeps its end and eviction rank. Eviction order: not held or end confirmed on two polls; redundant (contradicted first); the last log of a key whose judging failed on two polls. Never the last log of a held key whose latest read was live, that one read said ended, or that failed on one poll only. A failed judging `eth_call` is sent once more. `idx_r3_1_a_refused_newcomer_cannot_reopen_refuted_slots` (PoC B, restart included), `idx_r3_1_forged_keys_whose_judging_fails_make_room`, `idx_r3_1_one_failing_call_never_costs_a_held_key_its_slot`, `idx_r3_one_lying_end_never_costs_a_held_key_its_slot` (found by the property test in a first draft that let one unconfirmed end make a slot evictable), `idx_r2_1_a_full_position_evicts_only_what_the_contract_refuted` (now one poll later) |
| IDX-R3-2 | Low-Med | One lying `eth_call` stuck until a restart: one `shardState` answer of Voided (or any end) made the shard ended, not polled and evictable first; one wrong `getFinalizedRoot` answer was cached, leaving a later-final shard refused | FIXED: an end counts only when a read on a later poll also says ended (no live read between); a final view is cached only when a read on a later poll names the same one, or once admitted; a disagreeing read starts over from the newer one. ADR-0033 Amendment 2's "whatever a backend answers later" and docs/ops/incident-response.md corrected. `idx_r3_2_one_lying_view_answer_is_never_terminal` (PoC A), `idx_r1_3_a_case_ending_without_a_root_is_ended_and_not_polled` and `held_data_that_does_not_hash_to_the_root_is_not_served` (two reads now), `idx_r3_property_no_single_answer_keeps_a_held_final_shard_out` (400 seeds, up to a third of answers lying or failing, never twice in a row to one question, forged logs at the honest position from its first read, a restart each; checked once at 20,000 seeds and at a 50% liar). Residual restated by IDX-R4-1 (ADR-0033 Amendment 4): the operator's node is trusted for the operator's liveness only. A lying node (two agreeing lies, lies timed across calls, a log withheld from every read) can delay serving a held shard until it answers honestly and a held-shard rescan or restart runs; it can never make a wrong or unfinal root pass. Operators use a node they trust |
| IDX-R3-3 | Info | The STATUS residual line named only a backend withholding a log, not four genuine held (round, shard)s filling the honest log's position first | FIXED; docs-only: docs/adr/0033-chain-indexer.md; the residuals (a backend withholding a log, four genuine held (round, shard)s filling the position first, timed lies, two lies) are stated in docs/adr/0033-chain-indexer.md; the STATUS line has since been overwritten. L9 2026-10-14: ADR-0033 is the durable record |

## Chain indexer review IDX-R4 (2026-10-13)

Branch `indexer-fixes`, strike 3 on this branch (IDX-R2, R3 and R4 each found a way a lying RPC backend keeps a held final shard unserved). The lead's decision, ADR-0033 Amendment 4: threat-model correction. The operator's RPC node is trusted for the operator's own liveness; correctness never depends on it (every served root is read on chain again per request, clients verify roots on their own nodes), so a lying operator node can only make the operator serve less, fixed by using a node it trusts. Two cheap guarantees, no further liveness hardening. The PoC is a regression test in `crates/onyx-api/src/indexer_tests.rs`.

| Id | Sev | Threat | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| IDX-R4-1 | Low-Med (liveness only) | Two lying `shardState` answers on two polls (one backend of three always lying: 1 in 9 per pair of polls) confirmed a false end for the honest held key in its challenge window; a confirmed end made its last log evictable, four forged logs naming the held shard in rounds never opened evicted it, and once its block left the overlap the saved events no longer held it: the shard, final later, was never served, also after a restart | FIXED within the corrected model: (1) a chain-status end (or a failed judging) never makes the last kept log naming a held (round, shard) evictable; only a log of a shard not held or one repeating a key another kept log names may go; (2) a held-shard rescan (`eth_getLogs` from `deployBlock` filtered to the held ids, capped ranges, split and budget as the scan) from the third poll after every start and every `ONYX_INDEX_RESCAN_POLLS` polls (default 240) merges what it finds as candidates and reads every confirmed end again (and drops cached views of shards not served); a log it finds may replace a held log at its position that the same answer did not return and whose end is confirmed (else forged held-shard logs read first would block it for good). Residual (accepted): a lying node delays serving until it answers honestly and a rescan or restart runs. `idx_r4_1_two_lying_ends_cost_no_log_and_the_rescan_reads_them_again` (the PoC: served after the periodic rescan without a restart, and after one), `idx_r4_1_a_log_withheld_in_the_overlap_is_found_by_the_rescan_after_a_restart`, `idx_r4_1_one_of_three_lying_recovers_after_a_rescan` (the review's run shape, 60 seeds per run; 1,000 once), `idx_r4_relaxed_liars_recover_after_a_rescan` (the review's four relaxed models, 40 seeds each per run; 1,000 once), `idx_r2_1_a_full_position_evicts_only_unheld_or_repeated_keys`, `idx_r3_1_a_refused_newcomer_cannot_reopen_refuted_slots` and `idx_r3_1_forged_keys_whose_judging_fails_wait_for_the_rescan` (rewritten: recovery by the rescan); `idx_r3_property_no_single_answer_keeps_a_held_final_shard_out` unchanged. Each new test fails with its guarantee reverted |
| IDX-R4-2 | Low | (pre-existing, review note) One lying `getFinalizedRoot` answer naming the held rows' true root for a round never opened admitted that round, so forged rounds of a held shard could crowd a metric's 16 candidates (`MAX_METRIC_CANDIDATES`; `ChainRoots` still refused each per request) | FIXED: a (round, shard) enters the catalog only when `shardState` reads Finalized or two reads on two polls agree on the view. `idx_r4_2_one_lying_view_never_lists_a_forged_round` |


## Chain indexer review IDX-R5 (2026-10-13)

Branch `indexer-fixes`; scope: correctness, and recovery once the RPC is honest. ADR-0033 Amendment 5. Correction to IDX-R3-2, IDX-R4-1 and Amendment 4: "a lying node can never make a wrong or unfinal root pass" was wrong for this server; `ChainRoots` reads through the same node (IDX-R5-3).

| Id | Sev | Threat | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| IDX-R5-1 | Medium (merge-blocking) | Judging was pinned to the highest `finalized` head ever read (`i.head = i.head.max(reported)`): one lying answer far ahead made every later judging `eth_call` fail on an honest node ("header not found"), so no held shard was admitted or ended until a restart | FIXED: judging reads at this poll's reported head, never a remembered one; a (round, shard) all of whose kept logs lie above that head (a lagging backend) waits for a later poll; `/v1/health` `finalizedHead` is the last head read. `idx_r5_1_one_lying_finalized_head_fails_one_poll_only` (the review's PoC 1: served on the next honest poll, and after a restart), `idx_r5_1_a_lie_while_pending_never_pins_later_judging`. Both fail with the remembered max restored |
| IDX-R5-2 | Low | Servable keys admitted from lies (one lying poll: 16 forged rounds of a held shard with `shardState` Finalized) were never judged again and filled the metric's 16 candidates (`MAX_METRIC_CANDIDATES`, lib.rs `/v1/metrics`) ahead of the honest round, until a restart | FIXED: every rescan reads each served shard's final view again; two reads on two polls naming the same other view (or none) take it out of the catalog (`Catalog::remove_shard`) and judge it from the start; one refuting read changes nothing; `removed` on `/v1/health`. `idx_r5_2_lying_admissions_are_removed_after_a_rescan` (PoC 2: only the honest round listed, forged rounds end `not_on_chain`), `idx_r5_2_one_refuting_read_never_removes_a_served_shard`. The first fails with the re-judging removed, the second with removal on one read |
| IDX-R5-3 | Medium (docs) | `ChainRoots` uses the same `ONYX_RPC_URL` as the indexer (onyx-node main.rs `rpc()`/`rpc_logs()`), so "every request re-reads the root on chain" adds nothing against a lying operator node; a lying node can make the server serve a wrong or unfinal root. The client's chain check is opt-in: `verify_response(…, chain: None)` passes with `chain_checked: false` | CLOSED: the client checks roots on its own node by default and `verify_response(.., None)` is refused (`tests::the_client_checks_roots_on_its_own_node_by_default`, `tests::responses_verify_client_side_and_tampering_is_rejected`); the opt-out says NOT VERIFIED ON CHAIN. A lying operator node can still make the server serve a wrong root, which the default client refuses; an optional second server node is nice to have, TODO G1 keeps the default in SDKs. L9 2026-10-14: client-side attack closed by default; server-side residual accepted |
| IDX-R5-4 | Low (cost) | The held-shard rescan grows by about 216 `eth_getLogs` calls per day of age per 64 held shards (≈79k per rescan after a year), shared the scan's 2,000-call per-poll budget, and a rescan longer than the interval ran back to back | FIXED: own per-poll budget (`ONYX_INDEX_RESCAN_CALLS`, default 100), resumed on the next poll; the next periodic rescan is counted from the end of the previous one, in polls (`ONYX_INDEX_RESCAN_POLLS`) or seconds (`ONYX_INDEX_RESCAN_SECS`); cost per day at 1 month and 1 year in deployment.md "Rescan cost" with a wider span recommended. `idx_r5_4_the_rescan_has_its_own_budget_and_resumes` (fails with the shared budget, and with the interval counted from the start); onyx-node `the_indexer_is_opt_in_and_bounded`. Residual: at the default hourly interval a year-old deployment costs about 441k rescan calls a day per 64 held shards at span 200 (documented; daily or a wider span cuts it to 79k or 35k) |
| IDX-R5-5 | Low | One lying `finalized` head far ahead moved the saved cursor up to 400,000 blocks (the scan's budget) past blocks the node had finalized; logs there were missed (held shards' until a rescan, others' for good) | FIXED: a poll reads at most `max_jump` blocks (`ONYX_INDEX_MAX_JUMP`, default 100 = the overlap) past the head this poll and the previous one both reported (or past the cursor), so the overlap reads every block one lie let pass again. Cost: a start reaches the head on its second poll. `idx_r5_5_one_lying_head_moves_the_cursor_one_overlap_at_most` (fails without the clamp). Residual: two agreeing lying heads on consecutive polls still move it (the two-answer model of IDX-R3) |
| IDX-R6-1 | Low (review IDX-R6; honest load-balanced node) | `recheck_served` can remove a served shard when a lagging backend answers two polls with a head past the event but before the shard became final (challenge window / dEnd) | FIXED M7 loop 3 (ADR-0033 Amendment 6): each served shard keeps the pin it was admitted at; a recheck below it is not read and refutes nothing (still due on a later poll): `idx_r6_1_a_read_below_the_admission_pin_never_removes_a_served_shard` (a backend between event and finalization for 12 polls removes nothing; a refutation at the pin still removes; fails with the fix reverted) |
| IDX-R6-2 | Low (review IDX-R6; ops) | Rescan progress is in memory only: a restart starts it again from deployBlock; with 1,000 held shards a full rescan takes ~47 h at the default budget, so frequent restarts never finish it | FIXED M7 loop 3 (ADR-0033 Amendment 6): the state file keeps a rescan in progress (`rescan: {next, to}`, range-checked on load); the rescan after a restart resumes there: `idx_r6_2_a_restart_resumes_the_rescan_where_it_stopped` (fails with the resume reverted; a bad saved range is refused). Residual: the deployment.md cost table still assumes <=64 held shards |

## Client-side reserve check (ROADMAP D3, ADR-0034 Amendment 2): self-noted before review (2026-10-17)

Branch `reserve-client`. The client re-runs the reserve serving check on answers it verified on
its own node (`reserve::client_check`, `onyx_api::client::verify_row`, `/v1/served/{metric}`,
`onyx_reserve_serve::client`; the browser runs `reserve::derive_entity_chain` on the week
export). Adversarial pass: operator skips the check, forged base, swapped scan, wrong label set
version, crafted chain list, data theft in fallback. Fresh review D3-R1 (2026-10-17): no base
forgery found; 2 Medium (duplicate work, padded list) and 3 Low fixed, rows D3-R1-1..6. Each test
below was shown failing with its check removed (break-the-code, 9 mutations: base check, `base_ref`
check, label set check, answer-is-a-link check, flow cap, de-duplication, `min_as_of`, trusted
hash, list cap).

| Id | Sev | Threat | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| RES-C1 | Medium | Operator skips the check: a gate that clears every row serves the newer forged-base shard's OKX row with `servingCheck {crossChecked: true}`; the row verifies against its finalized root on the client's node | MITIGATED for a client running G-6: the forged row's base is not the previous link's end, and a list naming both shards of a range is not a chain: `api_reserve::a_client_refuses_a_forged_row_from_an_operator_who_skips_the_check`; a forged middle link, a whole chain raised from the start (passes the circular `check_chain`), a forged landing: `reserve_client::a_forged_base_is_refused_by_the_client_whatever_the_operator_serves`. Other entities' honest rows in the same shards still pass |
| RES-C2 | Medium | Swapped scan: the operator builds and finalizes a chain on another scan (its hash in the first `base_ref`) that lands on that scan's totals, and offers that scan as the anchor | MITIGATED: the client builds its pin from its own scan file (`ReservePin::from_scan` recomputes hash and totals) and compares the hash with one it trusts; the swapped chain is refused against it: `reserve_client::a_chain_on_a_swapped_scan_is_refused` (also shows a pin taken from the operator would pass its own chain). Residual: the trusted hash is the repository's and the website's; TODO D21 (anchor on chain) |
| RES-C3 | Medium | Wrong label set version: a chain bound to label set v1 (or any other content) served as v2 reserves, or a pin built from a scan over another version | MITIGATED: every link's binding names the pinned `LabelSetRef::hash`, and `from_scan` runs `check_labels`: `reserve_client::a_chain_over_another_label_set_version_is_refused`. D1's date-ranged sets get a new hash and a new pin |
| RES-C4 | Low | A crafted `/v1/served` list or answer (list shape before fetching: D3-R1-2): a shard left out, added, duplicated or reordered, a chain cut before the scan, a landing on another block, another recipe, another entity's leaf or index, a row naming another range, flows whose u128 wrap in a signed sum, an answer from a shard outside the checked chain or with edited fields | MITIGATED: the list is a hint, the leaf index comes from the pin, and the answer must equal a proven link (round, shard, root, index, row bytes): `reserve_client::the_client_check_binds_recipe_landing_block_and_tiling`, `api_reserve::the_client_reruns_the_serving_check_on_api_answers` |
| RES-C5 | Low (rights) | The client check leaks reserve data where it is withheld: a free list, or the links, under `ONYX_RIGHTS=fallback` | MITIGATED: `/v1/served` carries no row, and is 403 `label_rights_withheld` in fallback before anything is read (also on a server without the gate); every link is a paid `/v1/proofs` row, refused in fallback; the browser check runs only on the week export, which a fallback build does not ship: `api_reserve::the_served_list_is_withheld_in_fallback`, `api_reserve::fallback_rights_sell_no_reserve_row` |
| RES-C6 | Medium (residual) | What a client cannot check without a full node: that the scan saw every output at the listed addresses, and that the ranges other than the landing (before it, and after it up to the answer) are on the best chain | PARTIAL: the scan's block can be checked against the client's own headers (`ScanSnapshot::check_block`); completeness needs a second node's scan, TODO D2. FIXED D22 for depth and the best chain: `client_check` takes the client's own header chain; the pin's scan and flows file (`ReservePin::check_on`) and every link's tip, not only the landing's, must be the chain's block with 6 confirmations (`reserve_client::d22_every_links_tip_must_be_on_the_clients_header_chain`, `reserve_dated::d22_every_forged_dated_span_fails_closed`). The browser's week check has no header file yet (TODO D12) |
| RES-C7 | Low | The website checks the committed week export with the client check, not live API answers: the browser has no chain read and no binding check of an API answer | TODO D20 (browser check of live reserve answers) |
| RES-C8 | Info (cost) | The client check costs one paid row per link (89 today, at the operator's price and time decay) | ACCEPTED: the rows are what is sold; a free bundle would give an entity's whole history away for one row's price. A client that trusts the operator for the base reads `servingCheck` instead. Bound since D22 (D3-R2-2 fixed): one row per link between the answer and its anchor, at most the client's budget (`DEFAULT_SPAN_BUDGET` 4,096 rows, 10.24 USDC at 2,500 micro-USDC); 1 row for an answer at the pinned landing; links outside the span are not fetched |
