Fails closed (no wrong balance is accepted), but no dated chain can be client-checked | FIXED D22 2026-10-18 (ADR-0034 Amendment 3): `ReservePin::from_dated_scan` (dated set and its history, flows file trusted by `FlowsFile::hash`, `totals_at`); each link bound to the pinned set's window for its blocks, not past the publication, the entity's row at its window index; the entity's membership-change delta (`change_at`, the serving check's) applied between links. `reserve_dated.rs::d22_the_client_check_passes_an_honest_dated_chain` (the former fail-closed test, now a pass: `a` and `b` across the change, `c` anchored at its exit, an answer after the scan) and `d22_every_forged_dated_span_fails_closed` (wrong window hash; a change without its delta, alone or with A raised to land on the scan; a tip off the header chain or under 6 confirmations; a span that skips a link; a stale pin; an untrusted, forged or missing flows file; a version without its history; a forged exit base); list side `client_dated.rs` |

## Client check after D1 (ROADMAP D22, ADR-0034 Amendment 3): self-noted before review (2026-10-18)

Branch `reserve-dated-client`. The client check reads dated sets, checks every link on its own
headers and runs as a span from an anchor (`reserve::derive_entity_span`, shared with the
browser). Adversarial pass: a dishonest operator who finalizes any shard (flows rerun, bases are
params), a griefer making the client pay, a stale pin. Break-the-code, 7 mutations on the new
checks: delta applied, every link's tip on the headers, window hash, trusted flows hash, pin on
the headers, base walk after the first link, each caught; the exit end check survives (equivalent:
the walk already implies it, kept as defence). Fresh review D22-R1 (2026-10-18): no wrong balance
accepted; 1 Medium (cost before cheap refusals) and 2 Low fixed, 1 Low documented, rows D22-R1-*.
Fresh review D22-R2 (2026-10-18): a wrong balance accepted under a trusted flows file that disagrees
with the finalized flows (Medium, fixed), a repeated flows block and the list's memory bound (Low,
fixed), rows D22-R2-*; cost figures recomputed (1 row 0.0025 USDC; 89 rows 0.2225 USDC; 4,096 rows
10.24 USDC; `1 + 89w` within 4,096 up to w = 46); break-the-code 8 mutations, each caught.

| Id | Sev | Threat | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| D22-1 | Info (design) | The span's first `base_ref` is no longer read: a span from mid-chain cannot tell which chain its first link continues | ACCEPTED: rows' flows are reruns and only bases are params, so the anchor fixes every base of the span; a forged base anywhere in it is refused (`reserve_client::d22_a_span_from_the_landing_pays_only_the_links_to_the_answer`: a forged middle in a suffix, a forged start of a suffix), and a chain on a swapped scan is refused by the pinned totals (`a_chain_on_a_swapped_scan_is_refused`) |
| D22-2 | Medium | The flows file decides a membership change's delta and the exit and entry anchors: an operator's file would move them | MITIGATED: the client takes the file only under a hash it trusts (`FlowsFile::hash`, Borsh, domain `onyx-reserve-flows-v1`), on its own headers with 6 confirmations, every flow at an address of the set and no address below zero (`reserve_dated::d22_every_forged_dated_span_fails_closed`: untrusted, forged, missing), and, since review D22-R2-1, its per-entity flows equal to the finalized rows' on every link of the span it covers (`d22_r2_a_trusted_flows_file_must_agree_with_the_finalized_flows`). Residual: the trusted file's per-address split within one entity is its word (RES-13), TODO D11 |
| D22-3 | Low (cost) | Griefing the budget: an operator finalizes many one-block shards between an old answer and the landing, so an honest-looking span is long | MITIGATED: the span is counted before any fetch and refused over the client's budget (`api_reserve::a_padded_or_broken_chain_list_is_refused_before_any_fetch`, budget 88 on 89 links); a newer pin shortens it; the operator pays a finalized round per shard |
| D22-4 | Low (liveness) | A client whose header chain lags refuses honest answers in the last 5 blocks before its tip, and a pin under 6 confirmations | ACCEPTED (RES-4 by design, fail closed): `d22_every_forged_dated_span_fails_closed` (C refused on headers one block short, B accepted) |
| D22-5 | Low | The browser's week check reads no header file: its shard tips and the scan's depth are the commitment's word | TODO D12 (the website's depth check, with the header refresh tool) |
| D22-R1-1 | Medium (review D22-R1, cost and liveness) | Paid fetches before cheap refusals: a stale answer far from the landing, an answer under 6 confirmations or a stale pin were refused only after the whole span was paid; a list could misdescribe a link's range and the client paid on | FIXED: `link_requests` takes the client's headers and `Limits` and refuses, before any fetch, a pin not on the headers with 6 confirmations, an answer older than `min_as_of` or not 6 deep; each `LinkRequest` carries the listed range and root and `LinkRequest::matches` stops the fetch at the first misdescribed link (`client_dated::d22_cheap_refusals_come_before_any_fetch`; `api_reserve` `fetch_links` checks every link). Residual: the budget counts links, not blocks: one-block finalized shards still cost up to the budget (D22-3) |
| D22-R1-2 | Low (review D22-R1, DoS) | With `MAX_LINKS` gone the free list was parsed whatever its length | FIXED: `Limits::max_listed` (`DEFAULT_MAX_LISTED` 1,048,576, about 225 years at 89 shards a week; a memory bound on an unpaid list, not a cost cliff): `client_dated::d22_cheap_refusals_come_before_any_fetch` (a 2-entry cap refused; a 20,002-range list parses and its landing answer costs one link) |
| D22-R1-3 | Low (review D22-R1) | `FlowsFile::hash` commits the blocks only; the summary `flows`, `height`, `hash` could disagree with them under a trusted hash (`reconcile` reads `flows`) | FIXED: `FlowsFile::check_consistent` in `from_dated_scan` (`reserve_dated::d22_every_forged_dated_span_fails_closed`: summary edited, same hash, refused) |
| D22-R1-4 | Low (review D22-R1, liveness) | A pin checks one dated version: windows carry the version, so shards bound to an older version's windows fail a newer pin | DOCUMENTED (ADR-0034 Amendment 3 item 4; the serving check has the same limit): a client pins the version its shards name. TODO D25 (the first published dated version, v3, shipped with P2a as test data; windows per version from the history come with dated manifests) |
| D22-R1-5 | Info (review D22-R1, tests) | The pin's six-confirmation case stood in for the per-link one on the committed chain; the flows half of `check_on` and the browser's path on a dated chain were untested; `l.to < l.from` reported as past the publication | FIXED: per-link depth is `reserve_dated`'s block 971,202 (doc corrected); a trusted flows file with a block off the headers refused, and the browser's `dated: None` path refuses the dated chain (`d22_every_forged_dated_span_fails_closed`); own error text. Exit or entry with a change inside the span, and leave-then-rejoin, are not in the fixture world: TODO D23 (v3 has both on real heights once its scan exists) |
| D22-R2-1 | Medium (review D22-R2, wrong balance under a trusted file) | The client applied a trusted flows file without checking it against the finalized flows, as the serving check does: a file under a trusted hash that says `new` received 1,200 where the rerun says 200 lowers `a`'s delta at the change by 1,000, and a chain with A's base raised by 1,000 lands on the scan exactly; the client accepted A's balance 1,000 too high | FIXED: `derive_entity_span` refuses a link whose entity flows in the file (over its window's addresses) differ from the row's finalized `received`/`sent`, for every link the file covers: `reserve_dated::d22_r2_a_trusted_flows_file_must_agree_with_the_finalized_flows` (fails with the check removed: the forged chain is accepted). Residual: the file's split of one entity's flows between its addresses (RES-13, TODO D11) |
| D22-R2-2 | Low (review D22-R2) | `FlowsFile::check_consistent` did not check one block per height: a repeated block under a trusted hash (summary kept consistent, every block on the headers) counts its flows twice | FIXED: blocks must be contiguous, as `flows_from_jsonl` reads them: `d22_r2_a_trusted_flows_file_must_agree_with_the_finalized_flows` (fails with the check removed) |
| D22-R2-3 | Low (review D22-R2, DoS, claim) | `Limits::max_listed` was called a memory bound, but `link_requests` takes a `Value` the caller already parsed: an operator's huge body costs the client its memory before the cap is read | FIXED: `client::parse_served` refuses a body over `max_listed` times `MAX_LISTED_ENTRY_BYTES` (256) plus 1 KiB before parsing: `client_dated::d22_r2_the_served_body_is_bounded_before_it_is_parsed` (fails with the check removed). A client that parses the body itself bounds it itself |
| D22-R2-4 | Info (review D22-R2, cost, self-inflicted) | `link_requests` does not check that the client's own pinned flows file covers what the span needs (a membership change inside it, or an exit or entry anchor): a client pinned without the file, or with a short one, pays for the span before `derive_entity_span` refuses it. The operator cannot cause it | TODO D11 (with the flows residual: the list check asks `Balances::covers` for the span's anchor and changes before the first fetch) |

## M7 loop 3: delivery hardening (2026-10-13)

Branch `m7-loop3`. ADR-0023 Amendment 2, ADR-0033 Amendment 6, ADR-0034 RESAPI-R2 note. Items
fixed in their rows: M7-F5 residual, IDX-R5-3, REVLOG-R13-4, IDX-R6-1..3, RESAPI-R2-1/2. The
trusted forwarded-for item of PLAN "M7 loop 3" was already closed by M7-L48-F2 (loop 50). New
rows for what this loop added:

| ID | Severity | Threat | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| M7-L3-1 | Low (by design) | The settle check serves a request on a transfer proven at the node's latest block; a reorg of that block could undo it, as it could undo a facilitator's success | DOCUMENTED (delivery.md Assumptions, ADR-0023 Amendment 2): the same trust as a facilitator success; its receipt takes the same `credit` path (total-capped) as any facilitator receipt. Tests: `tests::a_timed_out_settle_that_landed_is_served_from_the_token` |
| M7-L3-2 | Medium (guarded) | Re-sending a timed-out settle could charge twice, or serve unpaid | MITIGATED: only the same signed authorization is re-sent (EIP-3009: one nonce moves money once), at most once, only while `validBefore` outlives another settle; a request is served only on a facilitator success or the token's logs. `tests::a_re_send_racing_the_first_settle_charges_once_and_serves` (first settle lands during the re-send: one transfer, served), `a_used_elsewhere_or_unread_authorization_is_never_served` |
| M7-L3-3 | Low (operator) | A settle task now runs up to two settles, two checks and the 2 s re-check wait (50 s with the defaults; 48 s before M7L3-R1-1): a stop waits longer | MITIGATED: `ApiState::settle_task_budget` is in `stop_budget`, and `onyx-node` drains for it; the default (66 s with slack) stays under the shipped 75 s supervisor stop: onyx-node `the_supervisor_stop_timeout_covers_the_checked_facilitator_settle` |
| M7-L3-4 | Low (client) | The default client check trusts the client's own node; a client pointed at the operator's node (or a public node the operator controls) gains nothing | DOCUMENTED (delivery.md "Verification", Assumptions): use a node you trust; the result says which chain and contract were read. TODO (M8): an optional second node in `ClientNode`, refusing on disagreement |

| ID | Severity | Threat | Status |
|---|---|---|---|

The payer was charged with no data and had to sign a new authorization (a second charge) | FIXED: (a) the check after a re-send waits `ApiConfig::settle_recheck_wait` (2 s, at most the check budget; in the stop budget, 66 s < 75 s); (b) a re-send refused as used has that check read the token's logs even when the node reads unused, and every check re-reads a use not found (or a node error) within its budget; (c) the identical retry (same header, resource, client) of an open intent skips verify and settle and runs the check (`IntentLog::adopt`), served only on a proven transfer of the exact value into OnyxRevenue. | SOAK-1 | Medium (money) | Self-settle runs no authorization check on the identical retry (`checks_unknown_settles` is facilitator-only): after a settle that landed but whose answer was lost, the payer's identical retry got 409 `payment_in_use` "already being settled for another request; this request added no charge". A client that believes it signs a new authorization and pays twice for one row. Measured before the fix (20-min trial): 69 identical retries got that 409; 2 of 1,163 authorizations used on chain were never served | FIXED: the identical retry of an open intent gets 503 `payment_pending` with `Retry-After: 30`, never a new settle, and is served from the resolver's proof once the transfer is proven (M7L3-R2-1). Tests (fail with the fix reverted): `tests::soak_1_the_identical_retry_of_an_unknown_self_settle_is_told_to_retry`, `tests::soak_1_a_self_crediting_facilitator_tells_the_identical_retry_to_wait` (credits on settle, review NB1). A retry racing the resolver between its proof and intent reads gets one error and is served on the next retry (no money effect; report "Review notes"). Residual: a client that stops retrying before the resolver's proof (or after its 10-minute window) is charged and not served (the M7-F5 semantics; the fee is credited, `paidButNotServed` in the report) |
| SOAK-2 | Medium (availability) | One node error at start stopped the start (exit 1): `ChainRoots::connect`, registry floors, level-2 pins and OnyxRevenue's code check had no retry. Behind a node failing about 27% of calls, 60 starts in a row failed over 10.6 minutes (run 1) | FIXED: `onyx_node::app::startup_step`, each start-up read tried 8 times with 0.5-8 s waits (about 31 s); a lasting failure still stops the start. Tests: `crates/onyx-node/tests/startup_retry.rs` (`soak_2_a_failed_node_read_at_start_is_tried_again` fails with one try) |
| SOAK-3 | Low (memory) | Settled responses (and every TTL cache) dropped expired entries only on a read or when the 65,536-entry / 256 MiB budget pushed them out, so a steady paid load kept every answered body long past its 10-minute life: onyx-node RSS grew from 7.8 to 39.9 MB over its first 60 minutes (run 1) | FIXED: `Lru::insert` drops expired entries from the least recently used end. Test: `cache::tests::soak_3_expired_entries_are_dropped_on_insert` (1,001 entries kept without the fix, 1 with it) |
| SOAK-4 | Medium (availability) | The deploy-block check (IDX-R1-4) read state at `deployBlock` on every start, so a node keeping only recent state (anvil after about 4,800 blocks here; a pruned full node after 128) could never restart onyx-node once the deployment was older: onyx-node-btc failed 44 starts in a row over 64 minutes in run 2, 29 of them with faults off | FIXED: a passed check is recorded in the bound indexer state file (`deployChecked`) and later starts skip it. Test: `indexer::tests::soak_4_a_restart_does_not_need_the_deploy_blocks_state_again` (also: the head-vs-`deployBlock` check still runs when the record is reused, review NB3). Residual: the first start (or one with a new state file) still needs a node with state from `deployBlock` (documented, IDX-R1-4) |
| SOAK-5 | Low (API) | A metric query whose `as_of` is older than every served shard answers 404 `unknown_metric`, though the metric exists (seen on every soak `as_of` before the first soak round finalized); a client may read it as a wrong metric name | FIXED (E9, 2026-10-16): a known metric asked at an `as_of` older than every shard answers 404 `no_shard_at_as_of`, naming the oldest `as_of`, before any 402; an unknown metric stays `unknown_metric`; a metric whose oldest shard this server refuses (fallback rights, test labels, restricted data) keeps that 403 or 451 at any `as_of` (E10 review). Tests: `onyx-api` `tests::an_as_of_older_than_every_shard_has_its_own_code`, `tests::the_fallback_403_cannot_be_skipped` (`as_of=99`). Residual: a `min_as_of` that filters every shard out still answers `unknown_metric` |
| SOAK-6 | Info (memory) | With SOAK-3 fixed, onyx-node's RSS still rose about 5 MiB an hour in run 2 (19.7 to 23.5 MiB medians, minutes 15-120: inside the 25% tolerance); it may be the allocator settling or a slow growth only a longer run shows | OPEN: TODO (L5 or G6): a 12-hour run of `scripts/soak.sh` with `--leak-window-minutes 720` |
| SOAK-7 | Info (coverage) | Not exercised by the soak: chain reorgs (anvil does not reorg), a real Base node (load-balanced backends, real rate limits), two paying processes behind one OnyxRevenue reporter key (onyx-node-btc carried unpaid traffic only), load above about 3 requests and 0.6 paid settles a second, and the tree merged with main at `407f83b` (contract and driver changes since `a363257`; run 4 on it was lost to a session restart) | OPEN: TODO E9 rerun `scripts/soak.sh` on main after merge; report "Coverage and limits"; reorgs are covered by unit tests only (indexer, resolver) |

## Fresh-machine install L7 (2026-10-15)

Report: docs/audit/2026-10-15-fresh-install.md. The shipped systemd unit installed on a fresh
Ubuntu 26.04 (systemd 259 as PID 1) by docs/ops/deployment.md alone, and both images built with
BuildKit.

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L7-SD-1 | Operator error / availability | Medium | systemd hands every `LoadCredential=` file as root-owned mode 0440 (an ACL for the service's user) in its own credentials directory; the server refused any key or `ONYX_RPC_URL_FILE` group can read, so the shipped unit could not start with its operator key (self-settle, facilitator with reporter) or the `rpc-url` credential (`ExecStartPre` exit 2: "must not be readable by group or others (mode 440)") | A regular file (not a symlink) directly in `$CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY` is accepted when the file is root:root with mode 0440 or tighter (no group write, nothing for others) and the directory is root:root and closed to others: exactly what systemd writes. Any other owner or group, a symlink, or an open directory falls back to the 0600 rule, so pointing `CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY` at a group-shared directory (e.g. `/etc/onyx` root:onyx 0750 with a root:onyx 0440 key, by hand or from an `EnvironmentFile=`) gains nothing (L7 review) | FIXED: `config::tests::credential_rule_accepts_only_root_owned_files_in_a_root_owned_closed_directory` (owner, group, dir owner, dir group, modes), `config::tests::credential_candidates_are_regular_files_directly_in_the_directory` (symlink in the directory pointing outside, file elsewhere, 0600 anywhere); checked under systemd 259: a real `LoadCredential=` file (`-r--r-----+ 0 0`, directory 550 0:0) passes, and `CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY=/etc/onyx` (root:onyx 0750) with a root:onyx 0440 file is refused (`must not be readable by group or others (mode 440)`) |
| L7-BK-1 | Supply chain | Low | The Dockerfile's `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1` line is a moving tag: BuildKit pulls and runs that frontend to parse the file, so the digest pins on `FROM` (OPS-7) did not fix the whole build | Syntax line pinned by digest; `scripts/check-boundaries.sh` refuses an unpinned `# syntax=` in any tracked Dockerfile (negative control: removing the digest gives exit 1) | FIXED: `scripts/check-boundaries.sh` syntax guard; BuildKit build with the pinned line in the L7 report |

## TLS front L11 (2026-10-15)

Report: docs/audit/2026-10-15-tls-front.md. Caddy 2.11.7 with `deploy/caddy/Caddyfile` in front
of onyx-node on loopback, `tls internal`, checked with curl from distinct loopback addresses.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TLS-1 | Griefer | Low | `request_body max_size` alone did not refuse a 2 KiB body: onyx-node answers a GET without reading its body, so Caddy returned that answer before reading past the cap (only a 1 MiB body got 413) | FIXED: `request_buffers 4KiB` reads the body before dialing; 1,025 bytes and more now get 413 (audit section 5); `caddyfile::limits_fit_the_server` requires `request_buffers` above `max_size` |
| TLS-2 | Griefer (connection exhaustion) | Low / Medium | onyx-node exempts its trusted proxy from `ONYX_MAX_CONNS_PER_IP` (AUD-1R-F1) and stock Caddy has no per-client connection cap, so one client can open many TLS connections to the proxy (Caddy's 10 s header and 60 s idle timeouts bound each); the file serves HTTP/1.1 only (TLS-8), so a connection cap also caps requests in flight | OPEN, Needs the project owner (the host, LC-8): on the chosen box the loop adds a host-firewall cap of new connections per source address on 443 (deployment.md "TLS in front"; launch checklist LC-9) |
| TLS-3 | Griefer (slowloris on port 80) | Low | Caddy's automatic HTTP->HTTPS redirect server did not take the global `servers` options (default timeouts, HTTP/3 on) | FIXED: the redirect is an explicit `http://` site block, so both servers get the 10 s header timeout and the header cap (`caddy adapt`, audit "Found and fixed"); `caddyfile::every_api_route_is_proxied_and_nothing_else` requires the block |
| TLS-4 | None (honest payer refused) | Low | Caddy's default header cap is 16 KiB for all headers, below one full `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` (`x402::MAX_PAYMENT_HEADER`, 16 KiB) plus the rest: a large valid payment would get 431 | FIXED: `max_header_size 32KiB`; a 16 KiB payment header passes (audit section 5); `caddyfile::limits_fit_the_server` |
| TLS-5 | Careless operator | Medium | `ONYX_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP_PUBLIC=1` with a port published on every interface (`docker run -p 8080:8080`) serves plain HTTP to the network | ACCEPTED: the opt-in is explicit, the server prints a warning naming the address at every start and in `--check-config`, and deployment.md "Run with Docker" says to pair it only with `-p 127.0.0.1:...`; the container cannot see how its port is published |
| TLS-6 | Local process on the host | Low | With `ONYX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1` any process on the host can connect to onyx-node directly and pick its rate-limit key with `X-Forwarded-For` | ACCEPTED: processes on the API host are the operator's own (the operator key and state sit there too); remote clients reach only Caddy, which drops their `X-Forwarded-For` (audit section 6) |
| TLS-7 | Griefer (review) | Medium | In Docker, Caddy's connections reach onyx-node from the bridge gateway (`::ffff:172.17.0.1`), not 127.0.0.1: with the documented `ONYX_TRUSTED_PROXIES=127.0.0.1` the forwarded header is ignored, all clients share one rate-limit bucket and the proxy hits `ONYX_MAX_CONNS_PER_IP` | FIXED docs-only: docs/ops/deployment.md ("TLS in front": in Docker, trust the bridge gateway address, with the command to read it, and check two clients get separate limits); the Caddyfile header says the same |
| TLS-8 | Griefer (review) | Low | Caddy's own error responses (413, 502) skipped the deferred `header` handler: no HSTS, no nosniff, `server: Caddy`; and HTTP/2's 250 streams per connection made a per-address connection cap no bound on requests in flight | FIXED: `handle_errors` sets the same headers; `protocols h1` (HTTP/1.1 only); `caddyfile::tls_hsts_and_loopback_upstream` requires both. The 431 comes from Go's HTTP server before any handler and stays bare |

## Registry pin in the node export L16 (2026-10-16)

`--export-node` now pins `OnyxRegistry`, so a node started from the export serves each shard at
the level the chain attested (THREATS L2R2-F2; ADR-0030 amendment L16). Adversarial pass on the
pin: can a wrong registry or swapped code slip through?

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L16-1 | Deployment integrity | Medium | The export read `registryCodeHash` from the chain at the broadcast's address (trust on first use): a proxy, or other bytecode there, would be pinned as it is and its implementation could change later | The export compares the runtime code with this checkout's forge `deployedBytecode`, only the immutable ranges (`owner`, `ledger`) masked, and refuses a different length or byte before writing the pin | FIXED: `only_the_registry_build_is_pinned` |
| L16-2 | Operator error / tampered manifest | Medium | The node checked only `keccak(code) == registryCodeHash`: a manifest naming another deployment's registry (its own owner and ledger, so its own attestations) together with that registry's matching hash was trusted | `levels::check_registry` also requires `ledger()` to be the manifest's `settlement` (whose code hash is pinned too); a contract with a matching hash that is not such a registry fails the call; the start stops after its tries; errors name no node URL | FIXED: `levels::tests::a_registry_bound_to_another_settlement_is_refused`; `scripts/docker-smoke.sh` step 4 (wrong hash; settlement as registry) |
| L16-3 | Wrong chain | Low | Identical registry bytecode at the same address on another chain (CREATE addresses repeat across chains for the same deployer and nonce) carries other attestations | The manifest's `chainId` is checked against the node's `eth_chainId` before the registry is read (the settlement step, same node client), and the ledger binding ties the registry to the pinned settlement | FIXED: `chains_follow_the_environment`; the chain check is the settlement step's (ACCEPTED for a node that lies about its chain id: the operator's node is trusted, as for every root) |
| L16-4 | Code swap after start | Low | The registry's code is checked once at start; the indexer reads `levelOf` later at `latest` | ACCEPTED: OnyxRegistry has no `delegatecall` or `selfdestruct` and is not a proxy (L16-1 pins the build), so its code cannot change after deploy; a restart checks again |
| L16-5 | Trust in the registry owner | Low | With the pin, a labelled shard's level is raised from the fail-closed 5 to the attested level, which rests on the owner-registered label set level | ACCEPTED: this is ADR-0030's existing trust (the owner is never the coordinator, REG-R1-F3); the chain's level never lifts a shard above a catalog input level or a supplied label level; owner key hardening is ROADMAP H1 |

Adversarial review of the L16 branch (2026-10-16, fresh reviewer; hardest on the level stand-in).
Level order checked: 1 (Recomputed) is strongest, 5 (TrackRecord) weakest, `weakest` takes the
higher number. Pricing never reads the level; the money effect is only `/v1/settlement` (L16-R4).

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L16-R1 | Level ordering | Medium | `attest` built on the current level: for a labelled shard with no supplied label level, a second, stronger attestation reset it to the input floor (attested 4, then 1: served at 1), and a label level supplied after an attestation lifted it above the chain's (attested 5, then label 1: served at 1). No path does either today (the start floors a fresh clone once per try; the indexer attests once per admission), but "never above an input level" held only by call order | `ShardMeta` keeps `attested_level` (the weakest attestation) and recomputes `proof_level` from its inputs on every setter: input floor, the label level (supplied, else the attested level standing in, else 5), the attested level. Order-independent; an attestation never lifts a shard above an input floor, a supplied label level or another attestation | FIXED: `catalog::tests::the_level_never_beats_an_input_in_any_order` (every sequence of up to three inputs, labelled and not, 7,232 cases) |
| L16-R2 | Lying view / encoding drift | Low | The stand-in trusted the attestation at (round, shard) for the label set's level without comparing the attestation's `recipe` and `labelSetHash` with the catalog's binding. The chain recomputes the shard id from both, so this needed the Rust and Solidity shard id encodings to drift apart, but then an attestation for another label set's level would rate this one | `registry_level` treats an attestation whose metric, recipe or label set is not the binding's as none (level 5) | FIXED: `levels::tests::an_attestation_for_another_label_set_or_recipe_is_none`; `scripts/docker-smoke.sh` step 4 shows the real chain's attestations still match (both shards at the attested level) |
| L16-R3 | Process | Low | The export's build check (L16-1) ran only `if let Some(--registry-broadcast)`: the registry address comes only from the broadcast today, but a later source of it would have pinned unchecked code silently | `registry_artifact` refuses a registry with no broadcast ("not pinned") | FIXED: `only_the_registry_build_is_pinned` |
| L16-R4 | Market (money) | Medium | UNPLANNED SEMANTIC CHANGE: before L16 a labelled catalog-file shard on onyx-node was always level 5, so `/v1/settlement` always answered 409 for it. Under the pin it takes the attested level, which the registry bounds by the owner-registered label set level. The money default accepts 1 and 3: today's label sets are registered at 4 (409 unchanged), but a label set the owner registers at 3 makes onyx-node settle markets on those shards | ACCEPTED as the intended L16 effect, with the lead to confirm before any label set is registered at 3: it is ADR-0030's trust in the owner's `registerLabelSet` (serve-api already trusts the operator's reviewed `label_set_proof_level` the same way), the chain's level only stands in for the unknown label level and never beats an input floor (L16-R1), pricing and `/v1/proofs` do not read the level; owner key hardening is H1; `catalog::tests::a_labelled_shard_settles_money_only_at_an_attested_accepted_level` |
| L16-R5 | Stale level | Low | The node reads `levelOf` once (at start, or when the indexer admits a shard). A recipe floor the owner raises later (`registerMetricMinLevel`, REG-F-F1) weakens `levelOf` on chain, but the node keeps serving the stronger level until it restarts; with L16 this now covers labelled shards too (attested level instead of 5) | ACCEPTED for testnets: the owner raising a floor restarts the nodes it runs (the restart reads `levelOf` again, as in the stop-serving-shard runbook); a periodic re-read is part of owner key hardening, TODO H1 |
| L16-R6 | Rights fallback (L14) | Low | `/v1/health` `shardLevels` counted every catalog shard, including the label-derived ones `ONYX_RIGHTS=fallback` refuses with 403: the counts reveal nothing new (indexer health lists every shard, each shard answer carries its level), but "served per level" was wrong in fallback | `shardLevels` counts only shards the server serves; `shardsWithheld` counts the fallback-withheld ones (0 when cleared). docker-smoke runs cleared (it sells the test label set's reserve row), so the fallback count is unit-tested only | FIXED: `fallback_rights_withhold_label_derived_shards_before_any_payment` |
| L16-R7 | Process (merge of L15) | Medium | Since L15 (a1b189c) onyx-node refuses an operator key that is not `OnyxRevenue.reporter()`, but `scripts/docker-smoke.sh` still mounted anvil's dev key 0 while the fork run makes a fresh operator key the reporter: both servers exited at start ("/v1/health answered 000"), so the Docker gate failed on main and hid every later step, including L16's | The smoke keeps the run's keys (`ONYX_DEMO_KEYS`) and mounts the run's `operator.key` (the reporter); no impersonation, the real setReporter path stays tested | FIXED: `scripts/docker-smoke.sh` (DOCKER SMOKE PASSED on 9dd6842) |

## History secret scan L13 (2026-10-15)

Report: docs/audit/2026-10-16-history-secret-scan.md. gitleaks 8.30.1 and trufflehog 3.97.9
(verification off) over all 428 commits on all refs, 18 unreachable commits and main's tree;
the repository's own patterns via `scripts/check-secrets.sh --history`; every distinct 64-hex
string derived as a private key against the 161 addresses in history. No value is written here.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SCAN-1 | Careless contributor | Low | The tree scan's allowlist entry for anvil's account 0 key (`ALLOW_RE`, since `bc1733f`) had one wrong hex digit: it allowlisted an unrelated 64-hex value and not anvil's key | FIXED: corrected from `cast wallet private-key --mnemonic "test ... junk"`; `scripts/check-secrets.sh --self-test` (in check-all) derives the key the same way and fails when `ALLOW_RE` does not start with it. The mistyped value stays in `bc1733f` (no rewrite); `--history` lists it as reviewed by full commit:file:line (`HISTORY_ALLOW_AT`), not by value |
| SCAN-2 | Data thief | Info | A private key held in a bare `KEY`/`key` constant (`const KEY: &str = "<64 hex>"`) is invisible to gitleaks' default rules, trufflehog and the repository's 5 patterns; only the derivation check found the one in `crates/onyx-api/src/evm_tx.rs` (`a3904a5` onward), which controls `0x34bf…5219` | ACCEPTED: that key is public by construction (sha256 of the phrase in its own comment; recomputed) and its address has nonce 0 and balance 0 on Base Sepolia (2026-10-15); a broader `key` pattern would flag the 8 public hashes in fixtures; the derivation check is rerun with gitleaks before any public push (docs/audit/2026-10-16-history-secret-scan.md) |
| SCAN-3 | Data thief (repository made public or mirrored) | Medium | Real credentials in history: the testnet deployer key, the CDP API key id/secret, RPC provider keys in URLs | OPEN (Needs the project owner): none found. Deployer: its address `0x80c9…7972` appears in history and none of 26,595 distinct 64-hex strings (reachable and unreachable commits) derives to it; no `.env*`, `*.key`, `*.pem`, `.onyx-testnet/` or keystore file was ever added, so no rotation. CDP and RPC: only placeholders (`9cccc2b`, `3ca12ec`, `bc1733f`, `51ac9b5`, `285efff`). Left: the counts-only cross-check of the real `.env` values against history (the loop never reads `.env`), run by the lead or the project owner with the command in the report; a non-zero deployer count means a new testnet deployer (lead/the project owner, never the loop). Rewrite-or-keep-private stays LC-26 / L8-H1..H3 |
| SCAN-4 | Data thief (review 2026-10-16) | Medium | A secret added only in a merge commit (a conflict resolution or an extra edit in the merge) was invisible to `--history` and to gitleaks: `git log -p` prints no patch for merges. Shown with a planted fake value in a throwaway clone | FIXED: `--history` reads merges with `--remerge-diff`, gitleaks runs with `--diff-merges=first-parent`; `check-secrets.sh --self-test` (check-all) plants a key in a merge resolution and requires both to report it. Rescan with merges: 0 new. Trufflehog and the derivation check did not cover merge-only lines; due with the pre-push rescan |
| SCAN-5 | Careless operator (review 2026-10-16) | Medium | `--history` exited 0 when gitleaks was not installed ("skipped") or exited 0 without writing its report, so a pre-push run could pass with half the scan missing | FIXED: `gitleaks_scan` fails on a missing binary, a non-zero exit or a missing report; `scripts/check-secrets.sh --self-test` (check-all) runs each case with a stand-in binary (`ONYX_GITLEAKS`) |

whole fallback public build, every node route in fallback, the switch's default, main's W12 merged.

Shipped: a label-derived share ("its proof-of-reserves file covers 99.8% of OKX's labelled value") and a per-entity count ("3,558 addresses also in Onyx's signed OKX set"). The guard only matched values found in the committed outputs (satoshis, 8-decimal BTC, leaves), so a share, a rounded total or a sum passed | FIXED: `apps/web/vite.config.ts` marks Svelte's template calls pure, so dead-branch text leaves the bundle (0 hits for both strings after); guard rule 4 (`entity_figures`) refuses any percentage, BTC/sat/₿ amount or 2+ place decimal within 100 bytes of a label-set company's name, whatever its value, in every encoding; run on the author's bundle it refuses `99.8%`. Tests: `public_build::the_fallback_guard_refuses_label_derived_totals` (plants share, rounded, ₿, short decimal, base64; passes heights, statuses, micro-USDC, Binance Pool), `public_build::a_fallback_build_carries_no_label_derived_totals` (run by the build). ## Level 5 track record C1 (2026-10-17, ADR-0036)

Design threats for `crates/onyx-track` (per-(source, metric) history against later level 1-3
answers). Tests are in `crates/onyx-track/src/tests.rs`.

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TR-1 | Copying, herding | High | A record scored on agreement with other sources rewards copying the crowd, and a colluding majority could make an honest source look wrong | Outcomes compare a statement only with a resolution at an accepted level; other sources are context only ("best of N", first to agree) | FIXED: `onyx_track::tests::peers_never_change_an_outcome` |
| TR-2 | Whitewashing | Medium | A source with a bad record re-registers under a new name and starts clean or better | No record starts above empty; a rate is shown only past 30 resolved over 5 subjects; sources are registry-reviewed `SourceId`s, so a new name is a new review | FIXED: `onyx_track::tests::a_new_source_starts_with_nothing` (the review itself is the registry's) |
| TR-3 | Cheating source (hedging) | High | State several values for one fact and keep the right one | Any second statement with another value or confidence makes the entry `Equivocated`, a confident miss (Brier 1), even when one value is right and even when the second comes late | FIXED: `onyx_track::tests::equivocation_is_a_confident_miss`, `onyx_track::tests::an_identical_restatement_is_one_statement` |
| TR-4 | Framing by weak answers | Medium | A level-4 claim, another level-5 value or a colluding level-2 majority "resolves" a fact against an honest source | Resolver levels are a subset of 1-3, default 1 and 3 (the money default's levels); 4 and 5 are refused in params, level 2 only when named | FIXED: `onyx_track::tests::only_levels_one_to_three_resolve` |
| TR-5 | Dishonest coordinator | Medium | Resolutions are caller input: omitting the one that shows a favoured source wrong leaves its fact `Unresolved`; a forged agreeing resolution with an early `public_from` turns a miss into `Void`, a contradicting one makes it `Contested` | Resolutions are append-only and a new one must be public after the previous commitment (TR-R1-1). C7 (ADR-0036 amendment 3): with `TrackParams.chain` set the resolution list is never an input: `chain::derive_resolutions` reads it from `OnyxSignedBook` settleable reports and `OnyxRegistry` observations at the commitment's finalized head, for every stated fact, and every client reruns it from its own node (`verify_resolutions`: an omission, a forgery or an addition is `Mismatch`, an on-chain answer without its preimage `Withheld`; `verify_chain` walks the log from its first entry, each at its own head, so an omission or forgery in an earlier commitment is found too); level 1 is refused, fail closed (TR-C7-7). Without `chain` (tests, the example) resolutions stay caller input | FIXED (chain mode): `onyx_track::chain::tests::an_omitted_or_forged_resolution_fails_the_client_check`, `onyx_track::chain::tests::a_recorded_observation_resolves_only_through_its_preimage`, `onyx_track::chain::tests::a_level2_preimage_must_be_the_registered_templates`, `onyx_track::chain::tests::an_omission_in_the_previous_commitment_is_caught_by_the_chain_walk`, `onyx_track::chain::tests::a_statement_is_resolved_by_the_books_settled_report`; on anvil `scripts/track-onchain-anvil.sh` |
| TR-6 | Dishonest coordinator, impersonation | Medium | Statements and their `committed_at` are caller input: a statement added under a source it never made, or dated earlier within the current period, before the truth | C5 (ADR-0036 amendment 1): a statement enters only signed by an active registered key of its own source (EIP-191, the level-3 key); `committed_at` is the timestamp of the finalized block carrying its batch's post, rechecked by the client's `verify_log` from its own chain reads; `check_extends` still refuses a statement new to a commitment that was revealable at the previous `as_of` | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_statement_enters_only_under_the_sources_registered_key`, `onyx_track::intake::tests::committed_at_is_the_post_block_time_never_the_callers`, `onyx_track::tests::history_cannot_be_rewritten`, `scripts/track-intake-anvil.sh` (local anvil: a backdated log refused) |
| TR-7 | Copier | Medium | A source copies another's published statement before the close and gets the same agreement count | Statements are sealed until `max(committed_at, close)`: only the batch root (over rows that include the unpredictable signature) is public before; a log revealing one early fails `verify_log`; `agreed_first` still credits only the earliest agreeing commit. A coordinator that leaks sealed rows is TR-I-11 | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::sealed_statements_stay_hidden_until_their_close`, `onyx_track::tests::a_copier_is_never_first`, `scripts/track-intake-anvil.sh` (commitment 1 reveals nothing before the closes) |
| TR-8 | Sybil | Medium | Many names each guess differently; by luck one looks perfect and is shown alone | Every record carries `metric_sources` ("one of N sources on this metric") and `metric_resolved_facts`, checked against the committed metric summary (TR-R1-5); below the threshold no rate is shown; names are registry-reviewed | FIXED (the crowd is shown, not prevented; names are registry-reviewed): `onyx_track::tests::sybil_guessers_show_as_best_of_n`, `onyx_track::tests::a_hidden_crowd_is_caught_by_the_metric_summary`; C6 prints "one of N sources on this metric" on every record (`track_view::tests::the_site_example_checks_and_shows_counts_by_the_rules`) |
| TR-9 | Dishonest server | High | The server commits an inflated record (misses moved to agreed) over honest entries | `verify_history` recounts the record from its proven entries (strictly ascending fact keys), with the neighbours outside its range proven, so a short, padded or duplicated range fails. It proves the record adds up over committed entries, not that each entry's outcome is right (that needs a rerun of `compute`, TR-R1-6) | PARTIAL: `onyx_track::tests::an_inflated_record_fails_the_recount`, `onyx_track::tests::a_client_verifies_a_record_and_its_history`, `onyx_track::tests::a_padded_history_is_refused`; C6: the browser runs `verify_history` (`track_view::tests::a_tampered_or_stale_example_file_shows_nothing`); C20: a client with the registry reruns `compute` on the served logs (`onyx_track::wire_log::tests::a_record_the_logs_do_not_give_is_refused_by_the_rerun`); TODO C23: the registry served so every client can rerun, C22 for logs with priced answers. P7 2026-10-18 (launch walk, LC-14): testnet launch accepted: the node and the coordinator are operator-run and a record drives no reward, serving or level (`onyx_track::tests::a_perfect_record_never_changes_a_level`). |
| TR-10 | History rewriting | High | A later commitment drops an old miss, edits a statement, or removes a resolution | `check_extends`: chained `prev`, later `as_of`, logs and params match their hashes, params keep every rule, every earlier statement and resolution kept unchanged, no re-resolved fact and no withheld resolution (TR-R1-1, TR-R1-2) | FIXED: `onyx_track::tests::history_cannot_be_rewritten`, `onyx_track::tests::an_appended_resolution_cannot_erase_a_miss`, `onyx_track::tests::params_cannot_change_a_committed_rule` |
| TR-11 | Market (money) | High | A good record is used to raise a level-5 value's level or to settle a money market (L16-R4 rule) | `onyx-track` returns no `ProofLevel` or `MarketPolicy`; a level-5 value stays level 5; the money default stays 1 and 3; check-boundaries refuses a file that uses `onyx_track` with level or market-policy code | FIXED: `onyx_track::tests::a_perfect_record_never_changes_a_level`, `scripts/check-boundaries.sh` (TR-11 fence) |
| TR-12 | Cheating source (selection) | Medium | State only easy facts (stable subjects, quiet days) to collect agreement, as R-SCORE-2 for labels | Records are per metric, never one blended score; each shows `metric_resolved_facts` so coverage is visible; the threshold needs 5 distinct subjects | FIXED (visible, C9): `onyx_track::tests::sybil_guessers_show_as_best_of_n` (coverage counts); C6 shows coverage and "one of N" beside every record (`track_view::tests::the_site_example_checks_and_shows_counts_by_the_rules`); C9: skill against persistence beside every established rate (`onyx_track::tests::skill_is_measured_against_the_last_known_value`): easy facts inside a metric, where the last known value already agrees, add nothing to it |
| TR-13 | Lookahead | Medium | The truth is public elsewhere before the metric's close (R-SCORE-1 for data): a fast copier states it on time | `Void` when the resolution's own `public_from` is at or before the close; every registered metric reviewed against its earliest publication anywhere (docs/spec/proof-ladder.md "Close-time rules"): only the example level-3 metric gets a rule today; the intake refuses a statement past its close (`PastClose`) and chain time makes `Late` trustworthy | PARTIAL: `onyx_track::tests::void_when_the_truth_was_public_before_the_close`, `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_statement_after_the_close_is_refused_or_late`; C9 (ADR-0036 amendment 4 item 1): `Close::PeriodStart`, the Bitcoin flow rule closes 7,200 s before the UTC day its fact totals (no block whose median time past is in the day is accepted earlier): `onyx_track::tests::a_period_fact_closes_before_its_period_starts`, `onyx_track::tests::a_period_fact_must_name_a_whole_period`; left: mempool inputs (TR-C9-1) and an entity stating on itself (TR-C9-2, TODO C92) |
| TR-14 | Rule gaming | Low | A wide tolerance makes every source agree | Tolerance is a reviewed per-metric rule pinned in the committed params hash; 0 for `Bool` and `Bytes`; at most `MAX_TOLERANCE` | FIXED: `onyx_track::tests::tolerance_applies_to_numbers_only` |

Fresh adversarial review TR-R1 of the C1 branch (2026-10-17; 7 PoC tests, all reproduced before
the fixes; 3 merge blockers, all fixed on the branch before merge).

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TR-R1-1 | Dishonest coordinator | High | A later commitment appended a contradicting resolution (fact becomes `Contested`) or an early agreeing copy (`Void`) for a fact already resolved, and `check_extends` accepted it: a committed miss vanished | `check_extends` refuses a new resolution for a fact the earlier log had resolved, and one public at or before the earlier `as_of` (withheld); a later contradiction waits for a dispute path | FIXED: `onyx_track::tests::an_appended_resolution_cannot_erase_a_miss`; the dispute path is TODO C7 |
| TR-R1-2 | Dishonest coordinator | High | `check_extends` never compared params: a wider tolerance in the next commitment turned an old miss into `Agreed` | `check_extends` takes both params, checks their hashes, and requires the later params to keep the resolver levels and every rule (rules may only be added for new metrics) | FIXED: `onyx_track::tests::params_cannot_change_a_committed_rule` |
| TR-R1-3 | Cheating source | Medium | Junk values at confidence 0 scored a perfect Brier (disagreed, `p^2 = 0`), and an established record ranked above an honest one | Confidence is `MIN_CONFIDENCE_PPM` (500,000) to 1,000,000: a statement claims its value is more likely right than not; rankings put the agreement count first | FIXED: `onyx_track::tests::a_statement_below_even_odds_is_refused` |
| TR-R1-4 | Liveness | Medium | `compute` refuses an old statement whose source, metric, rule or subject is no longer admissible, and the log may not drop it, so a registry removal would leave no valid next commitment | `StaticRegistry` has no removal and refuses duplicate sources, so rights cannot change; the spec states the registry only grows. Key revocation (C5) removes no source: a revoked key's statements stay admissible | TODO C90 (C9 left it, ADR-0036 amendment 4 item 4): retirements pinned in the params, a `Retired` outcome, the same exemption in key books and `verify_log`, before any registry removal path exists (none exists today, so nothing halts) |
| TR-R1-5 | Dishonest server | Medium | `metric_sources` and `metric_resolved_facts` were the record's own word: a server could show "1 source" and hide the Sybil crowd | A third tree of `MetricSummary` rows in the commitment; `verify_history` requires the record's numbers to equal its metric's committed summary. ## Level 5 track-record intake C5 (2026-10-17, ADR-0036 amendment 1): adversarial pass

Self-noted while building `onyx_track::intake` and `onyx_coordinator::track_chain` (back-dated
statements, statements after the answer, key rotation and revocation, replays, floods). Tests are in
`crates/onyx-track/src/intake_tests.rs`; the local-chain run is `scripts/track-intake-anvil.sh`.

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TR-I-1 | Impersonation | High | The coordinator, another source or anyone adds a statement under a source (a forged miss, or a hit it never made) | Only an EIP-191 signature by an active key of the payload's own source in the batch's key book admits it; every key in a book must be a reviewed level-3 `SourceKey` (TR-R3-2); the key id is the level-3 `SourceKey` id; a value edited after signing, a non-canonical signature, another source's key or an unknown key are refused, at the intake and again by `verify_log` | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_statement_enters_only_under_the_sources_registered_key`, `onyx_track::intake::tests::the_key_id_is_the_level3_key_id`, `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_key_outside_the_level3_registry_is_refused`; that the level-3 review itself is honest (provenance at the source's origin) is the level-3 lane's assumption (ADR-0028) |
| TR-I-2 | Back-dating | High | The coordinator (or a colluding source) dates a statement before the truth was known | `committed_at` is the finalized block time of the batch's post, never a parameter; the client recomputes it from its own reads; earlier or later times fail `verify_log` | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::committed_at_is_the_post_block_time_never_the_callers`, `scripts/track-intake-anvil.sh` |
| TR-I-3 | Hedging by hidden posts | High | Post several batch roots (one per value) and reveal only the one that turns out right | Headers chain by `seq` and `prev`; every post's transaction must be the dedicated poster's next nonce to the sink carrying exactly the header hash; the poster's nonce at the head must equal the posts shown, so one hidden post fails every read | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_hidden_post_is_caught`, `onyx_coordinator::track_chain::tests::a_post_is_the_posters_next_transaction_carrying_the_header`, `scripts/track-intake-anvil.sh` (a hedge from the poster refused) |
| TR-I-4 | Key revocation as an eraser | High | A source with a bad run declares its key compromised from an earlier time to erase its misses | Key books only move forward and take effect at the next batch's block; statements in final batches stand and are checked against their own batch's book; a book that drops or un-revokes a key is refused; one signer, one source | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::keys_rotate_forward_and_never_retroactively`, `scripts/track-intake-anvil.sh` (revoked key refused after rotation) |
| TR-I-5 | Flooding, dilution | Medium | A source floods statements to bloat the log or to dilute its misses with easy agreements | Pending cap per source per batch (4,096) and per batch (65,536); one entry per (source, fact); unresolved facts count nothing; a second value is a confident miss; a rate needs 30 resolved over 5 subjects, with coverage and "one of N" committed. Easy facts inside a metric still dilute, visible only as coverage | FIXED (C9, q-TR-5 decided): every established record on a period metric shows its skill against persistence (the last value known at each close), which easy facts cannot raise: repeating the known value scores 0 (they can pull a negative skill toward 0; the counts A_s and A_b are shown beside it, TR-C9-R1-6): `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_flood_is_capped_and_cannot_dilute_a_miss`, `onyx_track::tests::skill_is_measured_against_the_last_known_value`; gaming it: TR-C9-5..9 |
| TR-I-6 | Censoring coordinator | Medium | The coordinator delays a statement's post past its close so it turns `Late`, or never posts it | It cannot backdate, only delay. C9 (ADR-0036 amendment 4 item 5): the intake signs a receipt with a posting deadline at or before the close, as the poster account every payload's intake id names; `check_receipt` shows kept (provable before the reveal with the intake's inclusion proof), posted late, or broken, signed by the poster: a delay or a drop is attributable. A receipt never sets a commit time | PARTIAL: `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_kept_receipt_is_provable_before_the_reveal`, `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_broken_receipt_is_attributable`, `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_receipt_is_the_posters_for_this_statement`; a refusal to issue a receipt at all stays unprovable (TR-C9-12); TODO C91: broken receipts served beside the record |
| TR-I-7 | Replay | Medium | A statement replayed later (to add a duplicate or a second commit time), into another deployment, or carried twice in one forged batch | Payload binds the intake id (chain id, sink, poster, first nonce) and key; a payload digest is taken once over the intake's life; `verify_log` refuses a digest twice | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::replayed_statements_are_refused`, `scripts/track-intake-anvil.sh` |
| TR-I-8 | Selective reveal | Medium | The coordinator reveals a statement before its close (helping a copier) or withholds a revealed one (hiding a miss) | `verify_log` refuses a statement revealed before `max(committed_at, close)`; a batch holds one close only, so past `max(post time, close)` a batch with any row missing is refused (TR-R3-1); a row withheld anyway can never enter a later commitment (`check_extends`: Backdated) | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::sealed_statements_stay_hidden_until_their_close`, `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_withheld_reveal_is_caught`, `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_far_reveal_by_cannot_hide_a_hedge` |
| TR-I-9 | Stolen key | Medium | A thief signs statements under a source until the revocation reaches a batch | Revocation is effective from the next batch; the thief's earlier statements count against the source, like any use of its key; undoing them would reopen TR-I-4 | ACCEPTED: by design the key holder answers for its key; the level-3 registry's compromise path revokes it in the next book (ADR-0036 amendment 1 item 5) |
| TR-I-10 | Sequencer clock | Low | On an OP stack (Base) the sequencer sets block timestamps, within `max_sequencer_drift` (1,800 s) of its L1 origin, so a colluding sequencer could shift `committed_at` | The drift is bounded by the protocol, and closes are reviewed per metric in hours or days; a rule with a close window under the drift would be refused at review | ACCEPTED: the chain's clock is the trust root C5 asks for; a close shorter than `max_sequencer_drift` is not ruled (docs/spec/proof-ladder.md "Close-time rules") |
| TR-I-11 | Leaking coordinator | Medium | The coordinator hands sealed statements to a copier before their close | Only the coordinator holds sealed rows; the copier still is not `agreed_first`; leaks are not detectable. C50's drand/tlock fits: a leaf encrypted to the quicknet round at the batch's close (ADR-0036 amendment 4 item 5) | TODO C93 (after C51): rows encrypted to the round at their close, so the coordinator cannot read them early either |
| TR-I-12 | Equal block times | Low | A chain whose consecutive blocks can share a timestamp (a local anvil mining in one second) could carry a post after the head with the head's time; it would enter the next commitment as backdated if its close had passed | The spec assumes strictly increasing block times (Ethereum slots, OP Stack +2 s per block); the intake refuses a statement whose close passed before submission, so this needs a close inside the same second | ACCEPTED: local anvil only; Base blocks are 2 s apart |

Fresh adversarial review TR-R3 of the C5 branch (2026-10-17; code read only, every finding
checked against the code; 2 merge blockers, fixed before the first commit).

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Merge-blocking | `seal` takes one close per batch and `verify_log` requires every revealed statement's close to equal `reveal_by`, so completeness applies at each statement's own close | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_far_reveal_by_cannot_hide_a_hedge` (mutations "old reveal_by rule" and "seal all closes together" each fail it) |
| TR-R3-2 | Dishonest coordinator (impersonation) | High | The key book was only shape-checked: the coordinator could add its own key for a victim source and sign statements under its name. Merge-blocking | `KeyBook::validate(reg, reviewed)` requires every key to be a reviewed level-3 `SourceKey` of the same source and signer; the intake and `verify_log` both take the reviewed set | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_key_outside_the_level3_registry_is_refused` |
| TR-R3-3 | Dishonest coordinator (two intakes) | Medium | Nothing bound a commitment chain to one intake: two posters could each carry a hedge and the coordinator publish whichever chain won; a client running only `check_extends` accepted statements backdated inside an open window | `TrackParams.intake` pins the intake id; `extends` requires it equal, `submit` and `verify_log` refuse other params; the spec makes `verify_log` mandatory when it is set | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::the_params_pin_the_intake` |
| TR-R3-4 | Client robustness | Low | `CastRecord` never compared the node's chain id with the intake's and allowed a pinned depth on any RPC, so a client pointed at a fork could be fed made-up block times | `check_head_source`: chain id must match; a pinned depth only on a loopback RPC | FIXED: `onyx_coordinator::track_chain::tests::a_head_is_read_only_from_the_intakes_chain` |
| TR-R3-5 | Cost | Low | `submit` counted a source's pending statements by a linear scan (about 2 x 10^9 compares for a full batch) | Per-source counter, recounted on seal and key changes; the replay set grows with the intake's life by design (a digest is taken once, ever) | FIXED: `onyx_track::intake::tests::a_flood_is_capped_and_cannot_dilute_a_miss` (cap behaviour unchanged) |
| TR-R3-6 | Reviewer (holding) | Info | Checked and holding: replay blocked at intake and client with the intake id in the payload; canonical signatures only; poster-nonce count catches a hidden post; keys forward only and revocation never retroactive; leaves include the signature; `EarlyReveal` enforced and two revealed values score `Equivocated`; Borsh, Keccak, sorted rows, no floats; no panic or unchecked overflow on untrusted input in `verify_log` or `seal`; the fence covers every onyx-track source file and anything naming `track_chain` | ACCEPTED: no change needed beyond TR-R3-1..5 |

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |

| B2-2 | Process with write access to the spool | Low | On one host every observer writes into folders the coordinator's user owns, so any process of that user can overwrite another observer's file before the coordinator reads it: never a forged answer (signatures), but that observer's reveal is lost (a non-reveal, never slashed; a split may cost one of the fact's 3 draws) | PARTIAL (Needs the project owner): each observer writes only its own folder in a real deployment (its SSH key limited by a forced command to its own folder, ADR-0027 amendment 9 item 9; a separate OS or SFTP account does not work with the enforced modes, B2-R2-3, TODO B6); the rehearsal shares one user. The observer's posted commit and missing receipt show the loss (B2-3). docs-only: docs/adr/0027-proof-ladder-level-2.md |
| B2-3 | Coordinator | Medium | A coordinator drops an honest observer's reveal from the spool (or never reads it): the chain cannot tell, since no receipt was signed, so the round settles without it (REVLOG-1 through the new transport) | PARTIAL: the observer process waits for its receipt on chain and exits 3 without one, naming its posted commit as evidence (`examples/level2-observer.rs`); `b2_observers::b2_a_coordinator_that_drops_a_reveal_leaves_the_observer_without_a_receipt`. Provable with encrypted on-chain reveals, built in C4 (`sealed_reveals::c4_a_dropped_sealed_post_is_caught_where_a_dropped_spool_reveal_is_not`); C11 2026-10-17: the observer process posts them when the draw has a reveal key (`examples/level2-observer.rs`, rehearsed by `scripts/level2-sealed.sh`), and a dropped post fails every client (`c11_sealed::c11_2_a_skipped_slot_is_caught_before_anything_is_kept`); OPEN for spool observers (draws without a reveal key) until C12 closes the early view and level 2 runs sealed only |

## Level 5 track records served and shown C6 (2026-10-17, ADR-0036 amendment 2): adversarial pass

`/v1/track` (`onyx_api::track_serve`), the served form and its client check (`onyx_track::wire`),
the browser check (`apps/web/verify/src/track_view.rs`) and the Data page's section. No real
record exists today (no metric has a close-time rule); the site shows the labelled example.

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TR-S-1 | Dishonest server (rollback, fork) | Medium | The server publishes an older computation, the same one again, or a log that drops a statement, and serves it as its latest | `TrackStore::publish` appends a commitment only if `check_extends` holds against the published one (chained, later, params and every earlier statement and resolution kept) | FIXED: `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::the_store_never_goes_back` |
| TR-S-2 | Dishonest server (history truncation) | High | A served history drops, reorders or repeats entries, hides the neighbour just outside the range, or leaves out the history of a small record, to hide misses | The client runs `verify_history` on every body; `history` may be `null` only past `MAX_HISTORY` (1,024) entries, and then the client says the history was not checked | FIXED: `onyx_track::wire::tests::a_truncated_or_padded_history_is_refused`, e2e "C6 track records: a cut history fails the check and nothing is shown" |
| TR-S-3 | Proof forgery | High | Better counts in the record, a miss turned into an agreement in one entry, or a summary with fewer sources ("best of 1") | Rows travel as Borsh under Merkle proofs against the commitment; the record is recounted from its entries; the summary must match the record's two context numbers | FIXED: `onyx_track::wire::tests::forged_counts_and_outcomes_are_refused` |
| TR-S-4 | Dishonest server (substitution) | Medium | A valid record of another source or metric is served for the one asked | The body's ids and the record row's ids must equal what the client asked | FIXED: `onyx_track::wire::tests::another_record_is_refused` |
| TR-S-5 | Mislabelled example | Medium | The invented example shown as a real record, or a real record passed off as the example | The `example` flag must equal whether an id is an example id; a node's store refuses example ids; the site's check needs the flag and the pinned example commitment | FIXED: `onyx_track::wire::tests::the_example_flag_must_match_the_ids`, `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::a_node_store_refuses_example_ids`, e2e "C6 track records: an example record relabelled as real fails the check" |
| TR-S-6 | Malformed body | Low | A commitment that does not hash to `commitmentHash`, an `asOf` or params that differ, an extra key the client cannot check, uppercase hex, another level | Strict shape: exact keys, lowercase `0x` hex, Borsh with no trailing bytes, `params_hash` and the hash recomputed | FIXED: `onyx_track::wire::tests::a_mismatched_commitment_or_shape_is_refused` |
| TR-S-7 | Data thief (rights) | Medium | In `ONYX_RIGHTS=fallback`, records on label-derived metrics are served, or their existence probed through 404 versus 200 | 403 `label_rights_withheld` before any lookup for a metric the registry marks as needing a label set, with an `entity` name segment, or unregistered (fail closed); the index leaves them out and counts them | FIXED: `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::fallback_withholds_label_derived_records` |
| TR-S-8 | Made-up record | High | The API or the site shows a track record nobody stated, while no source states on a ruled metric (C9: the Bitcoin flows have the first rule; none is scored) | The API serves only published books (none on a node today: 404 `no_track_record` with its reason); the site says there is no real record and why, and shows only the labelled example | FIXED: `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::nothing_published_is_a_stable_404_and_an_empty_index`, e2e "C6 track records: the section says no real record exists and why", e2e "C6 track records: the example checks out and every card is labelled example" |
| TR-S-9 | Fence bypass (level, money) | High | onyx-api's pricing, payment or settlement path, or the node, reads a record once onyx-api depends on onyx-track | Only `track_serve` (and its tests) in onyx-api and `track_view` in the verifier name track code; each lib.rs names its module only as `pub mod`; `router_with` takes the routes as an opaque `Router`; the node's app.rs names track code on one line only, `onyx_api::track_serve::empty_routes(..)` (no data in, only a Router out); cargo-metadata dependents listed. Eight plants refused 2026-10-17 after review TR-S-R1 (lib.rs import, catalog naming track_serve, a level word in track_serve, app.rs reading a track store beside payment code, app.rs naming onyx_track, another node file mounting the routes, a re-export in the verifier's lib.rs, a macro) | FIXED: `scripts/check-boundaries.sh` (TR-S-9 fence) |
| TR-S-10 | Cost (free bodies) | Low | Free history bodies (up to 1,024 entries with proofs) requested in a loop to load the server | Per-client budget of 30 answers a minute (IPv6 by prefix), a 304 on a matching ETag costs nothing, the guard's concurrency limit and deadline apply | FIXED: `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::free_answers_are_limited_per_client`, `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::the_routes_join_the_api_behind_its_guard` |
| TR-S-11 | Misleading display | Medium | A rate shown below the threshold, a value called "verified", or one blended score | The verifier returns a rate and mean Brier only for an established record; the page shows counts and the threshold otherwise, per (source, metric), and never says verified or proven | FIXED: `track_view::tests::the_site_example_checks_and_shows_counts_by_the_rules`, e2e "C6 track records: the established example shows a rate, the other shows counts and the threshold only", e2e "C6 track records: the words verified and proven do not appear in the section", e2e "C6 track records: the headline counts match the checked history" |
| TR-S-12 | Stale data file on the site | Medium | The site's example file replaced by the older (honestly computed) commitment, whose proofs all check | The browser verifier pins the example's latest commitment and uses its `as_of` as the floor | FIXED: `track_view::tests::a_tampered_or_stale_example_file_shows_nothing` |
| TR-S-13 | Unchecked inputs | Medium | A client checks that a record adds up over its committed entries, not that each outcome is right: the logs are not served, so nobody outside the server can rerun `compute` or `verify_log` | Stated in the spec and ADR amendment 2; every outcome names its resolution hash | PARTIAL: C20 serves the logs and the intake (`GET /v1/track/log`) and `check_log_body` reruns `compute` with the client's registry and `verify_log` with its reviewed keys: `onyx_track::wire_log::tests::a_record_the_logs_do_not_give_is_refused_by_the_rerun`, `onyx_track::intake::tests::the_published_intake_gives_the_served_log`, `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::the_logs_are_served_and_rerun`, `track_view::tests::the_example_logs_rerun_in_the_browser`; TODO C22: logs holding level-1/2 answers are not served (403 `track_log_priced`), so those records cannot be rerun; TODO C23: the registry a rerun needs is not served |
| TR-S-14 | Dishonest server (fork after a known commitment) | Medium | A server drops committed statements, recomputes, and chains the new commitment to the one a client knows: the hash chain and `as_of` rise, every proof checks | The client's `known` check is documented as hash descent only; the server's own store refuses the rewrite (`check_extends`, TR-S-1). C7: a fork after a known commitment cannot be the latest (one chain on chain, `check_latest`); the coordinator can still post a rewrite as the next entry, which is then public and attributable to its poster | FIXED for a client that asks the logs with `since` (C20): every served commitment's log must hash to it and extend the one before, so a rewrite chained to the known commitment is refused however the logs are laid out: `onyx_track::wire_log::tests::a_rewrite_chained_to_the_known_commitment_is_refused`, `onyx_track::wire::tests::a_fork_chained_to_the_known_commitment_passes_the_hash_chain_only` (the record body alone still passes, as documented), `OnyxSignedBookTrack.t.sol::test_AForkOrAReplayIsRefused`; residual: logs not served for priced tracks, TODO C22 |

## Track-record logs, publication path, pages and `since` C20 (2026-10-18, ADR-0036 amendment 5): adversarial pass

`GET /v1/track/log` and `/v1/track/{source}/{metric}/history` (`onyx_api::track_serve`), the
publication (`onyx_track::publication`), the client checks (`onyx_track::wire::{check_log_body,
check_history_page, complete_history}`), the node's `ONYX_TRACK_PUBLICATIONS`, the coordinator's
`write_publication`, and the browser's remembered commitment (`apps/web/src/lib/trackSeen.ts`).

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Mitigation | Status |

| TR-C20-2 | Dishonest coordinator or operator (rewritten file) | High | The publication file is replaced by one that drops, reorders or truncates what the node served (a quiet rollback or a rewritten history), or by a file that does not check | The node serves a file only if `Publication::check` passes (a chain from a zero `prev`, each log hashing to its commitment and extending the one before, the rows giving the latest) and it `starts_with` what was served; the head it served is kept in `ONYX_STATE_DIR` so a restart cannot reset that floor (review C20-R1-1); otherwise the track routes answer 503 `track_store_unreadable` until fixed (the node keeps serving everything else). The coordinator's `write_publication` refuses the same and writes whole files by rename | FIXED: `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::a_node_serves_the_coordinators_publication_file`, `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::a_restart_never_goes_behind_what_was_served`, `onyx_coordinator::track_chain::tests::a_publication_is_written_whole_and_only_forward`, `onyx_track::publication::tests::a_tampered_publication_is_refused`, `onyx_track::publication::tests::a_later_file_must_start_with_the_earlier_one`; residual: losing `ONYX_STATE_DIR` loses the floor (as for the receipt journals) |
| TR-C20-3 | Data thief (rights) | Medium | In `ONYX_RIGHTS=fallback` the logs give label-derived values (entity flows) that the records route withholds | The log is 403 `label_rights_withheld` when any ruled metric is withheld; a node has no registry, so with a file every ruled metric counts as label-derived (fail closed) | FIXED: `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::fallback_withholds_the_logs_of_a_label_derived_track`, `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::a_file_served_track_is_withheld_in_fallback` |
| TR-C20-4 | Dishonest coordinator (rows not from the logs) | High | A commitment whose rows were computed from other answers than the logs it commits to (a miss turned into an agreement): its rows, hashes and every proof check, and the node, which has no registry, serves it | A client with the registry reruns `compute` on the served logs and must get the commitment again (`Recompute`); a registry with another root is said so (`RegistryDiffers`), never passed | PARTIAL: `onyx_track::wire_log::tests::a_record_the_logs_do_not_give_is_refused_by_the_rerun`, `onyx_track::wire_log::tests::served_logs_rerun_to_the_commitment`; C23 (2026-10-18): the registry a commitment names is served (`GET /v1/track/registry`) and every client, the browser included, rebuilds it and checks its root before the rerun: `onyx-api::track_serve::tests::whole_logs_rerun_with_the_served_registry_and_have_no_pages`, `track_view::tests::the_rerun_uses_the_served_registry_only_when_it_hashes_to_the_root`; TODO C24: the website has no live node yet (LC-8), so the browser reruns only the example. P7 2026-10-18 (launch walk, LC-14): testnet launch accepted: the node and the coordinator are operator-run and a record drives no reward, serving or level (`onyx_track::tests::a_perfect_record_never_changes_a_level`). |

| TR-C20-R1-2 | Cost (reload on the runtime) | Medium | A reload (read up to 256 MB, decode, recheck every step, steps times rows) ran under a mutex on the async workers, stalling the paid routes on the same runtime | Reload on the blocking pool before each track handler; the publication is checked outside the store's lock; after the first load only the new steps (`check_after`); each step's log grown from the one before; at most 65,536 steps | FIXED: `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::a_node_serves_the_coordinators_publication_file`, `onyx_track::publication::tests::a_publication_carries_the_example_chain_and_checks` |

| TR-C20-R2-3 | Cost (runtime stall) | Medium | Each handler's `serving()` re-read the file on the async worker under the mutex a running reload held, so a request arriving while a large file was checked parked a runtime worker (paid routes share the runtime) until the check ended, and every request queued a blocking task on the same mutex | One read at a time on the blocking pool (`try_lock`); a request never reads the file and never waits: it is answered from the last finished read (the publication it left stays served meanwhile) | FIXED: `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::a_request_never_waits_on_a_running_read` (times out when the reload waits on the lock) |
| TR-C20-R2-4 | Cost (page built before the budget) | Low | `GET .../history` built a page (up to 1,024 entries with proofs) before charging the client's budget, so a client past its budget still made the server build pages | The bound is checked first (cheap), then the budget, then the page is built | FIXED: `onyx_api::track_serve::tests::a_history_page_is_built_only_within_the_budget` (pins the order of the answers; the saved work itself is not observable in a test) |

| TR-C20-R2-6 | Rights and pricing (C22 judged) | Info | The 403 `track_log_priced` is stricter than the paid API: a level-1 row or level-2 result is free once past its metric's fresh window (docs/spec/pricing.md), and a metric without a policy is free, while the log stays 403 forever; the only ruled real metrics (Bitcoin entity flows) resolve at level 1, so no real record can be rerun | Kept (fail closed, nothing given away; the track routes are fenced from pricing code). ROADMAP C22 names the consistent rule: free once every priced answer's `public_from` plus its metric's fresh window has passed (`public_from` is no earlier than the API's clock start, so never free earlier than the API), windows passed to the store as plain data; decision in docs/TRACKER.md | ACCEPTED: TODO C22 |
| TR-C20-R2-7 | Reviewer (holding) | Info | Checked and holding: a log forked after the `since` commitment (counts in a link are not committed, but every link's log must hash to it, so its row set is fixed, and `check_extends` keeps it); links served before the known commitment must chain to it; a history assembled from pages of another commitment, shifted, cut, reordered or with a page dropped fails `check_history_page` or `complete_history`; a remembered commitment the since file lacks shows nothing (`unknown`); the record and history routes carry only resolution hashes and level numbers, never a value or a level-1/2 evidence hash, so no priced value is enumerable from them; the public and fallback sites ship only the example's invented level-3 log; with a file every ruled metric is withheld in fallback, so neighbour entries of withheld records are never served there; a file not written by the coordinator is served when it checks and extends the kept head (the node reads no chain), and a client pinning the on-chain `trackHead` refuses any commitment never posted (TR-R2-5; the browser reads no chain yet, C41); a crash between the coordinator's write and rename leaves the old file (the node reads only the renamed path); a file rolled back together with the state directory is the documented residual (TR-C20-2), and a client asking `since` the newer commitment gets 409 `unknown_commitment`; `since`, `at`, `from` refuse non-canonical forms and huge values; the index is unbudgeted and walks every record per page (behind the guard's concurrency limit; empty today) | ACCEPTED: holding as checked |

Log format 2 (`onyx_track::chained`), the second publication layout, `GET /v1/track/log` pages and

check_registry_body}`), `onyx_core::RegistryData` and the browser's `check_track_log_paged`.
Self-noted while building, against a lying server, a griefing coordinator and a data thief.

## Sealed reveals and attempt records (ROADMAP C4, 2026-10-17): adversarial pass

ADR-0027 amendment 10. Self-noted while building (C4-1..C4-9: a coordinator dropping or falsely
dismissing sealed posts, an observer posting garbage or copying another's ephemeral key, early
and late posts, replay, early decryption, a sealed round listing a withheld reveal), then a
fresh adversarial reviewer (C4-R1-*, 2026-10-17: 1 High fixed before merge (the ephemeral-key
"proof" was an ECDSA signature, a decryption oracle), 2 Medium (1 fixed, 1 partial with client
checks in C11), 2 Low, 3 Info), then a second fresh reviewer on the fixes (C4-R2-*: the Schnorr
fix holds; 1 Medium fixed (ciphertext length leaked the answer's length), 1 Low, 3 Info), then a
third fresh reviewer with a cryptography focus (C4-R3-*: construction sound; 2 Low fixed (an
untested load-bearing on-curve check; a dismissal of a post read from a lying node was a key
oracle, now the key proof is kept and re-checked), 2 Info).

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C4-1 | Coordinator | Medium | Drops a sealed reveal post (to steer the value or force `NoResult` and a re-draw), the REVLOG-1 move through the new channel | FIXED for posts in (`commit_close`, `reveal_close`]: `revealLogComplete` is false when such a post has status 0, `recordAttempt` reverts `IncompleteTranscript`: `sealed_reveals::c4_a_dropped_sealed_post_is_caught_where_a_dropped_spool_reveal_is_not`, `OnyxRegistrySealedReveals.t.sol::test_ADroppedSealedPostFailsTheLogAndTheRecord`, `invariant_SealedPostsAndRecordsAreWriteOnce`.
