| C4-2 | Coordinator | Medium | Dismisses a VALID post as garbage to drop it | FIXED: a dismissal carries `S` and a Chaum-Pedersen proof that `S = k·R`; the proof fixes the decryption, and a client refuses a dismissal whose plaintext is a valid reveal (`FalseDismissal`), a made-up `S` or a tampered proof (`BadProof`): `sealed_reveals::c4_garbage_is_dismissed_with_a_checkable_proof_and_a_valid_post_never_is`, `sealed::tests::dismissal_proofs_check_and_bind_their_context`. On chain status 2 needs an in-phase post and no receipt (`OnyxRegistrySealedReveals.t.sol::test_AReceiptedRevealIsNeverDismissed`); the proof itself is checked by clients, Rust and web (C11: `c11_sealed::c11_3_a_replayed_or_false_dismissal_is_refused`, `sealed_reveals::c11_the_page_refuses_a_section_that_is_not_the_rounds`) |

Break-the-code: dropping the re-check fails it. C11 2026-10-17: the coordinator reads `sealedKeyProofOf` with `sealedRevealOf` at one block and refuses a post whose proof fails before opening anything (`c11_sealed::c11_a_post_whose_key_proof_fails_is_never_opened`) |

The `z >= n` refusal in `keyProofValid` is an equivalent mutant under real inputs (`z + n` fits in 256 bits only for `z < 2^256 − n`, about 2^-128; `z = n` fails anyway), so no test can kill it; kept as a guard |

window and round id. Self-noted while building, on the four moves the milestone names

After merging main (C11 sealed reveals; STATUS and THREATS conflicts kept both sides). Each finding
reproduced by a failing test before the fix. Break-the-code: 8 mutations (level-3 and level-2
answers not yet usable at the head taken, the level-1 refusal removed, the operator check skipped,
an older `as_of`, a fork and a declaration after the first key accepted by the book, a commitment
head above the finalized head read), each caught.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Mitigation | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TR-C7-R2-1 | Nobody (registry growth) | Medium | With level 1 accepted (the default levels), a stated fact of a metric the registry registers as a recipe after it was committed (the level-5 use: early statements, the level-1 answer later) made every later derivation `Level1Unsupported`: the whole record halted, every source and metric | Chain mode refuses params accepting level 1 before the first commitment (no level-1 reader exists, so nothing is lost); a later recipe registration changes nothing | FIXED: `onyx_track::chain::tests::a_metric_registered_as_a_recipe_later_does_not_halt_the_chain` (red before the fix), `onyx_track::chain::tests::level1_is_refused_until_a_reader_exists` |
| TR-C7-R2-2 | Level-3 source (griefing) | Medium | A registered source signs a report on any stated fact and relays it through a contract: `Settled.report` is `None`, the coordinator has no reader for the bytes (no call traces), so every derivation is `Withheld` and the record halts until the preimage is found | Fail closed is right (skipping relayed reports would let a front-running relayer hide an honest answer); the bytes are in the internal call to `postReport`, so a tracing node recovers them | TODO C40: the coordinator recovers relayed reports from `debug_traceTransaction` |
| TR-C7-R2-3 | Lying or lagging node | Low | Three finality guards had no test: a level-3 fact shown before its dispute window ended, a level-2 observation shown before it was recorded, and a commitment head above the finalized head (`at_commitment`); removing any of them passed every test | Tests for each | FIXED: `onyx_track::chain::tests::an_answer_not_yet_usable_at_the_head_is_refused`; on anvil `scripts/track-onchain-anvil.sh` ("a commitment head that is not final") |
| TR-C7-R2-4 | Reviewer (second pass) | Info | Checked and holding: `postTrackCommitment` appends only to `msg.sender`'s log, only the successor of its latest with a rising `as_of` not past the block time, so a fork, a replay, an older commitment or another poster's spam cannot enter a pinned log, and two posts with one `prev` cannot both land; clients read `trackHead` at a finalized block (`CommitmentLogCast::head` takes the block from its caller: pass the finalized one). `declareOperator` is the C2 book's immutable `reviewer`, refused once a source has a key (`originOfSource` is never cleared), and a stating source must have a book key, so no statement predates its operator. Level-2 preimages are bound by domain-tagged Keccak over Borsh (self-delimiting; Keccak has no length extension; the result-hash mirror equals the coordinator's). The fence and gas snapshot pass after the merge; the anvil script binds `--port 0`, traps cleanup and stops its anvil | ACCEPTED: no change needed beyond TR-C7-R2-1..3 |

reader chose, a forged rehearsal record, the rehearsal taken for live data) and on its monitoring
(the 600 s breaker tripping unseen). Money: unchanged (the check settles nothing; ROADMAP H6).

## Ethereum adapter and chain statistics P4a (2026-10-19, ADR-0044): adversarial pass

Adversarial pass by the implementer: a cheating miner (rows not from the blocks), a lying RPC (a
fabricated chain, fabricated execution), a griefing block source, a JSON-only attacker on the
website, a data thief and privacy (free text in a shipped block input), a lying endpoint at fetch,
a protocol fork, rights, fuel, and test honesty. A fresh review is in the table after this one.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ETH-1 | Cheating miner | High | Commits Ethereum statistics that are not the blocks' (fees, counts, a row for another block), or feeds validators a source that is not the chain's bytes | FIXED (after review P4A-R1-1): the recipe hashes every header to its block hash, links each to its parent, rebuilds the transactions and receipts trie roots, and requires the source's first and last numbers and last hash to be the ones the shard's params pin (`EthStatsParams`, set from the snapshot by `params_for`; `spec_binds_snapshot`), so given the pinned tip the rows are those blocks' or the run fails; whether the pinned tip is Ethereum's is ETH-2. `eth_chain_stats::tests::a_broken_block_fails_with_its_code`, `golden_eth_chain::a_snapshot_naming_other_blocks_fails_the_run`, `golden_eth_chain::committed_mainnet_blocks_rerun_to_the_window_leaves` |
| ETH-2 | Lying RPC (a fabricated chain) | High | Post-merge blocks carry no proof of work: one endpoint can serve a self-consistent invented chain (hashes, parents and roots all right) | PARTIAL: the fetch stays at or below the endpoint's finalized block and a second operator must return the same hashes for the window's parent, first, every 50th and last block; by the hash chain the last hash fixes every block before it (`scripts/refresh-eth-onchain-tests.py`). TODO P4d: a beacon light-client check (sync-committee BLS signatures over the finalized header, the blst code onyx-tlock already reviewed) in the adapter and the browser |
| ETH-3 | Lying RPC (execution) | Medium | Serves receipts whose status or gas are not the result of running the transactions | ACCEPTED: receipts are bound to the header by its receipts root (`golden_eth_chain::edited_answers_are_refused`), so changing them needs a fabricated header (ETH-2); re-execution is a full node's job, and a validator with its own node sees a content-hash mismatch |
| ETH-4 | Griefing block source | Medium | A source that breaks block rules (a fee below the base fee, a fee cap below its priority cap, receipts of another type, gas that falls or overruns a transaction's limit, blobs that do not add up, a gas limit jump, a wrong base fee, non-canonical RLP) to make runs disagree or panic | FIXED: each is a recipe error code, never a row (receipt type, flat or falling cumulative gas, a last total that is not the header's, gas above the limit and malformed envelopes tested since review P4A-R1-5); `eth_chain_stats::tests::sealed_blocks_that_break_a_rule_fail_with_its_code`, `decode::tests::malformed_transactions_and_receipts_are_refused`, `rlp::tests::non_canonical_forms_are_refused`, `decode::tests::base_fee_follows_eip_1559`, `trie::tests::known_answers_from_ethereum_tests` |
| ETH-5 | JSON-only attacker on the website | Medium | Edits the window file: a field of a row, a row moved to another number, a time, a dropped, duplicated, swapped or undecodable leaf, a renamed or added day, the range or the recipe id | FIXED: the verifier rebuilds the commitment from the leaves and requires the pinned range, tip and recipe; nothing is drawn unless it passes. `eth_chain::every_json_only_edit_of_the_window_fails`, e2e "forged eth: the window does not check out" |
| ETH-6 | Data thief, privacy | Medium | The website ships one block's full recipe input; calldata, logs and the header's extra data can carry free text (messages, contact details written into the chain), and unlike Bitcoin's OP_RETURN (CHAIN-4) they cannot be trimmed, since the trie roots cover every byte | ACCEPTED with mitigations: the page never decodes or prints the input (it ships as base64 for the engine only); the exporter picks the smallest qualifying block whose bytes hold no e-mail-like text or profile link (`personal_text`, block 26,225,368: 72 KB, its readable runs are a builder tag, a pool symbol and a price-feed label); the public-build guard scans every shipped file, base64 decoded, for e-mails and profile links (`public_build::the_guard_refuses_emails_and_profile_links`) |

## Time-lock layer for sealed reveals (ROADMAP C12, 2026-10-17): adversarial pass

ADR-0027 amendment 12. Dependency review first (RESEARCH.md "Time-lock crates"): no tlock crate is
acceptable, so the layer is designed and its composition tested with a MOCK beacon
(`onyx_coordinator::timelock`); nothing ships and nothing calls it. Self-noted on the five moves
C12 names (early decryption, drand round substitution, wrong chain, a beacon that never
arrives, malleability across the two layers) and what the gas test found; then a fresh
adversarial reviewer (C12-R1-*, read-only: 0 High, 2 Medium (1 fixed, 1 re-rated to C53), 5 Low
(4 fixed, 1 to C50), 2 Info fixed); then a second fresh reviewer, cryptography (C12-R2-*: 0 High, 0 Medium;
1 Low to C31; crate claims, gas method and C50/C53 wording corrected).

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C12-1 | Coordinator with colluding observers | Medium | Early decryption (C4-7 through the new layer): the coordinator opens a time-locked post before the lock round, with its reveal key alone, amendment 10's path, or an earlier round's signature that is already out | PARTIAL: in the composition nothing opens without the lock round's signature (`BeaconMissing`), the ECDH key alone decrypts to garbage, an earlier round's signature is `BadBeacon` and does not open the time-lock: `timelock::tests::c12_1_the_coordinator_opens_nothing_before_the_lock_round`. With the real scheme (C50) and published quicknet signatures: `timelock::tests::c50_a_real_time_locked_post_opens_only_with_its_rounds_published_signature`. C51 2026-10-17: wired; the runner opens only after the lock round's signature verifies (`c51_timelocked::c51_without_the_lock_round_the_round_waits_and_a_late_beacon_loses_nothing`, THREATS C51-4); clock lag TODO C53 |
| C12-2 | Observer colluding with the coordinator; coordinator | Low | drand round substitution: an observer locks to an earlier round so the coordinator can read it early; a coordinator shows another round's signature, or claims an honest post's time-lock does not open, or makes up an opening, to dismiss it | PARTIAL (composition tested, mock beacon): the lock round is a function of `revealClose` (bound by the attempt record) and is in the key; a post locked to another round does not open and is dismissed, spoiling only its poster's own value; another round's signature is `BadBeacon`; "does not open" for a post that opens is `FalseDismissal`; a made-up opening is `BadOpening`; the true opening of a valid post is `FalseDismissal`: `timelock::tests::c12_2_round_substitution_spoils_only_the_substituters_own_post`. Real scheme (C50): a real Go ciphertext does not open under another published round's signature (`tests::c50_1_round_substitution_opens_nothing`, THREATS C50-1). C51 2026-10-17: wired, the lock round taken from the window the on-chain draw commits to, a post locked to an earlier round dismissed by the live runner and checked by both clients (`c51_timelocked::c51_dismissals_carry_openings_and_every_way_around_the_time_lock_is_dismissed`); the C53 clock rule is the remaining part: TODO C53 |
| C12-3 | Coordinator (beacon key) | Medium | Wrong chain: observers are made to lock to a beacon key the coordinator holds (a key served by the coordinator, read from chain, or a configurable flag), so it opens early | FIXED (C51, 2026-10-17; was PARTIAL): the chain hash, key, genesis and period are constants in code (`QUICKNET_*`), never arguments; the chain hash is in the key; a post locked to another chain is dismissed and that chain's signatures are refused: `timelock::tests::c12_3_a_post_locked_to_another_chain_is_garbage`; the pinned values are checked against api.drand.sh by the opt-in `timelock::tests::c12_live_quicknet_matches_the_pinned_chain`. Real scheme (C50): another chain's key or signature opens nothing, a real quicknet-t ciphertext included (`tests::c50_2_another_chains_key_or_signature_opens_nothing`, `interop::c50_a_quicknet_t_vector_does_not_open_under_quicknet`); with real IBE the chain hash is not in the time-lock (only in `k`), the key is. C50 2026-10-17: Go and tlock-js vectors decrypt and re-encrypt byte for byte on native and wasm32 (`interop::c50_every_fixture_check_passes_with_the_expected_counts`, `scripts/check-tlock-wasm.sh`); `tau` ending in zero bytes only in Onyx-made vectors (THREATS C50-9): a Go cross-check TODO C70 |

## The time-lock scheme (ROADMAP C50, 2026-10-17): adversarial pass

ADR-0027 amendment 13. drand/tlock's IBE for quicknet in `crates/onyx-tlock` on `blst` 0.3.17
(docs/audit/2026-10-17-blst.md), behind `timelock::QuicknetTimeLock`; interop vectors from
drand/tlock (Go) and tlock-js with published drand signatures (`fixtures/tlock`), native and
wasm32. Self-noted by the implementer on the moves C50 names (malformed points, wrong DST, round
substitution, G1/G2 swap, small-subgroup and infinity inputs, re-encryption mismatch) plus
panics, cross-target drift, supply chain and timing. Break-the-code (each mutation run against
`cargo test -p onyx-tlock`): no Fujisaki-Okamoto check, no G1 or G2 subgroup check, blst's GT
byte order, no H3 mask, no signature check in `open`: each caught; dropping our re-compression
(canonical) check survives, since blst already refuses every non-canonical encoding tried (kept
as a second line). Fresh cryptography review: C50-R1 below.

### Review C50-R1 (2026-10-17, fresh reviewer, cryptography)

Read against the Go reference, not the author's notes: kyber v1.3.1 `encrypt/ibe/ibe.go`
(<https://github.com/drand/kyber/blob/v1.3.1/encrypt/ibe/ibe.go>: `EncryptCCAonG2`,
`DecryptCCAonG2`, `h3`, `gtToHash`, `h4`) and drand `crypto/schemes.go`
(<https://github.com/drand/drand/blob/master/crypto/schemes.go>: `bls-unchained-g1-rfc9380` uses
`BLS_SIG_BLS12381G1_XMD:SHA-256_SSWU_RO_NUL_` on G1, key on G2, digest `sha256(round as uint64
big-endian)`). Matches line by line: DST, identity, `U = r·G2`, tags `IBE-H2/H3/H4`, H3's
`i = 1..65534` little-endian counter and one-bit mask, the Fujisaki-Okamoto check before any
plaintext is returned (Go compares points, Onyx compressed bytes of canonical points: the same
here). Every decoded point is `uncompress` + `validate` (infinity and subgroup) + re-compression;
`open` verifies the beacon against the pinned key before decrypting. Break-the-code (run, then
reverted): no FO check, no G2 subgroup check, no G1 subgroup check, the G2 DST, `open` without the
beacon check: each caught by `cargo test -p onyx-tlock`; `QuicknetTimeLock::verify_signature`
always true: caught; `QuicknetTimeLock::open` through the unverified path: SURVIVED (C50-R1-1, now
caught). Verdict: sound for merge as an unwired layer; C4-7 stays open until C51.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C50-R1-1 | Coordinator or client code at wiring (C51) | Low | `QuicknetTimeLock::open`'s own beacon check was untested: every caller verifies first (`beacon_checked`), so `open` rewritten over the public unverified decrypt (was `onyx_tlock::decrypt`) passed every coordinator test. Unverified decryption means nothing for attacker ciphertexts: a poster who picks a G1 point `s'` makes `V = sigma XOR H2(e(s', U))` and the time-lock "opens" under `s'` | FIXED: `timelock::tests::c50_r1_1_quicknet_open_checks_the_signature_itself` (a quicknet-t lock opens under quicknet-t's real signature, never through the pinned layer; break-the-code: the unverified `open` fails it); the function is now `decrypt_unverified` with a warning, and `scripts/check-boundaries.sh` refuses it outside onyx-tlock and the fuzz target |
| C50-R1-2 | Local observer of timing | Info | H3's range test `hashed < GROUP_ORDER` was an array compare that stops at the first differing byte, run on the ACCEPTED candidate, i.e. the secret scalar `r` (which opens the time-lock before the round): it timed whether `r`'s leading bytes equal the order's (about 1 in 128 for the first byte). Negligible bits, but it made C50-11's "leaks only how many outputs were out of range" untrue | FIXED: branch-free borrow compare `lt_be`, `tests::c50_r1_2_the_range_test_is_array_order`; the Go vectors still re-create byte for byte (`interop::c50_every_fixture_check_passes_with_the_expected_counts`). C50-11's accepted residual (loop count) is unchanged |
| C50-R1-3 | Test honesty | Info | Asked: is there any published Go or tlock-js quicknet ciphertext whose file key ends in zero bytes, to confirm the Onyx-made zero-tail vectors? Every armored vector in drand/tlock v1.2.0 `testdata` and `tlock_test.go` and in tlock-js's tests was read as data: besides the three used, all are fastnet (`dbd506d6…`) or testnet `7672797f…` (other schemes); none is quicknet. The Onyx code has no length-dependent path (fixed 16-byte arrays), so the bug class is absent by construction, but it is not confirmed against Go | OPEN: TODO C70 (Go cross-check) |

Adversarial pass by the implementer: a coordinator after an early view (every downgrade path to a
draw that is not time-locked, reading or opening before the lock round, choosing another round),
a lying or failing beacon source (forged, another round's, malformed, missing), griefing
observers (posts around the time-lock), a lying server toward the Rust and web clients, and
rehearsal-only switches on a live chain. Then a fresh review (C51-R1 below).

### ROADMAP E13 (2026-10-19): remote check host

`scripts/remote-check.sh` runs check-all for a worktree on the build machine (approved 2026-10-18), a
shared machine that runs a vendor's production indexing. Implementer's pass: what leaves the dev
box, what the run can do to the host's disk, CPU and memory, and what branch code can reach there
(docs/ops/remote-check.md). A fresh reviewer's pass (2026-10-19) added REMOTE-6..10 and the Landlock
sandbox of REMOTE-4.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| REMOTE-1 | Secret leak (sync) | Medium | The sync copies a worktree to a second machine: an `.env`, a key file, an untracked file holding a key, or a build or `.git` folder could leave the dev box with it | FIXED: the worktree's own secret scan, then the name and content rules over the exact file list (`scripts/check-secrets.sh --paths-from`, untracked files included, symlinks judged by name and copied as links, never followed), a refusal for `target/`, `node_modules/`, `apps/web/build/`, `.onyx-testnet/` and `.git/` paths, and rsync excludes for env and key names as a second layer: `scripts/remote-check.sh` (self-test in check-all: an untracked key, an untracked `deploy.env`, an untracked and a tracked `.key`, a tracked `.env`, tracked `target/` and `node_modules/` files all refused, no value printed; the exact list of a worktree with ignored, deleted and submodule files), `scripts/check-secrets.sh` (its self-test covers `--paths-from`) |
| REMOTE-2 | Disk exhaustion (shared host) | Medium | Cargo targets, the pnpm store and the fixture blocks fill the host's `/`, which the production indexing shares | FIXED: a run is refused under 60 GB free or with `~/onyx-build` plus `~/onyx-tools` over the 80 GB budget; a watchdog stops the job's own scope below 45 GB free or over budget (exit 4); `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`; old duplicate build files are swept after each run; `--clean <branch>` deletes only that branch's two folders: `scripts/remote-check.sh` (self-test: 59 GB free and 81 GB used refused, 60 and 80 allowed; a clean of one branch leaves the other branch, the fixtures and HOME) |
| REMOTE-3 | Resource starvation (shared host) | Medium | A full check-all (builds on 96 threads, three browser runs, anvil chains) starves the production jobs of CPU, memory or I/O, or a stop signal hits a process Onyx did not start | FIXED: refused above a 1-minute load of 60; every run is one systemd user scope with `MemoryMax=48G` and `CPUQuota=4800%` (half the threads), nice 19 and the idle I/O class (limits read back inside a probe scope on the host 2026-10-18: memory.max 51539607552, cpu.max 4800000 100000); the runner stops only its own named scope (dropped ssh session, watchdog): `scripts/remote-check.sh` (self-test: load 60.01 and 61 refused, 60 allowed) |
| REMOTE-4 | Branch code on a shared host | Medium | Everything check-all runs (build scripts, tests, the web build, npm packages) runs as the host's own user: a malicious or buggy branch or dependency could read or change the production work in that user's home | FIXED 2026-10-19 (separate `onyx-build` user plus the sandbox; review 2026-10-19): the job runs under a Landlock file-system sandbox (no root needed): it writes only its branch's source, target and TMPDIR folders, the private HOME and the crate cache, reads only the system folders and Onyx's two folders; the rest of the home, `/mnt`, `/tmp` (the production lock files), other branches, the fixtures, the tools and the runner are out of reach, and `/proc/<pid>/environ` of the host's other processes is denied; the runner refuses to start without Landlock (exit 3). Checked on the host 2026-10-19 (home listing, `.bashrc`, `/mnt/nvme`, `/tmp` and cgroup writes denied; node, cargo, git, DNS and Chrome with and without its own sandbox work inside). systemd's `ProtectHome=`/`BindPaths=` were tried first and are silently ignored in the host's user manager (AppArmor blocks unprivileged user namespaces). Also `env -i`, private HOME and TMPDIR, lockfile-pinned crates and npm packages only. Still open: signals to the same user's processes, Unix-socket connects (the user's systemd and D-Bus buses, PostgreSQL peer authentication) and TCP; closing them needs a separate Unix user (or a container) on the host. FIXED 2026-10-19 (the project owner approved): checks run as the separate `onyx-build` user (no password, no sudo, its own restricted key; the old copy in the project owner's home deleted), so signals, sockets and files of the project owner's processes are out of reach by Unix permissions; TCP stays open (needed for crates and npm). Tests: `scripts/remote-check.sh --self-test` (the job's own rules on a fake base: writes to the branch's folders pass; reading a file outside, listing HOME, writing another branch, the fixtures, a tool, the runner or next to Onyx's folders all fail) |
| REMOTE-5 | Test honesty (portability) | Low | Found by the first remote run: `machine_oom_abstains_instead_of_changing_the_verdict` fails on the 96-thread host. Under `ulimit -v 700000` rayon's global pool (one thread per CPU) cannot start, and the fast path panics ("The global thread pool has not been initialized") instead of abstaining; with 10 CPUs (the dev box) it abstains as the test wants ("cannot start run thread"). A validator on a large machine with a tight address-space limit would crash rather than abstain | OPEN: the remote runner sets `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=16` so the gate matches the dev box; TODO E1: the fast path builds its pool fallibly (a pool that cannot start is an abstain) and the test pins the thread count |
| REMOTE-6 | Secret leak (sync), review 2026-10-19 | Medium | The env and key rules missed credential files and tokens an untracked, unignored file could hold: a `secrets/` folder, an ssh key named `id_ed25519` without a PEM header, `.npmrc` registry tokens, wallet and key-store JSON, binary key stores (`.p12`, `.jks`: `grep -I` never reads binary files), GitHub, npm, AWS and `sk-` tokens, URLs holding a password. Separately, a submodule folder replaced by a symlink to another checkout passed the submodule check (both resolve to the same real path) and listed that checkout's files; rsync follows a symlinked folder on the way to a listed file, so they would have been copied | FIXED: `check-secrets.sh --paths-from` adds credential-file names and token forms for the sync list only (`SYNC_FILE_RE`, `SYNC_PATTERNS`; no hit on the current tree); `remote-check.sh` refuses any listed path whose folder does not resolve to itself. Self-test: `.ENV`, a `.Env.Local` the ignore rules miss, `secrets/notes.txt`, `id_ed25519`, an OpenSSH key by content, wallet and geth key stores, `.npmrc`, `.p12`, a GitHub token, an env-style password, a URL password and a quoted token are each refused with no value printed; a symlink to an outside `.ssh` folder is listed and copied as a link only (the self-test runs the real rsync into a local folder and compares it with the list); an ignored file holding a key is never listed; the symlinked submodule is refused |
| REMOTE-7 | Resource starvation and leftovers, review 2026-10-19 | Medium | `MemoryMax=48G` without `MemorySwapMax` let the job swap past 48 GB into the host's 96 GB swap (`memory.swap.max` was `max`), which the production work shares; a test server or browser that outlived the job kept running in its scope with no end; a dropped ssh session did not stop the job as the docs said (without a tty sshd sends no SIGHUP) | FIXED: `MemorySwapMax=0` (read back in a probe scope on the host: `memory.swap.max` 0); the runner stops its own scope when the job ends and when its output pipe closes (SIGPIPE ignored after the job starts, so a failed write ends `tail`, not the runner). Tests: `scripts/remote-check.sh` self-test, structure only (the swap cap, the two scope stops, SIGPIPE ignored only after the job starts; systemd cannot run there); on the host 2026-10-19: a run whose ssh client was killed (by PID) had its scope gone within seconds and its log ends "the caller went away"; a run stopped by the disk watchdog left no scope and reported exit 4. The stop after a normal end was not yet seen on a full run (TRACKER 2026-10-19) |
| REMOTE-8 | Exit-code honesty, review 2026-10-19 | Low | An unreachable host exited 12 (rsync's protocol error), not the documented 255; rsync used plain ssh without BatchMode, so a key problem could hang on a password prompt | FIXED: one `ssh true` before any copy (255), every copy runs over the same `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` options and exits 255 when it fails. Self-test (`scripts/remote-check.sh`): an unreachable host gives 255. check-all's own status still reaches the caller unchanged (no pipe; a stopped or killed job gives 4, 130, 137 or 143, never 0) |
| REMOTE-9 | Exit-code honesty, review 2026-10-19 | Medium | A real run reported `ALL CHECKS PASSED`, `check-all exit 0` and the host's `exit 0`, but `scripts/remote-check.sh` itself exited 1: bash reads a plain script from the file as it runs, and the reviewer's in-place edits of the same worktree's script during the lead's 81-minute run made bash resume at an old byte offset in new text (reproduced: an in-place rewrite during the ssh call turns 0 into 7 or 127). Any checkout, merge or edit of the file mid-run could do the same, in either direction | FIXED: both scripts are one `{ ... }` block, parsed whole before anything runs; the runner's own log lines print host paths as `~/...` (the host's home names its account). Self-test (`scripts/remote-check.sh`): a copy of the script with a fake ssh and rsync returns check-all's 0, 1 and 4 unchanged, and 0 and 1 unchanged while the fake ssh rewrites the script in place mid-run (the same test without the block gives 7) |
| REMOTE-10 | Resource starvation (concurrent runs), review 2026-10-19 | Medium | Every run is capped alone (48 GB, 48 CPUs), but nothing limited how many ran at once: on 2026-10-19 two agents' runs were on the host together, and three would be allowed 144 GB and 144 CPUs' worth on a machine whose production work uses about 50 GB; only the load guard (60) stood in the way | FIXED: at most 2 runs at once; a run waits for a free build slot (a flock in `~/onyx-build/locks`, held by the runner, never by the job or its leftovers) for up to 2 hours, then exits 3. Self-test (`scripts/remote-check.sh`): with both slots held a third run is refused; when one holder ends, the next run takes its slot |

## Hardware preflight P5 (2026-10-18, `onyx-node doctor`): adversarial pass

Pass by the implementer: an operator whose node a wrong reading stops, a contributor misled by a
generous or a stale threshold, a container that hides its real memory, and the doc, code and site
drifting apart. The doctor is not protocol data and moves no money; it only reads `/proc`, `/sys`
and `statvfs`.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HW-1 | Operator (availability) | Low | A start preflight that refuses on a low reading (RAM in a small container, a misread free space) would turn a slow machine into an outage; the Docker smoke's refused-start controls run in `--memory 1g` (its serving nodes in `--memory 2g`) | FIXED: the start only warns, except below 542,874 bytes free (the soak's largest state directory, where both soak runs topped out); `doctor::tests::the_node_refuses_only_below_the_measured_state_size` |
| HW-2 | Docs drift (honesty) | Low | Thresholds kept in the code, docs/ops/hardware.md, README and the Run page drift apart, so a contributor reads one minimum and the doctor checks another | FIXED: `doctor::tests::the_doc_table_matches_the_code` parses the doc's "Doctor thresholds" table; the e2e Run check requires every figure in the hardware section to be in docs/ops/hardware.md |
| HW-3 | Container (misreading) | Low | `/proc/meminfo` shows the host's RAM inside a container or a systemd scope, so a capped node would pass a RAM check it does not meet | FIXED: usable RAM is the smallest cgroup v2 `memory.max` on the path to the process, if below `MemTotal`; `doctor::tests::usable_ram_is_the_smaller_of_mem_total_and_the_cgroup`, `doctor::tests::the_smallest_cgroup_limit_on_the_path_wins`; cgroup v1 and hybrid hosts since P5-R1-2 |
| HW-4 | Contributor below the minimum | Low | A machine below the minimum runs recipes slowly or cannot allocate a run, and loses rewards in a round | ACCEPTED: a run that cannot allocate abstains (`HostError::Abstain`) instead of giving a wrong verdict, so a small machine costs its owner rewards, never correctness; the doctor says FAIL before the start |
| HW-5 | Misleading pass | Info | "Disk size" is the data directory's filesystem; a contributor whose node sits on another disk gets a pass for the wrong disk, and a rotational check of an overlay or btrfs subvolume (major 0) cannot see the disk | ACCEPTED: the doc and the usage say to point `--data-dir` at the node's disk; an unreadable disk type is a WARN on Linux, never a pass (`doctor::tests::disk_kinds_nvme_sata_ssd_hdd_partitions_and_mapped_devices`) |
| P5-R1-1 | Operator misled (honesty) | Medium | Review P5-R1 (fresh reviewer, 2026-10-19): the `node` row's RAM "minimum" of 2 GiB was the shipped unit's `MemoryMax=2G`, a cap, not a need (measured use 25.2 MiB peak), so `onyx-node doctor --role node` exited 1 with `FAIL ram` on a 2 GB machine whose `MemTotal` reads just under 2 GiB, and every start in a smaller container printed a `FAIL` line yet started | FIXED: 2 GiB is the recommended value (the only size the node was tested in), the minimum is "not measured"; below it is a `WARN`. `doctor::tests::node_threshold_edges_and_unknowns`; doc, README and Run page say so |
| P5-R1-2 | Container (misreading) | Medium | Only cgroup v2 was read: in a cgroup v1 container (older Docker hosts) or on a hybrid host the doctor reported the host's `MemTotal`, so a capped contributor passed a RAM check it does not meet | FIXED: the v1 memory controller's `memory.limit_in_bytes` on the path is read too (no-limit value, at or above 2^62, ignored) and the smaller limit wins. `doctor::tests::cgroup_v1_files_parse`, `doctor::tests::usable_ram_reads_cgroup_v1_and_hybrid_hosts` |
| P5-R1-3 | Docs (honesty) | Low | Numbers with a wrong or missing source: "SSD or NVMe recommended" was cited to bitcoin.org, whose pages ask only 100 MB/s; the node's 1 CPU was "one tokio runtime thread" (the runtime is multi-threaded); the buyer's 2,138 KiB pointed at the wrong benchmarks section; the indexer's daily 141-205 min was tagged measured but was carried forward from its notes; the contributor's 6 GiB added 2 GB and 4 GiB with no arithmetic (2 GB = 1,907 MiB, a run at the cap is 4,112 MiB: 6,020 MiB); section 4's logs were not committed; "waiting for CPU" was not measured | FIXED docs-only: docs/ops/hardware.md (each source re-read 2026-10-19 with User-Agent `onyx-dev`); section 4's logs and script in docs/audit/2026-10-18-hardware/; no threshold moved except P5-R1-1's |
| P5-R1-4 | Misleading pass | Low | The disk check knew only "rotational or not": a SATA SSD passed where every measured machine was NVMe, LVM or dm-crypt read the mapped device's own flag instead of the disks below, and off Linux every `/proc` or `/sys` value printed `WARN` instead of `SKIP` | FIXED: the disk kind is NVMe, other non-rotational, or rotational; a partition reads its disk, dm and md devices read their `slaves/` (NVMe only if all are, rotational if any is, a loop ends); off Linux an unread value is `SKIP`. `doctor::tests::disk_kinds_nvme_sata_ssd_hdd_partitions_and_mapped_devices`, `doctor::tests::off_linux_an_unread_value_is_a_skip_not_a_warn`; tested on a copy of sysfs's layout, not on SATA or HDD hardware |
| P5-R1-5 | Operator (availability) | Low | At a first start the state directory may not exist yet: `statvfs` failed, the preflight printed "could not be read" and could never refuse | FIXED: the preflight reads the nearest existing parent, the filesystem the directory will be made on, and creates nothing. `doctor::tests::the_node_refuses_only_below_the_measured_state_size` |

### ROADMAP P3a (2026-10-18): Bitcoin chain statistics from blocks alone (ADR-0043)

Adversarial pass by the implementer: a cheating miner (rows not from the blocks), a lying node or
mirror (prevouts, heights), a griefing block (rules broken, fuel), a data thief and privacy
(free text in a shipped block input), a JSON-only attacker on the website, a lying REST node, and
test honesty (definitions, window). A fresh review is still owed (ROADMAP P3).

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CHAIN-1 | Cheating miner | High | Commits chain statistics that are not the blocks' (fees, counts, a row for another block) | FIXED: a validator rebuilds the source from its own node, so the snapshot's content hash binds the transactions, and reruns the pinned recipe (level 1, no label, no price); the recipe's own header check (every block hash its header's, every header linked, the parent's included) is a consistency check only, it does not tie the transactions to the header (P3A-R1-3): `btc_chain_stats::tests::headers_must_hash_and_link`; the website window reruns from raw blocks to the committed leaves: `golden_chain::live_blocks_rerun_to_the_committed_window` |
| CHAIN-2 | Lying node or mirror | Medium | Serves prevouts (value, script, creation height) that are not the chain's, moving fees, coin-blocks destroyed and Taproot spends | PARTIAL: prevouts created inside the shard must equal the raw outputs they spend, at the height they were created (`chain::tests::creation_heights_are_checked`), fees are never negative and the coinbase claims at most subsidy plus fees (in the adapter and the recipe); prevouts created before the shard come from the node's index, as for every Bitcoin source (L16): a validator reruns from its own node and a lie is a content-hash mismatch. Second-node rerun tooling: TODO D2 |
| CHAIN-3 | Griefing block source | Medium | A source whose transactions break block rules (a negative fee, a coinbase that spends or is not first, an input from a later block, sizes that cannot be, sums past 21 M BTC) makes the recipe emit nonsense rows | FIXED: the recipe ends with `BAD_TX` or `OVERFLOW`, never a row: `btc_chain_stats::tests::transactions_that_break_block_rules_end_the_run`, `btc_chain_stats::tests::bad_inputs_fail_with_their_codes` |
| CHAIN-4 | Data thief, privacy | Medium | The website ships one block's full recipe input for the browser rerun; chain bytes can carry free text (OP_RETURN messages, coinbase handles, witness data), possibly naming a person, and the build guards then refuse or miss it | FIXED: an `OP_RETURN` script is carried as that byte alone and coinbase `scriptSig`s and witnesses are never carried (`chain::tests::op_return_payloads_are_never_carried`; the rows are unchanged, the recipe reads only that the output is unspendable); the shipped file is on the public allowlist and is scanned by every guard (handles: `pool_review::the_built_site_carries_no_persons_handle`; addresses, e-mail and profile links: `public_build::a_public_build_carries_no_label_rows`). Residual, ACCEPTED: data hidden in spendable-looking output scripts (fake keys) stays, as on every block explorer; the guards still scan it |
| CHAIN-5 | JSON-only attacker on the website | Medium | Edits the window file: a field of a row, a row moved to another height, a time, a dropped or duplicated block, a day removed, swapped or redated, another recipe, range or tip; or adds figures the page could read instead of the rows | FIXED: the verifier decodes every leaf, requires heights to run without a gap over the pinned range, intervals to link, days in date order with each block on its day, and recomputes the pinned commitment; every figure drawn is computed from the checked rows: `chain::every_json_only_edit_of_the_window_fails`, `chain::the_exported_window_checks_out_and_its_sums_are_the_rows`; in the browser: e2e "forged onchain: the window does not check out", e2e "onchain: one changed number is caught" |
| CHAIN-6 | Lying REST node, exposed node | Medium | `scripts/refresh-onchain.py` fetches blocks a node chooses: headers that do not link, block bytes that are not the header's, JSON for another block, another chain; or the script is pointed at a remote unauthenticated REST port | FIXED: each refused before its block is written, loopback only unless `--allow-remote`, no credentials in the URL; every consensus check is the exporter's (`load_chain_range`): `scripts/refresh-onchain-tests.py` (fake REST server on 127.0.0.1, run by check-all) |
| CHAIN-7 | Lazy reader, website trust | Low | The page reruns one block only; the other 1,359 rows rest on the commitment Onyx pinned from its own run | PARTIAL: any block reruns with `golden_chain` or the exporter on one's own node, and the independent Python recount agrees on all 22 fields of every block (`golden_chain::the_committed_window_rebuilds_its_commitment` requires it); the commitment on chain instead of in the verifier: TODO D6 |
| CHAIN-8 | Test honesty (window, definitions) | Low | A reader takes 1,360 blocks (4-13 Oct 2026) for the chain's history, or a metric for another vendor's definition of the same name | FIXED in the page and the ADR: the section names its blocks and dates, says what is not computed and why, and defines every field (docs/spec/recipes.md R-CHAIN-2); "active scripts" is per block, not daily active addresses. A full history: TODO P5 (hardware) and P3 (the window grows with refresh) |
| CHAIN-9 | Rights (fallback build) | Low | Chain figures ship in every build, also the fallback build that must carry no label-derived total; a chain figure could equal a committed company total, or sit next to a company name | FIXED: the files hold leaves (Borsh hex) and one block input, no company name and no label; the page draws chain figures only in its own section; the fallback guard scans the build as before: `public_build::a_fallback_build_carries_no_label_derived_totals` |
| CHAIN-10 | Griefing (fuel) | Low | A dense block makes a one-block shard too costly to rerun | ACCEPTED with the measurement: the window's largest block shard used 81,900,478 fuel, 2.05% of the 4 B limit (docs/ops/benchmarks.md); the weight limit allows at most about 111,000 outputs in a block (9-byte outputs at 36 weight units), about 4.2 times the densest block of the window (26,452 inputs and outputs), so under 10% by the same rate; the preflight still refuses any shard over half its fuel |

### ROADMAP C52 (2026-10-18): far-date unseal copy (ADR-0027 amendment 15)

Adversarial pass by the implementer: a coordinator that never unseals or names another far
date, a server lying toward clients about the far round, drawn observers posting far copies
that do not carry their body key (to keep their value sealed, or to publish it early), the
deterministic far `sigma`, a beacon that stops before the far date, clock lag at the far date,
book migration, and the price of publishing every value at the far date.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C52-1 | Coordinator / server (lying toward clients) | Medium | Names another far round: an earlier one publishes the round's values while later rounds of the fact still run (copying), a later one (or one past drand's life) never unseals | FIXED: the far round is a pure function of the registered template and the spec (`FeedTemplate::last_observable_day`, `timelock::LockRounds::of_round`), computed by the observer, the coordinator and each client for itself; a served `farRound` is only compared, a book's is compared with the template's at restore: `timelock::tests::c52_1_the_far_round_is_the_facts_and_anyone_recomputes_it`, `feed::tests::c52_the_last_observable_day_bounds_every_window_of_the_fact`, `c52_a_live_round_dismisses_a_bad_far_copy_and_serves_the_templates_far_round`, `sealed_reveals::c52_the_page_far_date_mirrors_match_the_coordinator`, `c51_the_round_book_keeps_the_time_lock_read` |
| C52-2 | Coordinator (REVLOG-5 residual) | Medium | A coordinator that never closes a fact never unseals its sealed rounds, so their outcome and `revealed` list stay its word for good | PARTIAL: every time-locked post carries a far copy of its body key; once the far round is out anyone unseals every post with that round's signature alone (no reveal key, no `S`, no `tau`) and recomputes the revealed set and the attempt record: `timelock::tests::c52_2_a_post_unseals_at_the_far_round_without_the_coordinator`, `timelock::tests::c52_4_a_sealed_round_unseals_without_the_coordinator_and_a_false_record_is_caught`, `timelock::tests::c52_real_far_copy_opens_only_with_the_far_rounds_published_signature`. The Rust client and the website do not unseal yet (fetch the far signature, unseal sealed attempts, recompute the outcome): TODO C83 |
| C52-3 | Drawn observer (colluding, or griefing) | Medium | Posts its valid reveal behind a far copy that does not carry its body key (another key, the right key under another `sigma`, a copy locked to the LOCK round so its value is public right after reveal close, junk), so its round would not unseal without the coordinator, or its value would leak early | FIXED: the coordinator re-encrypts the far copy from the unwrapped key at intake, before the far round exists, and dismisses the post with its opening when it differs, even with a valid body; clients accept that dismissal (far rule) and refuse a far-copy pretext against an honest post: `timelock::tests::c52_3_a_far_copy_that_does_not_carry_the_body_key_is_dismissed_at_intake`, `c52_a_live_round_dismisses_a_bad_far_copy_and_serves_the_templates_far_round`, `sealed_reveals::c52_the_page_far_date_mirrors_match_the_coordinator`. A copy locked to the lock round publishes only its poster's own value |
| C52-4 | Sequencer / colluding observer (clock lag) | Medium | Block time lagging the wall clock by more than a day: the far round's signature (and every value of the round) is public while catch-up blocks stamped inside the reveal phase still take posts, so a late colluder could copy | PARTIAL: the far date lies `UNSEAL_MARGIN_SECS` (one day) past the fact's latest possible reveal close, checked at seal and intake (`FarTooSoon`: `timelock::tests::c52_1_the_far_round_is_the_facts_and_anyone_recomputes_it`); a checkable lag rule is C12-6's: TODO C53 |
| C52-5 | drand outage / anyone (liveness) | Low | drand stops, or retires quicknet, before the far round: the far path never opens and the round stays sealed as before C52; a far date too far out is past any horizon Onyx can assume | PARTIAL, by design: no fallback (a coordinator-openable copy would reopen C4-7); the coordinator's path needs only the lock round; far dates are bounded at 1,096 days after the round's reveal close (`FarBeyondHorizon` at seal and intake: `timelock::tests::c52_1_the_far_round_is_the_facts_and_anyone_recomputes_it`); a beacon that never comes is C53's: TODO C53 |
| C52-6 | Test honesty (size, gas) | Info | Cost of the far copy | FIXED (measured): 144 bytes per post (426 for a numeric post), cap 1,294 -> 1,438 (128 + 144 + 142 + 1,024, no byte more), time-locked posts longer than 272 bytes, 579,811 gas cold for a 426-byte post (+113,486 over 282 in one test), runtime 20,505 B: `OnyxRegistrySealedReveals.t.sol::test_TheCapIsTheLargestExactAnswerSealedAndTimeLocked`, `OnyxRegistrySealedReveals.t.sol::test_ATimeLockedDrawsPostsCarryATimeLock`, `OnyxRegistrySealedReveals.t.sol::test_GasOfATimeLockedPost`, `timelock::tests::c12_sizes_against_the_registry_cap` |
| C52-7 | Data thief / business | Low | Every post of a time-locked draw, VALUE rounds included, becomes public, for free, at its far date: each observer's observation, salt and page hash (Treasury: 13 days after the record date; EDGAR: up to about two years) | ACCEPTED: the price of REVLOG-5's closure, chosen in PLAN q-C4-1 (a); the paid API sells values younger than the far date, a dismissed post's plaintext was already public with its dismissal (C4-R1-5), and only freely redistributable feeds may run time-locked draws (C52-R1-2) |
| C52-8 | Coordinator with a colluding observer | Low | Takes a post whose far copy does not carry its key as a REVEAL: a client cannot see it before the far date (it holds no `S`), so that observer's value would never unseal | PARTIAL: the post is on chain and the round recorded; at the far round the post unseals to garbage while served as revealed, a proof against the coordinator (`timelock::tests::c52_4_a_sealed_round_unseals_without_the_coordinator_and_a_false_record_is_caught`); clients run that check from C83: TODO C83 |
| C52-9 | Cryptanalyst | Low | The far copy's `sigma` is derived from the body key (encrypt-with-hash), not random: a reused or guessable key would show in its far copy | ACCEPTED: the key is a fresh uniform 16-byte value from the OS for every post (`seal_timelocked_random`), used once; deterministic encryption of a high-entropy message is secure in the random oracle model (Bellare, Boldyreva, O'Neill 2007; RESEARCH.md "Far-date unseal"), and it is what lets the coordinator check the copy at intake. One guess of a key can be tested against every post at once (about 2^128 / N work for N posts): still out of reach at 128 bits (review C52-R1-6) |

| C52-11 | Test honesty (book migration) | Low | A version-7 book's time-locked round (posts without a far copy) read under the new rules, or decoded wrongly | FIXED: version 8 carries the far round; a version-7 time-locked round is refused with a clear error and any other version-7 round loads: `observe::tests::an_unfinished_round_travels_with_the_book_and_is_rechecked`, `c51_the_round_book_keeps_the_time_lock_read`, `c51_r2_a_version_6_book_with_a_sealed_round_still_loads` |

#### Review C52-R2 (2026-10-18, fresh reviewer, cryptography, protocol and mutation)

Derived `sigma` found sound: the far copy is drand/tlock's FO ciphertext of a fresh uniform 128-bit key with `sigma` a hash of that key (encrypt-with-hash, one ciphertext per key, tags separate it from drand's own hashes); decryption is a function of the ciphertext, so a copy that re-encrypts at intake opens to that very key under the far signature, and there is no decryption oracle to exploit (before the far round nobody opens it, after it everyone does). Far round recomputed for the edges (a window starting the last second of the last observable day, a calendar's coverage end, a fixed subject, quicknet's 3 s grid from genesis, both horizon edges): sound. Mutations of 20 checks (intake far rule, unseal `sigma` rule, far round sum, both edges, redistribution, `far_sigma` round binding, coverage cut, dismissal far rule, web mirrors, client and web length rules, client and book far-round compares, registry length rule and cap): every one caught after the fixes below.

| C52-R2-2 | Test honesty (horizon) | Low | `FarBeyondHorizon` at exactly 1,096 days was untested: `>` mutated to `>=` passed every test, native and web | FIXED: both edges of the horizon and of the one-day margin, native and page: `timelock::tests::c52_1_the_far_round_is_the_facts_and_anyone_recomputes_it`, `sealed_reveals::c52_the_page_far_date_mirrors_match_the_coordinator` |
| C52-R2-3 | Test honesty (dismissals, lengths) | Low | Three checks no test caught under mutation: the page's far rule inside `check` (a far-copy dismissal of a valid body called false would refuse honest rounds on the website), the page's 272-byte rule (its test post also differed from the chain's slot, which refused it alone), and the Rust client's 272-byte rule | FIXED: `sealed_reveals::c52_r2_3_the_page_takes_a_far_copy_dismissal_end_to_end`, the 272-byte case in `sealed_reveals::c51_a_time_locked_section_checks_and_every_lie_is_refused` now matches the chain's slot and names the rule, `c51_timelocked::c52_a_live_round_dismisses_a_bad_far_copy_and_serves_the_templates_far_round` cuts every post to 272 bytes |

Implementer's pass over `crates/onyx-intake`, `onyx_api::submit` and the website's `#/submit`

| T2-3 | Budget evasion | Low | One origin spelled several ways (case, trailing dot, port, user information, an IP literal) gets several budgets | FIXED: `url_origin` lowercases, strips the dot and port, refuses user information and anything that is not a DNS name. `origin_budget::tests::spellings_of_one_origin_share_its_budget`, `origin_budget::tests::a_url_without_an_origin_is_refused`, `fetch::tests::origins` |
| T2-4 | Slot manipulation | Low | An observer picks its own fetch time (for example the last second, to see a fresher page) | ACCEPTED: the slot is a courtesy rule; fetch times are not observable, and the window bounds what any fetch may see (R-OBS-3). `fetch::tests::the_slot_depends_on_round_and_observer` |

### Partner tracker T11 (2026-10-24): TLSNotary presentation of a keyed source (ROADMAP S2b)

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Status / test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TLSN-1 | Notary collusion | High | A notary that colludes with the prover signs a transcript the server never sent | OPEN: the verifier trusts one pinned notary key (`wrong_notary_key_is_refused`). TODO S2: Onyx runs its own notary, or requires several, before any `tlsn-v1` answer is above level 4 |
| TLSN-2 | TLS 1.3 sources | Medium | TLSNotary supports TLS 1.2 only, so a TLS 1.3-only source cannot be proved | OPEN: the verifier requires TLS 1.2 (`recorded_presentation_verifies`). TODO S2: list each candidate source's TLS versions before it is offered as keyed |
| TLSN-3 | Redaction mistakes | High | The prover hides more than the key (for example the target or host), or the key leaks in a shown byte | FIXED in the verifier: only the value of the one declared header may be hidden; everything else in the request must be shown. `hiding_anything_but_the_declared_header_is_refused`, `demo_key_value_is_hidden_and_nothing_else_in_the_request`, `other_host_or_target_is_refused` |
| TLSN-4 | Replay | Medium | An old presentation is sent again as a fresh observation | FIXED when the policy sets a maximum age; sessions in the future are refused. `old_presentation_is_refused_when_a_max_age_is_set`, `session_in_the_future_is_refused` |
| TLSN-5 | Malformed input | Medium | A crafted presentation crashes or exhausts the verifier: tlsn-core allocates a transcript length read from the file before checking it (8 of the fixture's 18,553 single-bit flips, at bytes 15,228-15,231 and 15,236-15,239, ask for a huge allocation, about 1 TB in the logged one, and abort the process) | PARTIAL: size cap and exact decoding (`trailing_or_oversized_input_is_refused`); no flip changes what is proved, and the scan runs under a 4 GiB limit (`no_bit_flip_changes_what_is_proved`). the verifier now runs in a child process under an address-space limit and a deadline (`isolated::verify_isolated`): an aborting presentation is refused and the caller keeps running (`isolated::a_presentation_that_aborts_tlsn_core_is_refused_and_the_caller_survives`, `isolated::a_wrong_notary_key_is_refused_not_crashed`). TODO S2: the API calls it when it accepts `tlsn-v1` presentations |
| TLSN-6 | Identity by hash | Low | One bit of the presentation (byte 7,383 of the fixture) can flip and the presentation still verifies with the exact same result, so two different files carry one proof; a hash of the file used as an id or a duplicate check would count it twice | OPEN: `no_bit_flip_changes_what_is_proved` lists such bytes. TODO S2: key a stored presentation by its verified content (server, session time, transcript hash), never by the file's hash |

| U4-3 | Rights laundering | Medium | A submission answering "own data" or "not sure" for a public source gets pulled | FIXED: only public-domain or open-licence answers are fed; the adapter's reviewed rights govern the fetch. `u4_intake_feed::another_field_or_unclear_rights_are_refused` |
| U4-4 | Double recording, endless retries | Medium | A worker reruns a fed submission (a second round, a second value) or retries a failing one forever | FIXED: the feed ledger returns a fed submission's recorded evidence and runs nothing, refuses a fed id whose content changed, and stops after `MAX_FEED_ATTEMPTS` (3) failures with the last reason; refusals before the round (not approved, not the pinned feed, no recording) use no attempt. `u4_intake_feed::the_feed_ledger_feeds_once_and_bounds_failures` |
| U4-5 | Evidence leak or forgery on the public receipt (data thief, tampered ledger) | Medium | The fed receipt's public status carries operator reasons, proposal content or a hand-edited field the page renders | FIXED: only `level`, `recordDate`, `roundId`, `result`, `registry`, only for an approved receipt fed with its current hash; failures show nothing; the node shape-checks every field at startup and refuses a damaged ledger; the page accepts the exact key set only. `submit_tests::a_fed_receipt_shows_the_observers_evidence_and_nothing_private`, `u4_intake_feed::the_feed_ledger_feeds_once_and_bounds_failures`, e2e "PP1 receipt parser: exact evidence shape on approved receipts only; limits stated" |
| U4-6 | Evidence read as truth (contributor, buyer) | Low | "Checked by observers" is read as "the value is correct", or a rehearsal round as an on-chain one | FIXED: the page says the evidence shows the source published the value, not that it is correct, and names a `simulated` registry as "not posted on a chain". e2e "PP1 receipt parser: exact evidence shape on approved receipts only; limits stated"; the connected rehearsal `apps/web/tests/submission-live.mjs` checks the same words on the real node's receipt PP11 2026-10-25: the receipt now also shows the observers' value under the same words (the source published it; not a claim that it is correct); e2e "PP1 receipt parser: exact evidence shape on approved receipts only; limits stated" (it checks the value too) |
| PP9-1 | Operator feeding a made-up round (reviewer, node operator) | Low | A live round's evidence comes from a store file the operator passes: a forged store, a store of another date, or a chain the operator names could put false evidence on a receipt | FIXED 2026-10-25: `fed_from_store` loads the store with the pinned template (every round transcript is rechecked on load), needs a round for the approved record date, and takes the receipt's chain from the store's own `onchain` tag; an untagged store is refused. | PRE-10 | Double payout (reporter crash) | High | The reporter allocates the same usage twice (a crash or a lost receipt after the send), paying books with other buyers' pooled money | FIXED: the lines an allocation covers are marked in `<journal>.allocated` before the transaction is sent and unmarked only when nothing was broadcast or it reverted; an unknown outcome leaves them marked, so the money stays in the pool instead of being paid twice. `scripts/prepaid-anvil.sh` (second pass pays nothing).
