| CL4-6 | Terms bypass | High | A source whose terms forbid passing on data obtained with a personal key is laundered through "the contributor fetched it" | MITIGATED: a keyed manifest loads only under a docs/ops/data-sources.md section 6 row whose decision is exactly `OK keyed` (a plain `OK` row clears public manifests only; the project's table has no keyed row today); every other manifest rule still applies (rights, no other secret parameter, blocked hosts, stated ids); `keyed join` shows the terms and their hash, which the seat signs. `onyx-level2::a_keyed_manifest_without_cleared_terms_does_not_load`, `onyx-level2::a_fresh_seat_is_not_drawable` (a seat for other terms is left out); onyx-contrib: "keyed: join shows the terms, needs --yes without a terminal, and the seat holds nothing about the key (CL4-6, CL4-9)" (apps/contrib/test/keyed.test.mjs) |
| CL4-7 | Linkage by time or page | Medium | The provider matches a reveal's public fetch time or page hash with its own access log and served pages, and links an Onyx address to its customer | MITIGATED: a keyed observer fetches at its own random second (never derived from public data, never published), posts its commit at the window's end (review CL4-R1-2), fetches even when not drawn (CL4-R1-3); its reveal states the window start as `observed_at` and a page hash blinded with 32 fresh random bytes never kept. `onyx-level2::keyed_fetch_slots_are_not_derived_from_public_data`, `onyx-level2::a_keyed_round_writes_no_byte_of_the_key_anywhere` (reveal times and page hashes checked). Residual: the provider still sees which of its keys fetch during a round's window (ADR-0054 consequences) |
| CL4-8 | Replay of another holder's answer | Medium | A seat holder without a key (or without fetching) copies another holder's commit or reveal | MITIGATED (unchanged round rules): a commit binds the observer's address and is posted before any reveal; reveals open after commit close and are sealed or spooled; a copied commit cannot be revealed by the copier; blinded page hashes make even a copied hash one's own fresh value. `onyx-coordinator::copier_cannot_reveal_a_copied_commit_or_change_its_answer_late`, `onyx-coordinator::c4_copying_another_observers_ephemeral_key_is_refused` |
| CL4-9 | Key fingerprint linkage | High | A key hash, a fingerprint or any deterministic function of the key in a seat, a pool, a proposal or a reveal lets the provider (who knows every key) link the address to its customer | MITIGATED: nothing derived from a key is asked for, signed, stored or sent; a seat is exactly observer, source, operator, terms hash, time and signature; a pool member is an address and a bond. `onyx-level2::seats_and_pools_hold_no_key_and_no_key_fingerprint`, `onyx-core::keyed_access_is_in_the_fetcher_id_and_public_bytes_are_unchanged`; onyx-contrib: "keyed: join shows the terms, needs --yes without a terminal, and the seat holds nothing about the key (CL4-6, CL4-9)" (apps/contrib/test/keyed.test.mjs) |
| CL4-10 | Collusion | Medium | A colluding majority of the drawn holders settles a false value | ACCEPTED as THREATS L2-F2 for every level-2 round, plus a keyed-specific disclosure: the odds that a third of the pool colluding wins one draw (and the best of three) are shown next to every keyed value (`keyed` block of the summary and the coordinator's output). `onyx-level2::keyed_collusion_odds_are_shown`. Bonds that make collusion costly wait for the partners' economics (H3) |

### Review CL4-R1 (fresh adversarial reviewer, 2026-10-30)

A fresh reviewer read the whole CL4 change as a provider hunting keys and their owners, a holder
with many keys, a colluding coordinator and a prompt-injected assistant. Three High findings
(the key in a revealed value, the commit time, the drawn set against the keys that fetch), two
Medium that need code (the pool an observer accepts) or a disclosure (active probing), and Low or
Info ones. Fixed with tests unless the row says otherwise.

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Status / test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CL4-R1-1 | Key in the revealed value | High | A pointer or a provider that echoes the request puts the key (or a piece) in the value every holder commits and reveals on chain | FIXED: a keyed observer reads the value first and answers `Unavailable` when it holds any 10-byte piece of its key, in any case, as typed or percent-encoded (`keyed::keyed_page`, `ApiKey::held_in`); manifests serve numeric values only. `onyx-level2::a_keyed_reveal_never_holds_the_key`, `onyx-fetch::held_in_finds_any_piece_of_the_key` |
| CL4-R1-2 | Commit time tells the fetch time | High | The observer posted its commit seconds after its private fetch, so the provider matched its access log to the commit's time on chain | FIXED: a keyed observer posts its commit at the window's end whatever its fetch second (`keyed::keyed_commit_time`). `onyx-level2::keyed_commits_never_tell_the_fetch_second` |
| CL4-R1-3 | Drawn set against fetching keys | High | Only drawn holders fetched; over a few rounds the provider matches the public drawn sets with the keys it saw fetch and maps every key to its address | MITIGATED: every seat of the round's snapshot fetches once at its own private slot, drawn or not (an undrawn one discards the page), so the keys that fetch in a window are the whole snapshot. The local demo checks the fake provider answered all 9 seats (7 drawn, 2 as cover): docs-only: scripts/level2-keyed-anvil.sh. Residual: a seat whose observer is offline is missing from both sets, which the provider can still correlate over many rounds; and one fetch per seat per round must fit the provider's rate limit |
| CL4-R1-4 | Active probing by the provider | Medium | The provider answers one key differently (or refuses it) on purpose; the address whose public reveal differs is that key's | ACCEPTED: no code removes it (answers are public by design; `outlier_slash == miss_slash` keeps the holder's loss small); it is stated in `keyed join`'s preview, in ADR-0054 amendment 1 and here, so a holder joins knowing it |
| CL4-R1-5 | Observer accepts any pool | Medium | The pool check ran only with `--seats`, which the announcement path never gave, so a coordinator could draw addresses with no seat, fresh bonds or several seats of one operator | FIXED: a keyed observer refuses to run without the seats and refuses any pool but the round's keyed snapshot; a keyed round's announcement carries the seats and `apply_announcement` hands them over. `onyx-level2::a_keyed_observer_refuses_a_pool_that_is_not_the_snapshot` |
| CL4-R1-6 | Coordinator decides eligibility | Medium | Bond, bond time and history are the coordinator's word in the seats file, and it can leave honest seats out | TODO S2: read seat bonds, bond times and agreed rounds from the chain and publish the seat set for anyone to add to, before any keyed source goes to Base Sepolia (as CL4-3) |
| CL4-R1-7 | Seats never expire, not tied to a deployment | Low | A holder who stopped stays drawable and is slashed for misses; old seats are replayed into another deployment's pool | PARTIAL: a seat counts 90 days after it was signed (`KEYED_SEAT_TTL_SECS`), then the holder joins again. `onyx-level2::a_fresh_seat_is_not_drawable`. TODO S2: bind the seat to the chain id and registry |
| CL4-R1-8 | Not declaring an operator pays | Low | Declaring caps an operator at one seat per round; staying silent costs nothing | ACCEPTED: the operator rule only stops honest correlation (ADR-0054 item 6); `keyed join`'s preview and the README say so, next to the shown odds |
| CL4-R1-9 | Forged terms table through the assistant | Low | The MCP tools took a `repo` argument, so a prompt injection could point the terms check at a forged data-sources.md with an `OK keyed` row | FIXED: the terms folder comes from the user's `ONYX_CONTRIB_REPO` only; a `repo` argument is refused. onyx-contrib: "keyed MCP: join checks first, signs only on confirm; observe runs in the background; no result holds the key" (docs-only: apps/contrib/test/keyed.test.mjs) |
| CL4-R1-10 | Smaller key-handling gaps | Info | An observe error could echo text of a key-holding page; copies of the key (encoded query value, Bearer string, filled URL) are not zeroed | ACCEPTED: the observer's own errors now pass `ApiKey::redact` too (and onyx-contrib filters every line); the copies are kept, since they live only in the observer's memory for one request |

## CL8 (2026-10-30): time alignment for market data (ADR-0058)

What is built: `SubjectRule::Bucketed` (`onyx_core::feed`: closed buckets `[k × B, (k + 1) × B)` of
the UTC grid, B an hour or a day, observable `min_delay_secs..=max_delay_secs` after the bucket's
end), the asserts `Expect::BucketStart` and `Expect::Positive` (`onyx_core::feed_json`,
`onyx_json::read_at`), the pure alignment rule `onyx_core::aligned` (lower median of the included
venues, the min..max band, an exact integer disagreement flag, the four clocks, the answer id and
the client check), `onyx_level2::aligned` (composite manifests over bucketed venue manifests,
venue facts read from verified level-2 results stores and the chain record, the answer JSON) and
`scripts/level2-aligned-anvil.sh` (six loopback fake venues on a local anvil). Attackers: a venue
that lies about its clock or answers another bucket; a manipulator printing wash trades at a
bucket's edge on a thin venue; one venue or operator dominating a composite; a stale or halted
venue; a coordinator choosing windows or leaving out a disagreeing venue; an operator serving a
forged answer; a data thief passing on a venue's data against its terms. No venue is cleared
(docs/ops/market-venues.md): every test runs on fixtures and loopback fakes; nothing contacts a
real venue.

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Status / test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CL8-1 | Venue clock | High | A venue answers another bucket than the subject's: off by one interval, a day cut on local time, a candle stamped a few seconds off the grid by a skewed clock | MITIGATED: a bucketed template needs a `BucketStart` assert (in the fetcher id, so in the on-chain pin) that the venue's own time equals the subject's bucket start, in the declared form (seconds, milliseconds, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`); anything else gives `Unavailable`, and the venue is listed `unavailable`. `onyx-json::a_bucket_with_another_start_is_unavailable`, `onyx-level2::a_skewed_or_halted_venue_settles_unavailable`, `onyx-core::a_bucketed_template_needs_a_bucket_start_assert`. Residual: a venue that labels every candle consistently one interval off cannot be told from its own record; its value then differs from the others and raises the flag (CL8-2) |
| CL8-2 | Manipulation | High | One venue (a manipulated thin venue) moves the composite | MITIGATED: the lower median of at least `MIN_VENUES` (3) included venues and more than half of the listed ones; no value while a listed venue can still be observed (`pending`) or after one lapsed unobserved, so whoever pays for rounds never picks the subset (review CL8-R1-1); one far venue never moves it, the band shows it and `disagreement` is raised; nothing is trimmed or hidden. `onyx-core::one_far_venue_does_not_move_the_median_and_raises_the_flag`, `onyx-core::a_subset_of_observed_venues_cannot_set_the_median`, `onyx-level2::an_aligned_feed_from_six_loopback_venues_end_to_end`. Residual (stated): a majority of the included venues moved the same way moves the median; with an even count the lower half sets the lower median |
| CL8-3 | Units | Medium | Venues in different units or scales mixed (a stablecoin quote with a currency quote) | FIXED: one unit, scale and bucket length per composite, checked when the composite loads; no conversion is ever done. `onyx-core::a_composite_with_two_units_does_not_load`, `onyx-level2::composite_files_are_checked` |
| CL8-4 | Operator | High | The operator leaves out a venue that disagrees, relabels it, or serves a forged answer | MITIGATED: the venue list is the composite's (sorted, fixed in its file and its id); `aligned` refuses inputs that miss, add or reorder a listed venue; the answer has an id over every field; the client check recomputes it from the venue facts it verified as level-2 answers and refuses any difference; for every venue its store shows without a value, the client asks the chain (`observationOf`) and refuses a store that hides a recorded fact (review CL8-R1-2). `onyx-core::the_client_refuses_a_composite_missing_a_listed_venue`, `onyx-level2::the_client_refuses_a_store_that_hides_a_recorded_venue`, `onyx-level2::an_aligned_feed_from_six_loopback_venues_end_to_end`; on anvil, five forged answers and a hidden store refused (`scripts/level2-aligned-anvil.sh`). TODO S14: the browser's check and the served route |
| CL8-5 | Late prints | Medium | A bucket is read before late trades and venue corrections settle, so observers or rechecks disagree | FIXED: a bucket is observable only from `min_delay_secs` (at least 60 s) after its end, never while open. `onyx-core::a_bucket_is_observable_only_after_its_delay` |
| CL8-6 | Window shopping | Medium | A coordinator waits inside the observable range for a venue correction it prefers, or picks which bucket is observed | MITIGATED: `max_delay_secs - min_delay_secs` is at most 6 hours, one fact per bucket (`DatedFeed`), and the newest observable bucket is a function of the window and the template. `onyx-core::the_bucketed_observable_range_is_short`, `onyx-level2::the_latest_bucket_is_the_templates_choice`. ACCEPTED residual: inside 6 hours a venue's own correction can still be chosen; the value is the venue's record at that time, with its round |
| CL8-7 | Rights | High | A restricted venue's data leaks through a composite served as unrestricted | FIXED: the composite's rights are the strictest of its listed venues', whether or not that venue's value is included. `onyx-core::a_composite_with_a_restricted_venue_is_restricted` |
| CL8-8 | Clocks | Medium | A venue fact whose clocks contradict each other (observed before the bucket closed, a reveal outside its window, recorded before its window ended, a venue time other than the bucket) is counted | FIXED: every included fact passes `VenueFact::clock_check`, else the venue is listed `clock_mismatch`; a value round counts only once the chain recorded it (`observationLevel` 2), and a venue page is used only when its Keccak-256 is an agreeing reveal's page hash. `onyx-core::a_venue_whose_clocks_disagree_is_not_counted`, `onyx-core::every_answer_states_its_four_clocks`, `onyx-level2::a_venue_counts_only_when_recorded_and_only_with_its_own_page` |
| CL8-9 | Wash prints | Medium | Wash trades printed at a bucket's edge on a thin venue move that venue's close, the most edge-sensitive field of a candle | PARTIAL: the median of at least three venues and the shown band and flag bound one venue's effect (`onyx-core::one_far_venue_does_not_move_the_median_and_raises_the_flag`; the golden vectors' wash-print case); a bucketed descriptor must assert a positive volume on the value's own object (`onyx-core::bucket_start_must_pin_the_value_row`). TODO S14: per venue, read a volume-weighted or typical price where the venue publishes one, and a minimum volume or trade count per bucket instead of only a positive volume (one print of 0.00000001 passes today) |
| CL8-10 | Concentration | Medium | One venue dominates: the same venue (or host) listed under two feeds, a weight, or several venues under one operator | PARTIAL: a composite refuses the same venue (`rights.source`), host or terms row twice (review CL8-R1-3: two hosts of one reviewed party) and has no weights (one venue, one vote). `onyx-core::a_composite_listing_one_venue_twice_does_not_load`, `onyx-core::two_hosts_of_one_terms_row_do_not_load`, `onyx-level2::composite_files_are_checked`. TODO S14: the reviewer records each venue's owner (docs/ops/market-venues.md section 1) and a composite refuses two venues of one owner under different terms rows |
| CL8-11 | Stale venue | Medium | A halted or stale venue repeats its last price (a bucket with no trades) or returns no bucket | MITIGATED: venue manifests assert a positive volume (`Expect::Positive`) and exactly one candle; a stale or empty bucket gives `Unavailable` and the venue is listed `unavailable`. `onyx-json::a_halted_or_stale_venue_gives_no_value`, `onyx-level2::a_skewed_or_halted_venue_settles_unavailable`. Residual: a venue that keeps a tiny volume while stale passes; the median and the flag bound it (CL8-2), TODO S14 for a minimum volume (CL8-9) |
| CL8-12 | Rights bypass | High | A venue whose terms forbid passing its data on (or were never read) reaches an answer: a manifest for an uncleared host, a composite over it, or "the contributor fetched it" | FIXED: a venue manifest loads only with an `OK` host row under an `OK` terms row (CL3-7), so a composite over an uncleared venue does not load; a `Forbidden` venue never enters a composite; the project's terms table clears no market venue, and the demo venues load only under the fixture's synthetic table. `onyx-level2::a_venue_without_cleared_terms_never_loads`, `onyx-core::a_composite_with_a_restricted_venue_is_restricted`; the per-venue review is docs-only: docs/ops/market-venues.md |

### Review CL8-R1 (fresh adversarial reviewer, 2026-10-30)

A fresh reviewer read the CL8 commit (read only, no probes run) as a paying manipulator, a
coordinator, an operator serving forged answers, an operator with several hosts and a data thief.
Two High findings (a payer picking the counted subset; a store hiding a recorded venue), two
Medium, three Low and Info notes. Fixed with tests unless the row says otherwise. It also checked
and found sound: every new enum variant appended (no existing Borsh, fetcher or template id
moved), placeholder replacement, strict subject and RFC 3339 parsing, overflow in the bucket and
spread arithmetic, every `is_dated()` caller for bucketed templates, and the forged-answer checks.

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Status / test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CL8-R1-1 | Subset picking | High | Rounds run only when paid, one per venue fact: paying only for one honest and two manipulated venues of six gave an `aligned` value from three, final once the others' range passed | FIXED: `pending` while a listed venue can still be observed, no value once one lapsed unobserved, and included venues must be more than half of the listed. `onyx-core::a_subset_of_observed_venues_cannot_set_the_median`, `onyx-level2::a_bucket_lapses_after_its_last_round_could_close`. TODO S14: one composite hold pays for every listed venue's round (ADR-0049) |
| CL8-R1-2 | Hidden venue | High | The client built its inputs from stores the operator serves: dropping a venue's store (or keeping only an older failed attempt) made a recorded venue `not_observed` and the check passed | FIXED: for every venue not recorded in its store, the client reads `observationOf(metric, subject, 0)` (a dated fact's key ignores the window end) and refuses a store that hides a recorded result; a value round must be exactly the recorded one (`observationLevel` 2). `onyx-level2::the_client_refuses_a_store_that_hides_a_recorded_venue`; on anvil: `scripts/level2-aligned-anvil.sh` (the hidden-store attack) |
| CL8-R1-3 | Concentration | Medium | Venue identity was exact strings: one operator's `api.x` and `api2.x` with two source names counted twice | FIXED in part: the terms row is in the venue reference and a composite refuses it twice. `onyx-core::two_hosts_of_one_terms_row_do_not_load`. TODO S14: ownership across terms rows (CL8-10) |
| CL8-R1-4 | Wash prints | Medium | A bucketed descriptor needed no volume assert, and a positive volume of one tiny print passes | FIXED in part: a bucketed descriptor must assert a positive volume on the value's object. `onyx-core::bucket_start_must_pin_the_value_row`. TODO S14: a minimum volume and a volume-weighted price (CL8-9) |
| CL8-R1-5 | Venue clock | Low | The bucket-start assert could pin another row of a list than the value (start of row 0, close of row 1, the next bucket's price) | FIXED: the bucket-start and volume asserts must sit on the value's own object. `onyx-core::bucket_start_must_pin_the_value_row` |
| CL8-R1-6 | Rights | Low | `answer_json` prints every venue's value even for a `Restricted` composite; `RightsWithheld` is never produced yet | TODO S14: the route gates the venue values on the composite's rights and produces `rights_withheld` for a venue whose terms limit what is shown; nothing is served today (no route, no cleared venue) |
| CL8-R1-7 | Process | Low | The CL8 rows were missing from THREATS.md in the reviewed commit | FIXED: this section. docs-only: THREATS.md |
| CL8-R1-8 | Weaker than it looks | Info | Without a page the venue time is the asserted bucket start; a venue that labels a local-time candle as UTC passes every assert; the core clock check relies on the store check for the delay window | ACCEPTED: stated in ADR-0058 amendment 1 and rows CL8-1 and CL8-8; the store check (`FeedTemplate::matches` inside `ObservationStore::from_json`) enforces the delay window for every round a client reads |

## CL6 (2026-10-30): the credits ledger, relayed actions paid from credits (ADR-0056)

What is built: `OnyxPrepaidV2` (one spendable balance per account: `depositFor` with an origin
fixed by the payer, `depositWithAuthorization` through EIP-3009 `receiveWithAuthorization`,
`payRelayer` to an immutable relayer within the pool and a daily cap), `OnyxRevenueV2`
(`withdrawToCredits`, a 1% treasury floor), `script/DeployCredits.s.sol`, `onyx_api::credits`
(`/v1/credits/schedule`, `/v1/credits/{account}`, `/v1/credits/{account}/lines`, `POST
/v1/relay`), relay holds and gas lines in the prepaid journal, the reporter paying gas lines with
`payRelayer`, onyx-node `ONYX_RELAY_KEY_FILE`, `ONYX_RELAY_FEES`, `ONYX_CREDITS_FROM_BLOCK`, and
`scripts/credits-anvil.sh` (in check-all). Attackers: an account farming or minting credit, a
griefer cancelling exits or spending another account's relays, a sybil set draining the relayer's
gas, a front-runner, a curious reader of another account's purchases, a leaked reporter key, an
operator moving from v1 to v2. Testnet only; nothing is deployed on Base Sepolia (runbook
docs/ops/runbooks/deploy-credits.md).

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Status / test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CL6-1 | Wash buying | Medium | An account buys its own data to farm earned credit | MITIGATED (R-CR-3): `OnyxRevenueV2` refuses a split that keeps less than `MIN_TREASURY_BPS` (1%) for the treasury, so one address holding every role on a book gets back less than the fee, fuzzed over every accepted split and book shape. `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::testFuzz_NoAddressEarnsBackAFullFee`, `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_RevenueV2KeepsATreasuryFloor` |
| CL6-2 | Relayer acts for someone | High | The relayer sends a call its actor did not sign, or an account pays for another's action | MITIGATED: only four self-signed actions are relayed; the observer's (or receipt signer's, or depositor's EIP-712) signature is checked before anything is held, simulated or sent, and the voucher must be the actor's own. `onyx-api::the_relayer_refuses_an_action_without_the_actors_signature`, `onyx-api::a_receipt_for_the_observer_is_relayed_and_paid_by_it`, `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_DepositWithAuthorizationCreditsTheSignerOnly`; the anvil demo's `forged_commit` step |
| CL6-3 | Charged without the action | High | A relay that reverts, would revert or is not mined in time is charged | MITIGATED: the voucher is held, charged only when the transaction is mined without a revert, released otherwise (a stale relay hold is released at start). `onyx-api::a_reverted_relay_releases_its_hold`, `onyx-api::a_stale_relay_hold_is_released_at_start`; the demo's `repeat_commit` step (released, the relayer sent nothing) |
| CL6-4 | Relay spam | Medium | Relays drain the operator's ETH | MITIGATED: the fee voucher is held first (no spendable credit, no relay: R-CR-7), then 60 relays an hour and 3 failures a day per account, a base-fee cap and a daily gas budget, all before anything is sent. `onyx-api::relays_over_the_hourly_cap_are_refused_before_sending`, `onyx-api::no_relay_without_spendable_credit`; the demo's `over_cap` step. Residual: CL6-R1-2 |
| CL6-5 | Purchase privacy | Medium | A balance read reveals what an account bought | MITIGATED: lines and the journal's numbers need the account's own fresh (120 s), single-use proof; without one the view shows only chain data. `onyx-api::credits_lines_need_the_accounts_own_fresh_proof`; the demo's `lines_without_proof` step |
| CL6-6 | Exit griefing | Medium | `depositFor` (or a signed deposit relayed late) cancels or blocks someone's exit | MITIGATED: only the account's own `deposit` touches `exitAt`. `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_DepositForDoesNotCancelAnExit`, `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_DepositWithAuthorizationDoesNotCancelAnExit` |
| CL6-7 | Double-counted earnings | High | An earned share is both withdrawable from `OnyxRevenue` and credited | MITIGATED: `withdrawToCredits` zeroes the balance and counts it paid out before the call, requires exactly that amount to leave, resets the allowance, and is nonReentrant. `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_WithdrawToCreditsMovesTheBalanceOnce`, `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_WithdrawToCreditsRefusesAShortOrReentrantCredit` |
| CL6-8 | Forged origin | Low | Anyone tags a deposit "earned", "refund" or "payout" so the ledger shows earnings that were bought | MITIGATED: the origin is the payer's own (`revenue` only 2, owner-named sources only 3 or 4, everyone else 1). `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_DepositForOriginIsFixedByThePayer`, `CreditsInvariants.t.sol::invariant_AttacksNeverSucceed`; the demo refuses a buyer's `depositFor(.., 2)` |
| CL6-9 | Mint | High | Credit is created without the asset arriving | MITIGATED: every credit path pulls the token or checks the exact balance change; no mint, grant or transfer between accounts (R-CR-1, R-CR-6); token held = unspent balances + pool, and = everything in less everything out. `CreditsInvariants.t.sol::invariant_NoCreditFromNothing`, `CreditsInvariants.t.sol::invariant_BalancesPlusPoolEqualHoldings`, `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::testFuzz_CreditOnlyFromArrivedAsset`; the demo's conservation check |
| CL6-10 | Replay and malleability | High | A voucher of v1 or another chain, a lower or repeated total, a high-s twin, or a used deposit authorization is accepted | MITIGATED: the EIP-712 domain binds the contract; totals only rise within the balance; low s and v 27/28 only; EIP-3009 nonces. `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_VouchersAreBoundToThisContractAndRiseOnlyWithinTheBalance`, `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_HighSTwinsAreRefused`, `CreditsInvariants.t.sol::invariant_AttacksNeverSucceed` |
| CL6-11 | Front-run deposit | Medium | Someone submits a signed deposit to the token directly, so the asset arrives uncredited | MITIGATED: deposits use `receiveWithAuthorization`, which only the payee (the ledger) can submit; the credit goes to the signer, exactly the amount that arrived. `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_DepositWithAuthorizationCreditsTheSignerOnly` |
| CL6-12 | Reporter and relay fees | Medium | A leaked reporter key pays the pool out as relay fees | MITIGATED: `payRelayer` pays only the immutable relayer, never above the pool, never above `maxRelayPerDay` per UTC day; the reporter stays trusted for allocation as REV-1. `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_PayRelayerStaysInThePoolTheCapAndTheRelayer`, `CreditsInvariants.t.sol::invariant_RelayerPaidOnlyWithinTheCap` |
| CL6-13 | Fee schedule abuse | Medium | The server charges more than the published fee, or changes it under a client | MITIGATED: fees are fixed, positive, at most `MAX_RELAY_FEE`, one per action, published with a hash; a voucher must add exactly the fee, so a changed fee refuses the old voucher and charges nothing. `onyx-api::the_fee_schedule_is_bounded_and_a_changed_fee_is_never_charged`, `onyx-api::a_mined_relay_charges_exactly_the_scheduled_fee` |
| CL6-14 | Shared relayer key | Medium | The relayer's key is also the reporter's, an owner's or the coordinator's | MITIGATED: the contract and the deploy script refuse a relayer equal to the reporter or the owner (and the treasury); onyx-node refuses a relay key that is the reporter, an owner or the coordinator, or not `relayer()`. `OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_TheRelayerIsNeverTheReporterOrTheOwner`, `DeployCredits.t.sol::test_RefusesOtherChainsAndASharedRelayerKey`, `onyx-node::the_relay_key_is_its_own_and_the_symbol_decodes_strictly`. Level-2 pool members are not known to the node: TODO S7 check the relayer against the pool snapshot before a live relay |
| CL6-15 | Free action for the operator's loss | Low | A relay that ends pending, or a crash between mining and the charge, gives the actor its action without a fee | ACCEPTED: the hold is released (the account is never charged for an unknown outcome); the operator's loss is bounded by the per-account and daily gas limits, and an attacker cannot choose it |
| CL6-16 | Credit seen late | Info | A relayed deposit is spendable only once the node's `finalized` read shows it (minutes on Base Sepolia) | ACCEPTED: the same rule as every deposit (ADR-0046 amendment 2: no spend against a reorg-able deposit); its own fee is held against the incoming amount and charged only after mining |
| CL6-17 | v1 to v2 | Medium | Moving the node to `OnyxPrepaidV2` reuses v1's journal and books | FIXED with review CL6-R1-1 below; v1 vouchers are worthless on v2 (`OnyxPrepaidV2.t.sol::test_VouchersAreBoundToThisContractAndRiseOnlyWithinTheBalance`); v1 balances leave through v1's own exit, and v1's last vouchers are redeemed by a reporter run against the v1 journal (docs-only: docs/ops/runbooks/deploy-credits.md) |
| CL6-18 | Front-run relayed post | Low | Anyone copies a relayed post from the mempool and lands it first; the relay reverts unpaid | ACCEPTED: the actor's post lands either way (its goal); the relayer's lost gas counts toward the account's 3 failures a day and the daily budget |

### Review CL6-R1 (fresh adversarial reviewer, 2026-10-30)

A fresh reviewer read the CL6 change for theft, minting, double spends, relayer and fee abuse and
the move from v1. It found no way to create credit from nothing or to count an earned share twice
(each checked path is listed in its report), and one High, three Medium and two Low issues. All are
fixed with tests except the residual of CL6-R1-2.

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Status / test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CL6-R1-1 | v1 to v2 | High | The node kept `prepaid.journal` when `ONYX_PREPAID` moved to v2: each buyer's v1 total was asked again on v2 (paid twice) and a stale v1 voucher made every redemption batch revert | FIXED: a journal is bound to its contract (`<journal>.domain`, written once every line was checked); a journal whose vouchers are another contract's is refused at start; the node names new journals per contract (`prepaid-0x<contract>.journal`). `onyx-api::a_journal_from_another_contract_is_refused` |
| CL6-R1-2 | Gas drain | Medium | A flat fee let one account spend the whole daily gas budget with a few large sealed reveals | PARTIAL: each account's relays may use at most `account_gas_per_day` (2.5M gas) of the 20M budget. `onyx-api::one_account_cannot_spend_the_whole_daily_gas_budget`. Many funded accounts together can still use the day's budget (then relays answer 503 until the next day; nothing is lost but the operator's test gas). TODO S7: price each relay by its simulated gas with a fixed credits-per-gas rate, measured on Base Sepolia |
| CL6-R1-3 | Paid-for reverts | Medium | A deposit authorization expiring seconds after the simulation reverted on chain at the relayer's cost, repeatably | FIXED: a deposit must be valid now and for at least the hold time plus 60 s. `onyx-api::a_deposit_expiring_before_it_can_be_mined_is_refused` |
| CL6-R1-4 | Relay lockout | Medium | A voucher header naming a victim, with any signature, spent the victim's hourly relays | FIXED: the voucher's signature is checked first, and relays are counted only once the account's own voucher is held. `onyx-api::a_forged_voucher_does_not_spend_the_actors_relays` |
| CL6-R1-5 | Total leak | Low | An unsigned voucher learned an account's journal total and whether a hold was pending (also on the answer routes) | FIXED: `PrepaidBook` checks the signature before anything else. `onyx-api::an_unsigned_voucher_learns_nothing_about_the_total` |
| CL6-R1-6 | Relay payout | Low | The reporter's pass applied the daily cap per pass, so later passes of a day reverted and a backlog never cleared | FIXED: the pass reads `relayDay` and `relayPaidToday` and pays only what today's cap has left. `onyx-api::a_second_pass_in_a_day_pays_only_what_the_cap_leaves` |

## CL7 (2026-10-30): correction markets, settled only by a later recheck round (ADR-0057)

What is built: `OnyxCorrections` (contracts/src), `onyx_core::recheck_of` and
`SubjectRule::Recheck`, `onyx_coordinator::corrections` (the contract's outcome rule, the recheck
pool that leaves out bettors and original observers, the recheck schedule), the `recheck` note on
`/v1/observations` answers with `client::verify_recheck`, `onyx-source recheck` (the paired
template's ids), `contracts/script/DeployCorrections.s.sol` and `scripts/corrections-anvil.sh`
(local anvil: a value, a market, a recheck that disagrees, payouts to the wei; in check-all).
Attackers: a bettor who wants the recheck to say what it bet; a recheck observer who also trades;
a coordinator that records early, late or never; an opener choosing terms; a griefer opening
markets to burn values; a loser trying to void a lost market; a server that flips the note.
Test network only (tONYX); every economic number is a placeholder (ADR-0057 open question 1).

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Status / test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CL7-1 | Forged value | High | A market is opened on a value the registry never recorded, so No wins against a lie | MITIGATED: `open` rebuilds `resultHash(spec, round, value)` from the original fact's recorded spec and result (the `OnyxObservedFacts` rule, shared Rust vectors). `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_OpenRefusesAValueTheRegistryDidNotRecord`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_ResultHashMatchesTheRustVectors` |
| CL7-2 | Oracle timing | High | The recheck is drawn or recorded while trading is open, so insiders (or anyone reading the transcript) trade on its value | MITIGATED: a market settles only from a recheck recorded by `resolveBlock` from a draw announced after `closeBlock` (the fact's latest draw: none follows a result); any other recheck makes the market void (every bet and the open fee refunded). `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_ARecheckRecordedBeforeTheCloseVoids`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_ARecheckRecordedAfterResolveBlockVoids`, `CorrectionsInvariants.t.sol::invariant_SettledOnlyFromATimelyRecheck` |
| CL7-3 | Recheck observers trading | High | A bettor sits on the recheck committee and reveals what it bet, or a recheck observer bets | PARTIAL: the deciding committee is unknown while trading is open (its draw comes after the close, on chain); the recheck pool leaves out every bettor and every original observer, which a client recomputes (`onyx_coordinator::corrections::check_recheck_pool`). `onyx-coordinator::the_recheck_pool_excludes_bettors_and_original_observers`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_ARecheckDrawnBeforeTheCloseVoidsEvenIfRecordedAfter`. TODO S9: the recheck runner (ADR-0049 worker) that draws from that pool, and `client::verify_observation` taking the market's bettor list |
| CL7-4 | Opener sets the terms | Medium | The opener picks a tolerance that decides the market | MITIGATED: `open` takes no tolerance; the market copies the pair's, set once by the owner from the reviewed template. `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_TheToleranceIsThePairsNotTheOpeners` |
| CL7-5 | Spam markets | Medium | Markets on every value, or many markets on one value | MITIGATED: an open fee per market (kept when a recheck round was drawn for it), a minimum bet and minimum windows; several markets of one value block nobody and all settle from the one recheck (review CL7-R1-1). `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_SeveralMarketsOfOneValueSettleFromOneRecheck`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_OpenTakesTheOpenFee`, `CorrectionsInvariants.t.sol::invariant_OneRecheckPerValue` |
| CL7-6 | Draw grinding | Medium | The coordinator redraws the recheck round until a committee it likes records | ACCEPTED as for every level-2 metric: the registry's subject bound (3 public draws per metric and subject, ADR-0027 amendment 6) applies to the `.recheck` metric unchanged. `OnyxRegistryDrawBound.t.sol::test_HeldDrawsOnOtherWindowsDoNotBuyAFourthTry` |
| CL7-7 | Publisher revises to win | Low | The source's publisher changes the value to win its own bet | ACCEPTED: outside Onyx's control; the market settles on what the source says at the recheck, and ADR-0057 states it. docs-only: docs/adr/0057-correction-markets.md |
| CL7-8 | Recheck reads something else | High | The recheck template reads another URL, selector or source than the original, or another metric's result settles the market | MITIGATED: `recheck_of` is a pure function that changes only metric, feed and the observable days, and `onyx-source recheck` prints its id for the registry; on chain only the pair's `.recheck` metric settles, and a pair never changes. `onyx-core::recheck_of_changes_only_metric_feed_and_window`, `onyx-core::recheck_of_refuses_what_has_no_correct_later`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_OnlyThePairedRecheckSettles` |
| CL7-9 | Stuck funds | High | Nobody resolves, or a recheck never comes, and bets stay locked | MITIGATED: anyone voids after `resolveBlock` without a timely recheck (after the grace blocks in any case); every bet is refunded and the open fee too when no recheck round was tried; the contract's balance always equals what it owes. `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_RefundsWhenNoRecheckArrivesByTheDeadline`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_AfterTheGraceAnUnresolvedMarketVoids`, `CorrectionsInvariants.t.sol::invariant_CorrectionsHoldWhatTheyOwe` |
| CL7-10 | Front-running the recheck | High | A trader sees the recheck's draw, committee or result before the close and bets on it | MITIGATED: bets stop at `closeBlock`; a market opens only while the recheck fact has no result; a recheck recorded from a draw announced at or before the close voids the market. `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_BetsCloseAtTheCloseBlock`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_OpenRefusesAValueWhoseRecheckStarted`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_ARecheckDrawnAtTheCloseBlockVoids`. Residual by design: the source is public, so whoever reads it before the close knows more; the Yes pool works as a bounty for a correction (ADR-0057 consequences) |
| CL7-11 | Manipulating the recheck | High | The coordinator records a false recheck result, or a colluding recheck committee reports a false value | PARTIAL: the recorded result is the coordinator's attestation (ADR-0042 amendment 2 item 5) and the coordinator may not bet; a client recomputes the note from the recheck's own transcript (`client::verify_recheck`); a colluding committee is THREATS L2-F2. `onyx-api::a_recheck_that_disagrees_is_a_note_never_a_fall`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_NoAdminPath`. TODO S6: a challenge window before `resolve` (as NL6-2) before anything of value is traded |
| CL7-12 | Griefing with tiny markets | Medium | A griefer opens a market that closes at once or can never be rechecked, burning the value's only correction market | MITIGATED: minimum trading and recheck blocks, a maximum market length, a minimum bet; no market blocks another of the same value, and a draw that records nothing burns nothing (review CL7-R1-1, CL7-R1-2; ADR-0057 amendment 1). `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_OpenRefusesTooShortOrTooLongMarkets`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_SeveralMarketsOfOneValueSettleFromOneRecheck`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_ADrawBeforeTheCloseThatRecordsNothingDoesNotBurnTheValue`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_BetLimits` |
| CL7-13 | Stale-value markets | Medium | A market on a value whose recheck days are already over (it can never settle), or on a value everyone knows was revised | MITIGATED: the runner schedules the recheck only in the first allowed window after the close and finds none when the days are over, so the market voids with every bet and the open fee refunded; a value known to be revised pays No by design. `onyx-coordinator::the_recheck_runs_in_the_first_allowed_window_after_the_close`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_RefundsWhenNoRecheckArrivesByTheDeadline` |
| CL7-14 | Admin outcome | High | The owner (or the coordinator, or the treasury) decides, changes or cancels a market | MITIGATED: there is no owner function but `pair` (append-only, metrics only); the owner, the coordinator and the treasury may not bet; resolve and void follow the same rules for everyone; the economics are immutable per deployment. `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_NoAdminPath`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_PairRefusesNonDatedOrUnregisteredMetrics` |
| CL7-15 | Payout rounding | Medium | Rounding pays a trader more than its share or loses money | MITIGATED: each winner gets `stake + floor(stake * distributable / winningPool)`, never above its exact share and less than one wei below it; dust goes to the treasury after the last winner; in == out + fee + dust. `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::testFuzz_PayoutsConserveAndRoundDown`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_RoundingDustGoesToTheTreasury`, `CorrectionsInvariants.t.sol::invariant_PayoutsConserve` |
| CL7-16 | Reentrancy | Medium | A hostile token or hook reenters `withdraw` to be paid twice | MITIGATED: a lock on every token-moving function, state written before the transfer. `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_WithdrawCannotBeReentered` |
| CL7-17 | Loser voids a lost market | High | After a recheck that went against it, the losing side voids the market at the deadline before anyone resolves | MITIGATED: a timely recheck cannot be voided until `graceBlocks` after `resolveBlock`, and anyone can resolve it meanwhile. `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_ATimelyRecheckIsNotVoidedDuringTheGrace` |
| CL7-18 | False note | Medium | A server flips `recheck.matches`, names another result, or a cache keeps an answer without its note | MITIGATED: the client recomputes the note from the two verified answers and refuses any difference; the ETag names the recheck's fact; an answer whose paired recheck is pending is not cached as immutable. `onyx-api::a_recheck_that_disagrees_is_a_note_never_a_fall`, `onyx-api::a_pending_recheck_keeps_the_answer_revalidating`, `onyx-api::the_etag_names_the_recheck_once_served` |
| CL7-19 | A "No" read as a fall | Low | A recheck that disagrees lowers the value's level or removes it | MITIGATED: the note is next to the value; `proofLevel` and the ladder are unchanged. `onyx-api::a_recheck_that_disagrees_is_a_note_never_a_fall`. TODO S6: the ladder's contradiction kind `Recheck` (ADR-0048 amendment 2 item 4) and the site's note next to the value |

### Review CL7-R1 (fresh adversarial reviewer, money, 2026-10-30)

A fresh reviewer read the contract, the registry calls it makes, the payout library and the
off-chain rules as a bettor, an opener, a griefer, the losing side, the coordinator, the owner and
a hostile token, and wrote proof-of-concept tests. No theft and no settlement other than from a
timely paired recheck was found; four griefing and fee findings were demonstrated (all four PoCs
passed before the fixes), each fixed with a regression test. Checked sound by the reviewer: the
value binding (`resultHash`, little-endian i128), recheck timeliness and its complement in `void`,
int128 extremes, the uint128 casts, payouts and dust, liabilities on every path, reentrancy, no
admin outcome.

| ID | Category | Severity | Threat | Status / test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CL7-R1-1 | Free squat | Medium | An opener holds the value's only live market with a close after the recheck days (the runner never draws), voids it with the fee refunded and reopens in one transaction: honest openers locked out at no cost, the value never settles | FIXED: several markets of one value may run (no `MarketExists`); a squat blocks nobody and voids with its fee refunded once the recheck is drawn before its close. `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_SeveralMarketsOfOneValueSettleFromOneRecheck` |
| CL7-R1-2 | Insider early draw | Low | The coordinator announces the recheck's draw while trading is open: the market voided, the opener's fee went to the treasury (the operator) and the value could never get a market again | FIXED: only the draw that RECORDED the recheck must come after the close (a draw that records nothing voids nothing and burns nothing); a market voided by an early recheck refunds the opener's fee. `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_ADrawBeforeTheCloseThatRecordsNothingDoesNotBurnTheValue`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_AnEarlyRecheckRefundsTheOpenFee`. Residual (ADR-0057): the coordinator can still void a market by recording early; it gains no fee from it |
| CL7-R1-3 | Risk-free cap fill | Low | Sybil addresses fill the whole pool cap on one side so nobody can take the other side; either outcome returns their stakes | FIXED: each side holds at most half the pool cap (and `maxBetPerAddress` at most half the cap). `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_OneSideCannotFillTheWholePool`, `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_ConstructorRefusesBadParams` |
| CL7-R1-4 | A late draw kills the next market | Low | A draw scheduled for an earlier, voided market lands before a new market's close: the new market voided with its fee to the treasury | FIXED with CL7-R1-2: a draw that records nothing does not void; a recheck recorded from a draw before the close refunds the fee. `OnyxCorrections.t.sol::test_AnEarlyRecheckRefundsTheOpenFee` |
| CL7-R1-5 | Two tolerances | Info | The API note's `matches` uses the template's tolerance; the contract uses the pair's, which the owner enters and nothing on chain checks, so the note can say "matches" while the market pays No | TODO S6: the client compares the `Paired` event's tolerance with the recheck template's before trusting a market (THREATS CL7-4 sets the pair by review only) |
| CL7-R1-6 | Exclusion by address only | Info | The owner, the coordinator and the treasury can bet from other addresses; a recheck observer can bet through another address | ACCEPTED: insider rules and the recheck pool exclusion are per address, as for `OnyxFutures` (THREATS NL6-12); bonds that make it costly wait for the partners' economics (H3) |
| CL7-R1-7 | Withheld preimage | Info | The coordinator records a timely recheck but withholds its round id, so nobody can resolve; the market voids after the grace with the fee to the treasury | ACCEPTED: covered by "the coordinator can void a market" (ADR-0057 consequences); the round id is in the public transcript the API serves, so withholding it is visible |

## Issuer rosters, label set v3 (ROADMAP P2a, 2026-10-18, ADR-0037 Amendment 1)

Label set v3 of `test.onyx.entities.btc`: 11 issuers' own dated rosters (206 snapshots,
`fixtures/rosters/`), memberships by the 8,928-block listing rule, signatures verified in Onyx,
per-entity flows over the live fixture blocks (`history/rosters-week.json`). Moves considered: a
cheating issuer or file, a lazy builder trusting the indexer's grades, a data thief or privacy
leak through roster rows, stale rosters counted forever, a back-dated history, a rights leak.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ROS-1 | Privacy | High | A roster row could name an individual: a sanctioned person's address in an exchange file, customer deposit custody, page text with staff or auditor names | FIXED: labels name only the 11 registered companies; the government-filing deny list drops any roster address a filing names (1 OKX address, OFAC); BitMEX's custodial section and Binance's third-party-custodian rows are never read; raw pages and PDFs are not committed, only their address extracts. `labels_v3::v3_drops_the_address_a_government_filing_names`, `labels_v3::v3_names_only_reviewed_issuers_from_their_own_hosts_never_wbtc_or_cbbtc`, `roster::tests::a_denied_address_is_dropped_and_denial_wins` |
| ROS-2 | Lazy builder | High | A row graded "signed" on the indexer's word, or a published redeem script that does not hash to its address kept | FIXED: Onyx verifies every published signature itself (port of the indexer's rule: script binds to the address, enough distinct recovered keys) and drops a row whose script does not bind; a failed signature leaves the row published. `signed_roster::tests::signed_roster_okx_p2sh_2_of_3_verifies`, `signed_roster::tests::signed_roster_multisig_threshold_shortfall_fails`, `signed_roster::tests::signed_roster_script_not_hashing_to_address_fails`, `labels_v3::v3_grades_signed_only_for_the_issuers_that_sign` |
| ROS-3 | Cheating source / builder | Medium | Snapshot heights for MEXC, Bybit, Bitfinex 2022 and Crypto.com come from the indexer's header-timestamp mapping, and Deribit, Bitfinex (current) and BITB from a tip observed at the fetch; Onyx has not checked them against headers, so a wrong height moves a window | TODO D12: the header tool checks every `indexer-mapped` height (block time at or after the snapshot time, the block before it earlier) once it can read old headers; the block times are kept in each `snapshots.json` for that check |
| ROS-4 | Reader | Medium | A one-off or stale roster counted for years (ADR-0037 item 1 closed a range only when a later publication dropped the address) | FIXED: a listing supports 8,928 blocks; gaps and stale lists close at expiry. `roster::tests::a_stale_last_listing_closes_at_expiry_with_both_edges`, `roster::tests::a_gap_longer_than_max_age_splits_the_range_at_expiry`, `roster::tests::monthly_publications_survive_one_missed_month` |
| ROS-5 | Cheating builder | Medium | A committed snapshot file edited, or an extract that does not follow from the raw bytes | FIXED for the committed bytes: every file's sha256 is in its `snapshots.json`, which `SHA256SUMS` pins, and the listings refuse a mismatch; the set rebuilds byte for byte. `labels_v3::v3_rebuilds_byte_for_byte_from_the_committed_rosters`. Residual: extracts (OKX rows, PDF and page addresses) follow from raw files not in git; TODO D23: re-fetch each raw snapshot (`build-rosters.py fetch`) and re-extract on a schedule |
| ROS-6 | Reader | Medium | Balances shown for entities whose addresses no scan holds (a base of zero would read as a real balance) | FIXED: `export-rosters` gives a balance only for an entity all of whose in-range addresses the committed scan holds (Binance, BITB), cross-checked against the v2 reserve chain where the address sets agree; others show none with the reason. TODO D23: a scan of every v3 address and the reserve chain over v3 windows |
| ROS-7 | Operator | High | Rights: seven new issuers' terms are unread, and wBTC's forbid redistribution | OPEN (Needs the project owner, L8-5): v3 is test data, shown in the private preview only; a fallback public build refuses `history/rosters-week.json` by path (`public_build::a_fallback_build_carries_no_label_derived_totals`); wBTC and cbBTC are refused by the builder (`labels_bridge::the_v3_fixture_is_only_the_dated_roster_set_from_recorded_sources`); the release step fails until S17-S23's terms are read (`scripts/check-source-terms.py`) |
| ROS-8 | Cheating issuer | Medium | Two issuers list one address at the same time (a shared custodian, a copy error, a griefing listing) | FIXED: the address is dropped for both. `roster::tests::two_entities_at_once_drop_the_address_but_a_move_is_kept` |
| ROS-9 | Cheating publisher | Medium | A forged undated prefix restarts a dated history so a later version can rewrite served heights | FIXED: undated versions only as a prefix numbered from 1, same name, each with other labels; the gate loads them from checksummed fixtures. `dated::tests::a_dated_history_may_start_after_undated_versions`, `labels_v3::v3_is_the_first_dated_version_after_the_undated_v1_and_v2` |
| ROS-10 | Builder | Low | PDF text splits long addresses over lines and uses ligatures ("ﬂ"), so an extract could miss or mis-join an address | FIXED: NFKC, then a failing candidate is joined only when the join passes the checksum; every Bybit list equals the indexer's independent extraction at import. `labels_v3::the_roster_builder_self_test_passes_and_every_file_is_checksummed` |
| ROS-11 | Reader | Low | Snapshots before 2026 of OKX, BitMEX and MEXC are not in v3 (size), and no later version of this name may add them (no back-dating) | ACCEPTED for a test fixture: the hashes are recorded in `snapshots.json`; a production set keeps the full history outside git. TODO D24 |

### Review P2a-R1 (fresh adversarial reviewer, 2026-10-18)

The reviewer re-derived all 18,444 memberships in Python from the listings (0 mismatches) and
attacked the verifier, the loader, the proof level and the committed bytes.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P2a-R1-1 | Cheating issuer | High | The verifier port accepted a key-hash address (1..., bc1q...) listed with any public key as its "script" and a signature by that key: the script was never hashed against the address (the indexer's Python has the same gap) | FIXED: a key-hash address's script must be one key whose hash160 is the address's. `signed_roster::tests::signed_roster_a_key_hash_address_with_someone_elses_key_fails` (no committed row used that path) |
| P2a-R1-2 | Cheating issuer | Medium | Any signed message counted, so a copied third-party proof would grade a row signed; HTX signs some rows "King will be back!" | FIXED: signed only when the message names the issuer (OKX, CoinEx; HTX as "huobi" or "HTX"); 88 HTX rows over another message are published. `rosters::tests::a_signature_counts_only_over_a_message_naming_the_issuer`. A signature shows the key signed at some time; the snapshot dates the listing (documented in ADR-0037 Amendment 1 item 3) |
| P2a-R1-3 | Reader | Medium | v3 is published at 971,207 while the newest snapshot is at 963,899: 3,690 memberships close by expiry in that gap, and no later version may reopen them | ACCEPTED: the expiry is the rule's answer for listings Onyx holds, and the fixture blocks (to 971,199) can only run windows of a set published after them. Snapshots of 2026-08-21 to 2026-10-13 can enter only a later set name; TODO D23 fetches them before the next published set |
| P2a-R1-4 | Data thief / privacy | Medium | Committed raw CoinEx workbooks carried a person's first name and an editor id in their metadata; BitMEX YAMLs carried the custodial section (11 customer deposit addresses) | FIXED: CoinEx is committed as its worksheet cells (CSV) and BitMEX as its height and address section; both keep the raw hashes. `labels_v3::v3_rebuilds_byte_for_byte_from_the_committed_rosters` |
| P2a-R1-5 | Lazy validator | Medium | The window proof level ignored the shard's heights (any v3 stretch got level 4 on any range, the empty window too), and was wired into `label_set_proof_level` | FIXED: `dated_window_proof_level(set, from, to)` requires `set == v3.window(from, to)` with at least one label; `label_set_proof_level` is unchanged (a v3 window is level 5 there). `labels_v3::v3_windows_are_level_4_anything_else_level_5` |
| P2a-R1-6 | Cheating builder | Low | The loader let a member stretch `to` past its last cited listing's expiry (or open it), cite a record past the publication, or carry no evidence in a file with a table; the table's order and record shapes were unchecked | FIXED: each range must be supported by its cited listings (closed by expiry, open only when alive at the publication), every record is shape-checked, the table sorted and unique, evidence required with a table. `labels_v3::a_forged_v3_file_is_refused_by_the_loader` |
| P2a-R1-7 | Cheating publisher | Low | A dated file published at `u64::MAX` with every member from 0 would read as an undated version in `check_history` and skip the back-dating rule | FIXED: a dated file may not use that height. `labels_v3::a_forged_v3_file_is_refused_by_the_loader` |
| P2a-R1-8 | Builder | Low | A signed row whose script does not bind was kept as published while an unsigned one was dropped | FIXED: a non-binding script drops the row either way (ADR-0037 Amendment 1 item 3); 0 rows affected. `rosters::tests::a_non_binding_script_drops_the_row_signed_or_not` |
| P2a-R1-9 | Operator | Info | `history/rosters-week.json` must exist for the fallback guard; the old bridge script shares the name `build-label-set-v3`; `scripts/audit-privacy-scan.py` reads v1 and v2 only | FIXED (export committed) for the first; the second is documented in both files' headers; TODO D23: the privacy scan reads v3 and `fixtures/rosters` |

### Review P2a-R2 (fresh adversarial reviewer, 2026-10-19)

The reviewer re-imported OKX, BitMEX, Binance, HTX, CoinEx and Deribit from the indexer's raw
files (`build-rosters.py import ... --out`: every committed file and manifest identical), checked
the raw sha256 and extracts of the other five, traced 33 rows (3 per issuer) to their snapshot,
URL, hash and fetch date with their window edges, rebuilt v3 byte for byte, recounted Deribit's
flows on 2026-10-13 and Binance's on 2026-10-12 (its memberships end at 971,006) by hand from the
fixture blocks (equal to `rosters-week.json`), and found no v3 address in the indexer's wBTC or
cbBTC rows.

| ID | Attacker | Severity | Finding | Status |
